metric.description: Character n-gram cosine distance. This is a reproducible lexical baseline, not a semantic or faithfulness score.

units.leftText: These are the names of the sons of Israel who went to Egypt with Jacob, each with his family:
units.rightText: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt (every man and his household came with Jacob):

units.leftText: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah;
units.rightText: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah,

units.leftText: Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin;
units.rightText: Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin,

units.leftText: Dan and Naphtali; Gad and Asher.
units.rightText: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.

units.leftText: The descendants of Jacob numbered seventy in all, including Joseph, who was already in Egypt.
units.rightText: And all the souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were seventy souls: and Joseph was in Egypt already.
leftNotes: 1:5 MT (see also Genesis 46:27|GEN 46:27*); DSS and LXX (see also Acts 7:14) seventy-five

units.leftText: Now Joseph and all his brothers and all that generation died,
units.rightText: And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.

units.leftText: but the Israelites were fruitful and increased rapidly; they multiplied and became exceedingly numerous, so that the land was filled with them. Oppression by a New King (Acts 7:15–19|ACT 7:15-19*)
units.rightText: And the children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them.

units.leftText: Then a new king, who did not know Joseph, came to power in Egypt.
units.rightText: Now there arose a new king over Egypt, who knew not Joseph.

units.leftText: “Look,” he said to his people, “the Israelites have become too numerous and too powerful for us.
units.rightText: And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we:

units.leftText: Come, let us deal shrewdly with them, or they will increase even more; and if a war breaks out, they may join our enemies, fight against us, and leave the country. ”
units.rightText: come, let us deal wisely with them, lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they also join themselves unto our enemies, and fight against us, and get them up out of the land.
leftNotes: 1:10 Or and take the country

units.leftText: So the Egyptians appointed taskmasters over the Israelites to oppress them with forced labor. As a result, they built Pithom and Rameses as store cities for Pharaoh.
units.rightText: Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh store-cities, Pithom and Raamses.

units.leftText: But the more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied and flourished; so the Egyptians came to dread the Israelites.
units.rightText: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and the more they spread abroad. And they were grieved because of the children of Israel.

units.leftText: They worked the Israelites ruthlessly
units.rightText: And the Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigor:

units.leftText: and made their lives bitter with hard labor in brick and mortar, and with all kinds of work in the fields. Every service they imposed was harsh.
units.rightText: and they made their lives bitter with hard service, in mortar and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field, all their service, wherein they made them serve with rigor.

units.leftText: Then the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, whose names were Shiphrah and Puah,
units.rightText: And the king of Egypt spake to the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah:

units.leftText: “When you help the Hebrew women give birth, observe them on the birthstools. If the child is a son, kill him; but if it is a daughter, let her live.”
units.rightText: and he said, When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them upon the birth-stool; if it be a son, then ye shall kill him; but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.

units.leftText: The midwives, however, feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt had instructed; they let the boys live.
units.rightText: But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men-children alive.

units.leftText: So the king of Egypt summoned the midwives and asked them, “Why have you done this? Why have you let the boys live?”
units.rightText: And the king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said unto them, Why have ye done this thing, and have saved the men-children alive?

units.leftText: The midwives answered Pharaoh, “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women, for they are vigorous and give birth before a midwife arrives.”
units.rightText: And the midwives said unto Pharaoh, Because the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women; for they are lively, and are delivered ere the midwife come unto them.

units.leftText: So God was good to the midwives, and the people multiplied and became even more numerous.
units.rightText: And God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty.

units.leftText: And because the midwives feared God, He gave them families of their own.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made them households.

units.leftText: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people: “Every son born to the Hebrews you must throw into the Nile, but every daughter you may allow to live.”
units.rightText: And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive.
leftNotes: 1:22 SP, LXX, and Targum Yonaton; Hebrew does not include to the Hebrews.

units.leftText: Now a man of the house of Levi married a Levite woman,
units.rightText: And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.

units.leftText: and she conceived and gave birth to a son. When she saw that he was a beautiful child, she hid him for three months.
units.rightText: And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.

units.leftText: But when she could no longer hide him, she got him a papyrus basket and coated it with tar and pitch. Then she placed the child in the basket and set it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.
units.rightText: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch; and she put the child therein, and laid it in the flags by the river’s brink.
leftNotes: 2:3 The Hebrew can also mean ark; also in verse 5; see Genesis 6:14|GEN 6:14*.

units.leftText: And his sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.
units.rightText: And his sister stood afar off, to know what would be done to him.

units.leftText: Soon the daughter of Pharaoh went down to bathe in the Nile, and her attendants were walking along the riverbank. And when she saw the basket among the reeds, she sent her maidservant to retrieve it.
units.rightText: And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to bathe at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river-side; and she saw the ark among the flags, and sent her handmaid to fetch it.

units.leftText: When she opened it, she saw the child, and behold, the little boy was crying. So she had compassion on him and said, “This is one of the Hebrew children.”
units.rightText: And she opened it, and saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews’ children.

units.leftText: Then his sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Shall I go and call one of the Hebrew women to nurse the child for you?”
units.rightText: Then said his sister to Pharaoh’s daughter, Shall I go and call thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee?

units.leftText: “Go ahead,” Pharaoh’s daughter told her. And the girl went and called the boy’s mother.
units.rightText: And Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, Go. And the maiden went and called the child’s mother.

units.leftText: Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Take this child and nurse him for me, and I will pay your wages.” So the woman took the boy and nursed him.
units.rightText: And Pharaoh’s daughter said unto her, Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will give thee thy wages. And the woman took the child, and nursed it.

units.leftText: When the child had grown older, she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses and explained, “I drew him out of the water.” The Rejection and Flight of Moses (Acts 7:23–29|ACT 7:23-29*)
units.rightText: And the child grew, and she brought him unto Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses, and said, Because I drew him out of the water.
leftNotes: 2:10 Moses sounds like a Hebrew term that means to lift out.

units.leftText: One day, after Moses had grown up, he went out to his own people and observed their hard labor. He saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his own people.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown up, that he went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens: and he saw an Egyptian smiting a Hebrew, one of his brethren.
leftNotes: 2:11 Or his brothers

units.leftText: After looking this way and that and seeing no one, he struck down the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
units.rightText: And he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he smote the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.

units.leftText: The next day Moses went out and saw two Hebrews fighting. He asked the one in the wrong, “Why are you attacking your companion?”
units.rightText: And he went out the second day, and, behold, two men of the Hebrews were striving together: and he said to him that did the wrong, Wherefore smitest thou thy fellow?

units.leftText: But the man replied, “Who made you ruler and judge over us? Are you planning to kill me as you killed the Egyptian? ” Then Moses was afraid and thought, “This thing I have done has surely become known.”
units.rightText: And he said, Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? thinkest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian? And Moses feared, and said, Surely the thing is known.
leftNotes: 2:14 Cited in Acts 7:27|ACT 7:27* and Acts 7:35
2:14 LXX Are you planning to kill me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?Cited in Acts 7:28|ACT 7:28*

units.leftText: When Pharaoh heard about this matter, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian, where he sat down beside a well.
units.rightText: Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.

units.leftText: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they came to draw water and fill the troughs to water their father’s flock.
units.rightText: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father’s flock.

units.leftText: And when some shepherds came along and drove them away, Moses rose up to help them and watered their flock.
units.rightText: And the shepherds came and drove them away; but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.

units.leftText: When the daughters returned to their father Reuel, he asked them, “Why have you returned so early today?”
units.rightText: And when they came to Reuel their father, he said, How is it that ye are come so soon to-day?
leftNotes: 2:18 Reuel was also called Jethro; see Exodus 3:1|EXO 3:1*.

units.leftText: “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds,” they replied. “He even drew water for us and watered the flock.”
units.rightText: And they said, An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and moreover he drew water for us, and watered the flock.

units.leftText: “So where is he?” their father asked. “Why did you leave the man behind? Invite him to have something to eat.”
units.rightText: And he said unto his daughters, And where is he? why is it that ye have left the man? call him, that he may eat bread.

units.leftText: Moses agreed to stay with the man, and he gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses in marriage.
units.rightText: And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.

units.leftText: And she gave birth to a son, and Moses named him Gershom, saying, “I have become a foreigner in a foreign land.” God Hears the Cry of the Israelites
units.rightText: And she bare a son, and he called his name Gershom; for he said, I have been a sojourner in a foreign land.
leftNotes: 2:22 Gershom sounds like the Hebrew for foreigner.

units.leftText: After a long time, the king of Egypt died. The Israelites groaned and cried out under their burden of slavery, and their cry for deliverance from bondage ascended to God.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the course of those many days, that the king of Egypt died: and the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up unto God by reason of the bondage.

units.leftText: So God heard their groaning, and He remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
units.rightText: And God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.

units.leftText: God saw the Israelites and took notice.
units.rightText: And God saw the children of Israel, and God took knowledge of them.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, Moses was shepherding the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian. He led the flock to the far side of the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.
units.rightText: Now Moses was keeping the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian: and he led the flock to the back of the wilderness, and came to the mountain of God, unto Horeb.
leftNotes: 3:1 Moses’ father-in-law Jethro was also called Reuel; see Exodus 2:18|EXO 2:18*.
3:1 That is, Mount Sinai, or possibly a mountain in the range containing Mount Sinai

units.leftText: There the angel of the LORD appeared to him in a blazing fire from within a bush. Moses saw the bush ablaze with fire, but it was not consumed.
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
leftNotes: 3:2 Or Angel

units.leftText: So Moses thought, “I must go over and see this marvelous sight. Why is the bush not burning up?”
units.rightText: And Moses said, I will turn aside now, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt.

units.leftText: When the LORD saw that he had gone over to look, God called out to him from within the bush, “Moses, Moses!” “Here I am,” he answered.
units.rightText: And when Jehovah saw that he turned aside to see, God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses. And he said, Here am I.

units.leftText: “Do not come any closer,” God said. “Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.”
units.rightText: And he said, Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.
leftNotes: 3:5 Cited in Acts 7:33|ACT 7:33*

units.leftText: Then He said, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” At this, Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God.
units.rightText: Moreover he said, I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. And Moses hid his face; for he was afraid to look upon God.
leftNotes: 3:6 Cited in Matthew 22:32|MAT 22:32*, Mark 12:26, Luke 20:37, and Acts 7:32

units.leftText: The LORD said, “I have indeed seen the affliction of My people in Egypt. I have heard them crying out because of their oppressors, and I am aware of their sufferings.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said, I have surely seen the affliction of my people that are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows;

units.leftText: I have come down to rescue them from the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them up out of that land to a good and spacious land, a land flowing with milk and honey— the home of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
units.rightText: and I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land unto a good land and a large, unto a land flowing with milk and honey; unto the place of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite.

units.leftText: And now the cry of the Israelites has reached Me, and I have seen how severely the Egyptians are oppressing them.
units.rightText: And now, behold, the cry of the children of Israel is come unto me: moreover I have seen the oppression wherewith the Egyptians oppress them.

units.leftText: Therefore, go! I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring My people the Israelites out of Egypt.”
units.rightText: Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt.
leftNotes: 3:10 Cited in Acts 7:34|ACT 7:34*

units.leftText: But Moses asked God, “Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh and bring the Israelites out of Egypt?”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto God, Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt?

units.leftText: “I will surely be with you,” God said, “and this will be the sign to you that I have sent you: When you have brought the people out of Egypt, all of you will worship God on this mountain.”
units.rightText: And he said, Certainly I will be with thee; and this shall be the token unto thee, that I have sent thee: when thou hast brought forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this mountain.
leftNotes: 3:12 Cited in Acts 7:7|ACT 7:7*

units.leftText: Then Moses asked God, “Suppose I go to the Israelites and say to them, ‘The God of your fathers has sent me to you,’ and they ask me, ‘What is His name?’ What should I tell them?”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto God, Behold, when I come unto the children of Israel, and shall say unto them, The God of your fathers hath sent me unto you; and they shall say to me, What is his name? What shall I say unto them?

units.leftText: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM. This is what you are to say to the Israelites: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”
units.rightText: And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.
leftNotes: 3:14 Or I WILL BE WHAT I WILL BE

units.leftText: God also told Moses, “Say to the Israelites, ‘The LORD, the God of your fathers — the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob — has sent me to you.’ This is My name forever, and this is how I am to be remembered in every generation.
units.rightText: And God said moreover unto Moses, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, Jehovah, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath sent me unto you: this is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations.

units.leftText: Go, assemble the elders of Israel and say to them, ‘The LORD, the God of your fathers — the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — has appeared to me and said: I have surely attended to you and have seen what has been done to you in Egypt.
units.rightText: Go, and gather the elders of Israel together, and say unto them, Jehovah, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, hath appeared unto me, saying, I have surely visited you, and seen that which is done to you in Egypt:

units.leftText: And I have promised to bring you up out of your affliction in Egypt, into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites— a land flowing with milk and honey.’
units.rightText: and I have said, I will bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt unto the land of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite, unto a land flowing with milk and honey.

units.leftText: The elders of Israel will listen to what you say, and you must go with them to the king of Egypt and tell him, ‘The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us. Now please let us take a three-day journey into the wilderness, so that we may sacrifice to the LORD our God.’
units.rightText: And they shall hearken to thy voice: and thou shalt come, thou and the elders of Israel, unto the king of Egypt, and ye shall say unto him, Jehovah, the God of the Hebrews, hath met with us: and now let us go, we pray thee, three days’ journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to Jehovah our God.

units.leftText: But I know that the king of Egypt will not allow you to go unless a mighty hand compels him.
units.rightText: And I know that the king of Egypt will not give you leave to go, no, not by a mighty hand.
leftNotes: 3:19 Literally except by a mighty hand

units.leftText: So I will stretch out My hand and strike the Egyptians with all the wonders I will perform among them. And after that, he will release you.
units.rightText: And I will put forth my hand, and smite Egypt with all my wonders which I will do in the midst thereof: and after that he will let you go.

units.leftText: And I will grant this people such favor in the sight of the Egyptians that when you leave, you will not go away empty-handed.
units.rightText: And I will give this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians: and it shall come to pass, that, when ye go, ye shall not go empty.

units.leftText: Every woman shall ask her neighbor and any woman staying in her house for silver and gold jewelry and clothing, and you will put them on your sons and daughters. So you will plunder the Egyptians.”
units.rightText: But every woman shall ask of her neighbor, and of her that sojourneth in her house, jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment: and ye shall put them upon your sons, and upon your daughters; and ye shall despoil the Egyptians.

units.leftText: Then Moses answered, “What if they do not believe me or listen to my voice? For they may say, ‘The LORD has not appeared to you.’”
units.rightText: And Moses answered and said, But, behold, they will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice; for they will say, Jehovah hath not appeared unto thee.

units.leftText: And the LORD asked him, “What is that in your hand?” “A staff,” he replied.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto him, What is that in thy hand? And he said, A rod.

units.leftText: “Throw it on the ground,” said the LORD. So Moses threw it on the ground, and it became a snake, and he ran from it.
units.rightText: And he said, Cast it on the ground. And he cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moses fled from before it.
leftNotes: 4:3 Hebrew nachash, in contrast to Aaron’s staff, which became a tanninin Exodus 7:10|EXO 7:10*

units.leftText: “Stretch out your hand and grab it by the tail,” the LORD said to Moses, who reached out his hand and caught the snake, and it turned back into a staff in his hand.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Put forth thy hand, and take it by the tail: (and he put forth his hand, and laid hold of it, and it became a rod in his hand);

units.leftText: “This is so that they may believe that the LORD, the God of their fathers — the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob — has appeared to you.” Moses’ Hand
units.rightText: that they may believe that Jehovah, the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath appeared unto thee.

units.leftText: Furthermore, the LORD said to Moses, “Put your hand inside your cloak. ” So he put his hand inside his cloak, and when he took it out, his hand was leprous, white as snow.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said furthermore unto him, Put now thy hand into thy bosom. And he put his hand into his bosom: and when he took it out, behold, his hand was leprous, as white as snow.
leftNotes: 4:6 Hebrew into your bosom; twice in this verse and twice in verse 7
4:6 The Hebrew word traditionally translated as leprous was used for various skin diseases; see Leviticus 13.

units.leftText: “Put your hand back inside your cloak,” said the LORD. So Moses put his hand back inside his cloak, and when he took it out, it was restored, like the rest of his skin.
units.rightText: And he said, Put thy hand into thy bosom again. (And he put his hand into his bosom again; and when he took it out of his bosom, behold, it was turned again as his other flesh.)

units.leftText: And the LORD said, “If they refuse to believe you or heed the witness of the first sign, they may believe that of the second.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, if they will not believe thee, neither hearken to the voice of the first sign, that they will believe the voice of the latter sign.

units.leftText: But if they do not believe even these two signs or listen to your voice, take some water from the Nile and pour it on the dry ground. Then the water you take from the Nile will become blood on the ground.” The Appointment of Aaron
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, if they will not believe even these two signs, neither hearken unto thy voice, that thou shalt take of the water of the river, and pour it upon the dry land: and the water which thou takest out of the river shall become blood upon the dry land.

units.leftText: “Please, Lord,” Moses replied, “I have never been eloquent, neither in the past nor since You have spoken to Your servant, for I am slow of speech and tongue.”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Jehovah, Oh, Lord, I am not eloquent, neither heretofore, nor since thou hast spoken unto thy servant; for I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to him, “Who gave man his mouth? Or who makes the mute or the deaf, the sighted or the blind? Is it not I, the LORD?
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto him, Who hath made man’s mouth? or who maketh a man dumb, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? is it not I, Jehovah?

units.leftText: Now go! I will help you as you speak, and I will teach you what to say.”
units.rightText: Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt speak.

units.leftText: But Moses replied, “Please, Lord, send someone else.”
units.rightText: And he said, Oh, Lord, send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send.

units.leftText: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Moses, and He said, “Is not Aaron the Levite your brother? I know that he can speak well, and he is now on his way to meet you. When he sees you, he will be glad in his heart.
units.rightText: And the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Moses, and he said, Is there not Aaron thy brother the Levite? I know that he can speak well. And also, behold, he cometh forth to meet thee: and when he seeth thee, he will be glad in his heart.

units.leftText: You are to speak to him and put the words in his mouth. I will help both of you to speak, and I will teach you what to do.
units.rightText: And thou shalt speak unto him, and put the words in his mouth: and I will be with thy mouth, and with his mouth, and will teach you what ye shall do.

units.leftText: He will speak to the people for you. He will be your spokesman, and it will be as if you were God to him.
units.rightText: And he shall be thy spokesman unto the people; and it shall come to pass, that he shall be to thee a mouth, and thou shalt be to him as God.

units.leftText: But take this staff in your hand so you can perform signs with it.” Moses Leaves for Egypt
units.rightText: And thou shalt take in thy hand this rod, wherewith thou shalt do the signs.

units.leftText: Then Moses went back to his father-in-law Jethro and said to him, “Please let me return to my brothers in Egypt to see if they are still alive.” “Go in peace,” Jethro replied.
units.rightText: And Moses went and returned to Jethro his father-in-law, and said unto him, Let me go, I pray thee, and return unto my brethren that are in Egypt, and see whether they be yet alive. And Jethro said to Moses, Go in peace.
leftNotes: 4:18 Moses’ father-in-law Jethro was also called Reuel; see Exodus 2:18|EXO 2:18*.

units.leftText: Now the LORD had said to Moses in Midian, “Go back to Egypt, for all the men who sought to kill you are dead.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses in Midian, Go, return into Egypt; for all the men are dead that sought thy life.

units.leftText: So Moses took his wife and sons, put them on a donkey, and headed back to Egypt. And he took the staff of God in his hand.
units.rightText: And Moses took his wife and his sons, and set them upon an ass, and he returned to the land of Egypt: and Moses took the rod of God in his hand.

units.leftText: The LORD instructed Moses, “When you go back to Egypt, see that you perform before Pharaoh all the wonders that I have put within your power. But I will harden his heart so that he will not let the people go.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, When thou goest back into Egypt, see that thou do before Pharaoh all the wonders which I have put in thy hand: but I will harden his heart and he will not let the people go.
leftNotes: 4:21 Or stiffen or strengthen

units.leftText: Then tell Pharaoh that this is what the LORD says: ‘Israel is My firstborn son,
units.rightText: And thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith Jehovah, Israel is my son, my first-born:

units.leftText: and I told you to let My son go so that he may worship Me. But since you have refused to let him go, behold, I will kill your firstborn son!’”
units.rightText: and I have said unto thee, Let my son go, that he may serve me; and thou hast refused to let him go: behold, I will slay thy son, thy first-born.

units.leftText: Now at a lodging place along the way, the LORD met Moses and was about to kill him.
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the way at the lodging-place, that Jehovah met him, and sought to kill him.
leftNotes: 4:24 Hebrew him

units.leftText: But Zipporah took a flint knife, cut off her son’s foreskin, and touched it to Moses’ feet. “Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me,” she said.
units.rightText: Then Zipporah took a flint, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet; and she said, Surely a bridegroom of blood art thou to me.
leftNotes: 4:25 Hebrew his feet

units.leftText: So the LORD let him alone. (When she said, “bridegroom of blood,” she was referring to the circumcision.) The People Believe Moses and Aaron
units.rightText: So he let him alone. Then she said, A bridegroom of blood art thou, because of the circumcision.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, the LORD had said to Aaron, “Go and meet Moses in the wilderness.” So he went and met Moses at the mountain of God and kissed him.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said to Aaron, Go into the wilderness to meet Moses. And he went, and met him in the mountain of God, and kissed him.

units.leftText: And Moses told Aaron everything the LORD had sent him to say, and all the signs He had commanded him to perform.
units.rightText: And Moses told Aaron all the words of Jehovah wherewith he had sent him, and all the signs wherewith he had charged him.

units.leftText: Then Moses and Aaron went and assembled all the elders of the Israelites,
units.rightText: And Moses and Aaron went and gathered together all the elders of the children of Israel:

units.leftText: and Aaron relayed everything the LORD had said to Moses.
units.rightText: and Aaron spake all the words which Jehovah had spoken unto Moses, and did the signs in the sight of the people.

units.leftText: and they believed. And when they heard that the LORD had attended to the Israelites and had seen their affliction, they bowed down and worshiped.
units.rightText: And the people believed: and when they heard that Jehovah had visited the children of Israel, and that he had seen their affliction, then they bowed their heads and worshipped.

units.leftText: After that, Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Let My people go, so that they may hold a feast to Me in the wilderness.’”
units.rightText: And afterward Moses and Aaron came, and said unto Pharaoh, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness.

units.leftText: But Pharaoh replied, “Who is the LORD that I should obey His voice and let Israel go? I do not know the LORD, and I will not let Israel go.”
units.rightText: And Pharaoh said, Who is Jehovah, that I should hearken unto his voice to let Israel go? I know not Jehovah, and moreover I will not let Israel go.

units.leftText: “The God of the Hebrews has met with us,” they answered. “Please let us go on a three-day journey into the wilderness to sacrifice to the LORD our God, or He may strike us with plagues or with the sword.”
units.rightText: And they said, The God of the Hebrews hath met with us: let us go, we pray thee, three days’ journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice unto Jehovah our God, lest he fall upon us with pestilence, or with the sword.

units.leftText: But the king of Egypt said to them, “Moses and Aaron, why do you draw the people away from their work? Get back to your labor!”
units.rightText: And the king of Egypt said unto them, Wherefore do ye, Moses and Aaron, loose the people from their works? get you unto your burdens.

units.leftText: Pharaoh also said, “Look, the people of the land are now numerous, and you would be stopping them from their labor.” Bricks and Straw
units.rightText: And Pharaoh said, Behold, the people of the land are now many, and ye make them rest from their burdens.

units.leftText: That same day Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters of the people and their foremen:
units.rightText: And the same day Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters of the people, and their officers, saying,

units.leftText: “You shall no longer supply the people with straw for making bricks. They must go and gather their own straw.
units.rightText: Ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick, as heretofore: let them go and gather straw for themselves.

units.leftText: But require of them the same quota of bricks as before; do not reduce it. For they are lazy; that is why they are crying out, ‘Let us go and sacrifice to our God.’
units.rightText: And the number of the bricks, which they did make heretofore, ye shall lay upon them; ye shall not diminish aught thereof: for they are idle; therefore they cry, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our God.

units.leftText: Make the work harder on the men so they will be occupied and pay no attention to these lies.”
units.rightText: Let heavier work be laid upon the men, that they may labor therein; and let them not regard lying words.

units.leftText: So the taskmasters and foremen of the people went out and said to them, “This is what Pharaoh says: ‘I am no longer giving you straw.
units.rightText: And the taskmasters of the people went out, and their officers, and they spake to the people, saying, Thus saith Pharaoh, I will not give you straw.

units.leftText: Go and get your own straw wherever you can find it; but your workload will in no way be reduced.’”
units.rightText: Go yourselves, get you straw where ye can find it: for nought of your work shall be diminished.

units.leftText: So the people scattered all over the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
units.rightText: So the people were scattered abroad throughout all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.

units.leftText: The taskmasters kept pressing them, saying, “Fulfill your quota each day, just as you did when straw was provided.”
units.rightText: And the taskmasters were urgent saying, Fulfil your works, your daily tasks, as when there was straw.

units.leftText: Then the Israelite foremen, whom Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over the people, were beaten and asked, “Why have you not fulfilled your quota of bricks yesterday or today, as you did before?” The Cry of the Israelites
units.rightText: And the officers of the children of Israel, whom Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over them, were beaten, and demanded, Wherefore have ye not fulfilled your task both yesterday and to-day, in making brick as heretofore?

units.leftText: So the Israelite foremen went and appealed to Pharaoh: “Why are you treating your servants this way?
units.rightText: Then the officers of the children of Israel came and cried unto Pharaoh, saying, Wherefore dealest thou thus with thy servants?

units.leftText: No straw has been given to your servants, yet we are told, ‘Make bricks!’ Look, your servants are being beaten, but the fault is with your own people.”
units.rightText: There is no straw given unto thy servants, and they say to us, Make brick: and, behold, thy servants are beaten; but the fault is in thine own people.

units.leftText: “You are slackers!” Pharaoh replied. “Slackers! That is why you keep saying, ‘Let us go and sacrifice to the LORD.’
units.rightText: But he said, Ye are idle, ye are idle: therefore ye say, Let us go and sacrifice to Jehovah.

units.leftText: Now get to work. You will be given no straw, yet you must deliver the full quota of bricks.”
units.rightText: Go therefore now, and work; for there shall no straw be given you, yet shall ye deliver the number of bricks.

units.leftText: The Israelite foremen realized they were in trouble when they were told, “You must not reduce your daily quota of bricks.”
units.rightText: And the officers of the children of Israel did see that they were in evil case, when it was said, Ye shall not diminish aught from your bricks, your daily tasks.

units.leftText: When they left Pharaoh, they confronted Moses and Aaron, who stood waiting to meet them.
units.rightText: And they met Moses and Aaron, who stood in the way, as they came forth from Pharaoh:

units.leftText: “May the LORD look upon you and judge you,” the foremen said, “for you have made us a stench before Pharaoh and his officials; you have placed in their hand a sword to kill us!”
units.rightText: and they said unto them, Jehovah look upon you, and judge: because ye have made our savor to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to slay us.

units.leftText: So Moses returned to the LORD and asked, “Lord, why have You brought trouble upon this people? Is this why You sent me?
units.rightText: And Moses returned unto Jehovah, and said, Lord, wherefore hast thou dealt ill with this people? why is it that thou hast sent me?

units.leftText: Ever since I went to Pharaoh to speak in Your name, he has brought trouble on this people, and You have not delivered Your people in any way.”
units.rightText: For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in thy name, he hath dealt ill with this people; neither hast thou delivered thy people at all.

units.leftText: But the LORD said to Moses, “Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh, for because of My mighty hand he will let the people go; because of My strong hand he will drive them out of his land.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Now shalt thou see what I will do to Pharaoh: for by a strong hand shall he let them go, and by a strong hand shall he drive them out of his land.

units.leftText: God also told Moses, “I am the LORD.
units.rightText: And God spake unto Moses, and said unto him, I am Jehovah:

units.leftText: I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as God Almighty, but by My name the LORD I did not make Myself known to them.
units.rightText: and I appeared unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, as God Almighty; but by my name Jehovah I was not known to them.
leftNotes: 6:3 Hebrew El-Shaddai

units.leftText: I also established My covenant with them to give them the land of Canaan, the land where they lived as foreigners.
units.rightText: And I have also established my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojournings, wherein they sojourned.

units.leftText: Furthermore, I have heard the groaning of the Israelites, whom the Egyptians are enslaving, and I have remembered My covenant.
units.rightText: And moreover I have heard the groaning of the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians keep in bondage; and I have remembered my covenant.

units.leftText: Therefore tell the Israelites: ‘I am the LORD, and I will bring you out from under the yoke of the Egyptians and deliver you from their bondage. I will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with mighty acts of judgment.
units.rightText: Wherefore say unto the children of Israel, I am Jehovah, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and I will rid you out of their bondage, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm, and with great judgments:

units.leftText: I will take you as My own people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God, who brought you out from under the yoke of the Egyptians.
units.rightText: and I will take you to me for a people, and I will be to you a God; and ye shall know that I am Jehovah your God, who bringeth you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians.

units.leftText: And I will bring you into the land that I swore to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I will give it to you as a possession. I am the LORD!’”
units.rightText: And I will bring you in unto the land which I sware to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will give it you for a heritage: I am Jehovah.

units.leftText: Moses relayed this message to the Israelites, but on account of their broken spirit and cruel bondage, they did not listen to him.
units.rightText: And Moses spake so unto the children of Israel: but they hearkened not unto Moses for anguish of spirit, and for cruel bondage.

units.leftText: So the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Go and tell Pharaoh king of Egypt to let the Israelites go out of his land.”
units.rightText: Go in, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.

units.leftText: But in the LORD’s presence Moses replied, “If the Israelites will not listen to me, then why would Pharaoh listen to me, since I am unskilled in speech? ”
units.rightText: And Moses spake before Jehovah, saying, Behold, the children of Israel have not hearkened unto me; how then shall Pharaoh hear me, who am of uncircumcised lips?
leftNotes: 6:12 Hebrew I have uncircumcised lips; also in verse 30

units.leftText: Then the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron and gave them a charge concerning both the Israelites and Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the Israelites out of the land of Egypt. Genealogies of Moses and Aaron
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, and gave them a charge unto the children of Israel, and unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: These were the heads of their fathers’ houses: The sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, were Hanoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi. These were the clans of Reuben.
units.rightText: These are the heads of their fathers’ houses. The sons of Reuben the first-born of Israel: Hanoch, and Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi; these are the families of Reuben.

units.leftText: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman. These were the clans of Simeon.
units.rightText: And the sons of Simeon: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanitish woman; these are the families of Simeon.
leftNotes: 6:15 Zohar is a variant of Zerah; see Numbers 26:13|NUM 26:13* and 1 Chronicles 4:24.

units.leftText: These were the names of the sons of Levi according to their records: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Levi lived 137 years.
units.rightText: And these are the names of the sons of Levi according to their generations: Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari; and the years of the life of Levi were a hundred thirty and seven years.

units.leftText: The sons of Gershon were Libni and Shimei, by their clans.
units.rightText: The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, according to their families.

units.leftText: The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Kohath lived 133 years.
units.rightText: And the sons of Kohath: Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel; and the years of the life of Kohath were a hundred thirty and three years.

units.leftText: The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. These were the clans of the Levites according to their records.
units.rightText: And the sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites according to their generations.

units.leftText: And Amram married his father’s sister Jochebed, and she bore him Aaron and Moses. Amram lived 137 years.
units.rightText: And Amram took him Jochebed his father’s sister to wife; and she bare him Aaron and Moses: and the years of the life of Amram were a hundred and thirty and seven years.

units.leftText: The sons of Izhar were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
units.rightText: And the sons of Izhar: Korah, and Nepheg, and Zichri.

units.leftText: The sons of Uzziel were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
units.rightText: And the sons of Uzziel: Mishael, and Elzaphan, and Sithri.
leftNotes: 6:22 Elzaphan is a variant of Elizaphan; see Numbers 3:30|NUM 3:30*.

units.leftText: And Aaron married Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab and sister of Nahshon, and she bore him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
units.rightText: And Aaron took him Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab, the sister of Nahshon, to wife; and she bare him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

units.leftText: The sons of Korah were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph. These were the clans of the Korahites.
units.rightText: And the sons of Korah: Assir, and Elkanah, and Abiasaph; these are the families of the Korahites.
leftNotes: 6:24 Abiasaph is a variant of Ebiasaph; see 1 Chronicles 6:23|1CH 6:23* and 1 Chronicles 9:19.

units.leftText: Aaron’s son Eleazar married one of the daughters of Putiel, and she bore him Phinehas. These were the heads of the Levite families by their clans.
units.rightText: And Eleazar Aaron’s son took him one of the daughters of Putiel to wife; and she bare him Phinehas. These are the heads of the fathers’ houses of the Levites according to their families.

units.leftText: It was this Aaron and Moses to whom the LORD said, “Bring the Israelites out of the land of Egypt by their divisions.”
units.rightText: These are that Aaron and Moses, to whom Jehovah said, Bring out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt according to their hosts.

units.leftText: Moses and Aaron were the ones who spoke to Pharaoh king of Egypt in order to bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
units.rightText: These are they that spake to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring out the children of Israel from Egypt: these are that Moses and Aaron.

units.leftText: Now on the day that the LORD spoke to Moses in Egypt,
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the day when Jehovah spake unto Moses in the land of Egypt,

units.leftText: He said to him, “I am the LORD; tell Pharaoh king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
units.rightText: that Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying, I am Jehovah: speak thou unto Pharaoh king of Egypt all that I speak unto thee.

units.leftText: But in the LORD’s presence Moses replied, “Since I am unskilled in speech, why would Pharaoh listen to me?”
units.rightText: And Moses said before Jehovah, Behold, I am of uncircumcised lips, and how shall Pharaoh hearken unto me?

units.leftText: The LORD answered Moses, “See, I have made you like God to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will be your prophet.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, See, I have made thee as God to Pharaoh; and Aaron thy brother shall be thy prophet.

units.leftText: You are to speak all that I command you, and your brother Aaron is to tell Pharaoh to let the Israelites go out of his land.
units.rightText: Thou shalt speak all that I command thee; and Aaron thy brother shall speak unto Pharaoh, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.

units.leftText: But I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and though I will multiply My signs and wonders in the land of Egypt,
units.rightText: And I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and multiply my signs and my wonders in the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: Pharaoh will not listen to you.
units.rightText: But Pharaoh will not hearken unto you, and I will lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth my hosts, my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.

units.leftText: And the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD, when I stretch out My hand against Egypt and bring the Israelites out from among them.”
units.rightText: And the Egyptians shall know that I am Jehovah, when I stretch forth my hand upon Egypt, and bring out the children of Israel from among them.

units.leftText: So Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD had commanded them.
units.rightText: And Moses and Aaron did so; as Jehovah commanded them, so did they.

units.leftText: Moses was eighty years old and Aaron was eighty-three when they spoke to Pharaoh. Aaron’s Staff
units.rightText: And Moses was fourscore years old, and Aaron fourscore and three years old, when they spake unto Pharaoh.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,

units.leftText: “When Pharaoh tells you, ‘Perform a miracle,’ you are to say to Aaron, ‘Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh,’ and it will become a serpent. ”
units.rightText: When Pharaoh shall speak unto you, saying, Show a wonder for you; then thou shalt say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and cast it down before Pharaoh, that it become a serpent.
leftNotes: 7:9 Hebrew tannin; here and in verse 10, in contrast to Moses’ staff, which became a nachashin Exodus 4:3|EXO 4:3* and was noted again in Exodus 7:15

units.leftText: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did just as the LORD had commanded. Aaron threw his staff down before Pharaoh and his officials, and it became a serpent.
units.rightText: And Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharaoh, and they did so, as Jehovah had commanded: and Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.

units.leftText: But Pharaoh called the wise men and sorcerers and magicians of Egypt, and they also did the same things by their magic arts.
units.rightText: Then Pharaoh also called for the wise men and the sorcerers: and they also, the magicians of Egypt, did in like manner with their enchantments.

units.leftText: Each one threw down his staff, and it became a serpent. But Aaron’s staff swallowed up the other staffs.
units.rightText: For they cast down every man his rod, and they became serpents: but Aaron’s rod swallowed up their rods.

units.leftText: Still, Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said. The First Plague: Blood
units.rightText: And Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he hearkened not unto them; as Jehovah had spoken.
leftNotes: 7:13 Or stiffened or strengthened; also in verse 22

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh’s heart is unyielding; he refuses to let the people go.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Pharaoh’s heart is stubborn, he refuseth to let the people go.
leftNotes: 7:14 Or heavy or stubborn

units.leftText: Go to Pharaoh in the morning as you see him walking out to the water. Wait on the bank of the Nile to meet him, and take in your hand the staff that was changed into a snake.
units.rightText: Get thee unto Pharaoh in the morning; lo, he goeth out unto the water; and thou shalt stand by the river’s brink to meet him; and the rod which was turned to a serpent shalt thou take in thy hand.

units.leftText: Then say to him, ‘The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to tell you: Let My people go, so that they may worship Me in the wilderness. But until now you have not listened.
units.rightText: And thou shalt say unto him, Jehovah, the God of the Hebrews, hath sent me unto thee, saying, Let my people go, that they may serve me in the wilderness: and, behold, hitherto thou hast not hearkened.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD says: By this you will know that I am the LORD. Behold, with the staff in my hand I will strike the water of the Nile, and it will turn to blood.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah, In this thou shalt know that I am Jehovah: behold, I will smite with the rod that is in my hand upon the waters which are in the river, and they shall be turned to blood.

units.leftText: The fish in the Nile will die, the river will stink, and the Egyptians will be unable to drink its water.’”
units.rightText: And the fish that are in the river shall die, and the river shall become foul; and the Egyptians shall loathe to drink water from the river.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt— over their rivers and canals and ponds and all the reservoirs— that they may become blood.’ There will be blood throughout the land of Egypt, even in the vessels of wood and stone.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and stretch out thy hand over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers, over their streams, and over their pools, and over all their ponds of water, that they may become blood; and there shall be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood and in vessels of stone.

units.leftText: Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD had commanded; in the presence of Pharaoh and his officials, Aaron raised the staff and struck the water of the Nile, and all the water was turned to blood.
units.rightText: And Moses and Aaron did so, as Jehovah commanded; and he lifted up the rod, and smote the waters that were in the river, in the sight of Pharaoh, and in the sight of his servants; and all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood.
leftNotes: 7:20 Hebrew he raised the staff; see verse 19; some translators Moses raised the staff.

units.leftText: The fish in the Nile died, and the river smelled so bad that the Egyptians could not drink its water. And there was blood throughout the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And the fish that were in the river died; and the river became foul, and the Egyptians could not drink water from the river; and the blood was throughout all the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: But the magicians of Egypt did the same things by their magic arts. So Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said.
units.rightText: And the magicians of Egypt did in like manner with their enchantments: and Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he hearkened not unto them; as Jehovah had spoken.

units.leftText: Instead, Pharaoh turned around, went into his palace, and did not take any of this to heart.
units.rightText: And Pharaoh turned and went into his house, neither did he lay even this to heart.

units.leftText: So all the Egyptians dug around the Nile for water to drink, because they could not drink the water from the river.
units.rightText: And all the Egyptians digged round about the river for water to drink; for they could not drink of the water of the river.

units.leftText: And seven full days passed after the LORD had struck the Nile.
units.rightText: And seven days were fulfilled, after that Jehovah had smitten the river.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh and tell him that this is what the LORD says: ‘Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh, and say unto him, Thus saith Jehovah, Let my people go, that they may serve me.

units.leftText: But if you refuse to let them go, I will plague your whole country with frogs.
units.rightText: And if thou refuse to let them go, behold, I will smite all thy borders with frogs:

units.leftText: The Nile will teem with frogs, and they will come into your palace and up to your bedroom and onto your bed, into the houses of your officials and your people, and into your ovens and kneading bowls.
units.rightText: and the river shall swarm with frogs, which shall go up and come into thy house, and into thy bedchamber, and upon thy bed, and into the house of thy servants, and upon thy people, and into thine ovens, and into thy kneading-troughs:

units.leftText: The frogs will come up on you and your people and all your officials.’”
units.rightText: and the frogs shall come up both upon thee, and upon thy people, and upon all thy servants.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers and canals and ponds, and cause the frogs to come up onto the land of Egypt.’”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch forth thy hand with thy rod over the rivers, over the streams, and over the pools, and cause frogs to come up upon the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: So Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt; and the frogs came up, and covered the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: But the magicians did the same thing by their magic arts, and they also brought frogs up onto the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And the magicians did in like manner with their enchantments, and brought up frogs upon the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “Pray to the LORD to take the frogs away from me and my people. Then I will let your people go, that they may sacrifice to the LORD.”
units.rightText: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron, and said, Entreat Jehovah, that he take away the frogs from me, and from my people; and I will let the people go, that they may sacrifice unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: Moses said to Pharaoh, “You may have the honor over me. When shall I pray for you and your officials and your people that the frogs (except for those in the Nile) may be taken away from you and your houses?”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Pharaoh, Have thou this glory over me: against what time shall I entreat for thee, and for thy servants, and for thy people, that the frogs be destroyed from thee and thy houses, and remain in the river only?

units.leftText: “Tomorrow,” Pharaoh answered.
units.rightText: And he said, Against to-morrow. And he said, Be it according to thy word; that thou mayest know that there is none like unto Jehovah our God.

units.leftText: The frogs will depart from you and your houses and your officials and your people; they will remain only in the Nile.”
units.rightText: And the frogs shall depart from thee, and from thy houses, and from thy servants, and from thy people; they shall remain in the river only.

units.leftText: After Moses and Aaron had left Pharaoh, Moses cried out to the LORD for help with the frogs that He had brought against Pharaoh.
units.rightText: And Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh: and Moses cried unto Jehovah concerning the frogs which he had brought upon Pharaoh.

units.leftText: And the LORD did as Moses requested, and the frogs in the houses, the courtyards, and the fields died.
units.rightText: And Jehovah did according to the word of Moses; and the frogs died out of the houses, out of the courts, and out of the fields.

units.leftText: They were piled into countless heaps, and there was a terrible stench in the land.
units.rightText: And they gathered them together in heaps; and the land stank.

units.leftText: When Pharaoh saw that there was relief, however, he hardened his heart and would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said. The Third Plague: Gnats
units.rightText: But when Pharaoh saw that there was respite, he hardened his heart, and hearkened not unto them, as Jehovah had spoken.
leftNotes: 8:15 Or made heavy; also in verse 32

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the earth, that it may turn into swarms of gnats throughout the land of Egypt.’”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch out thy rod, and smite the dust of the earth, that it may become lice throughout all the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: This they did, and when Aaron stretched out his hand with his staff and struck the dust of the earth, gnats came upon man and beast. All the dust of the earth turned into gnats throughout the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And they did so; and Aaron stretched out his hand with his rod, and smote the dust of the earth, and there were lice upon man, and upon beast; all the dust of the earth became lice throughout all the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: The magicians tried to produce gnats using their magic arts, but they could not. And the gnats remained on man and beast.
units.rightText: And the magicians did so with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but they could not: and there were lice upon man, and upon beast.

units.leftText: “This is the finger of God,” the magicians said to Pharaoh. But Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said. The Fourth Plague: Flies
units.rightText: Then the magicians said unto Pharaoh, This is the finger of God: and Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he hearkened not unto them; as Jehovah had spoken.
leftNotes: 8:19 Or stiffened or strengthened

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Get up early in the morning, and when Pharaoh goes out to the water, stand before him and tell him that this is what the LORD says: ‘Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Rise up early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh; lo, he cometh forth to the water; and say unto him, Thus saith Jehovah, Let my people go, that they may serve me.

units.leftText: But if you will not let My people go, I will send swarms of flies upon you and your officials and your people and your houses. The houses of the Egyptians and even the ground where they stand will be full of flies.
units.rightText: Else, if thou wilt not let my people go, behold, I will send swarms of flies upon thee, and upon thy servants, and upon thy people, and into thy houses: and the houses of the Egyptians shall be full of swarms of flies, and also the ground whereon they are.
leftNotes: 8:21 Literally a noxious mixture; also in verses 22, 24, 29, and 31

units.leftText: But on that day I will give special treatment to the land of Goshen, where My people live; no swarms of flies will be found there. In this way you will know that I, the LORD, am in the land.
units.rightText: And I will set apart in that day the land of Goshen, in which my people dwell, that no swarms of flies shall be there; to the end thou mayest know that I am Jehovah in the midst of the earth.

units.leftText: I will make a distinction between My people and your people. This sign will take place tomorrow.’”
units.rightText: And I will put a division between my people and thy people: by to-morrow shall this sign be.
leftNotes: 8:23 LXX and Vulgate; Hebrew I will set redemption

units.leftText: And the LORD did so. Thick swarms of flies poured into Pharaoh’s palace and into the houses of his officials. Throughout Egypt the land was ruined by swarms of flies.
units.rightText: And Jehovah did so; and there came grievous swarms of flies into the house of Pharaoh, and into his servants’ houses: and in all the land of Egypt the land was corrupted by reason of the swarms of flies.

units.leftText: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “Go, sacrifice to your God within this land.”
units.rightText: And Pharaoh called for Moses and for Aaron, and said, Go ye, sacrifice to your God in the land.

units.leftText: But Moses replied, “It would not be right to do that, because the sacrifices we offer to the LORD our God would be detestable to the Egyptians. If we offer sacrifices that are detestable before the Egyptians, will they not stone us?
units.rightText: And Moses said, It is not meet so to do; for we shall sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians to Jehovah our God: lo, shall we sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes, and will they not stone us?

units.leftText: We must make a three-day journey into the wilderness and sacrifice to the LORD our God as He commands us.”
units.rightText: We will go three days’ journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice to Jehovah our God, as he shall command us.

units.leftText: Pharaoh answered, “I will let you go and sacrifice to the LORD your God in the wilderness, but you must not go very far. Now pray for me.”
units.rightText: And Pharaoh said, I will let you go, that ye may sacrifice to Jehovah your God in the wilderness; only ye shall not go very far away: entreat for me.

units.leftText: “As soon as I leave you,” Moses said, “I will pray to the LORD, so that tomorrow the swarms of flies will depart from Pharaoh and his officials and his people. But Pharaoh must not act deceitfully again by refusing to let the people go and sacrifice to the LORD.”
units.rightText: And Moses said, Behold, I go out from thee, and I will entreat Jehovah that the swarms of flies may depart from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people, to-morrow: only let not Pharaoh deal deceitfully any more in not letting the people go to sacrifice to Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then Moses left Pharaoh and prayed to the LORD,
units.rightText: And Moses went out from Pharaoh, and entreated Jehovah.

units.leftText: and the LORD did as Moses requested. He removed the swarms of flies from Pharaoh and his officials and his people; not one fly remained.
units.rightText: And Jehovah did according to the word of Moses; and he removed the swarms of flies from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people; there remained not one.

units.leftText: But Pharaoh hardened his heart this time as well, and he would not let the people go.
units.rightText: And Pharaoh hardened his heart this time also, and he did not let the people go.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh and tell him that this is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.
units.rightText: Then Jehovah said unto Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh, and tell him, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of the Hebrews, Let my people go, that they may serve me.

units.leftText: But if you continue to restrain them and refuse to let them go,
units.rightText: For if thou refuse to let them go, and wilt hold them still,

units.leftText: then the hand of the LORD will bring a severe plague on your livestock in the field— on your horses, donkeys, camels, herds, and flocks.
units.rightText: behold, the hand of Jehovah is upon thy cattle which are in the field, upon the horses, upon the asses, upon the camels, upon the herds, and upon the flocks: there shall be a very grievous murrain.

units.leftText: But the LORD will make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, so that no animal belonging to the Israelites will die.’”
units.rightText: And Jehovah shall make a distinction between the cattle of Israel and the cattle of Egypt; and there shall nothing die of all that belongeth to the children of Israel.

units.leftText: The LORD set a time, saying, “Tomorrow the LORD will do this in the land.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah appointed a set time, saying, To-morrow Jehovah shall do this thing in the land.

units.leftText: And the next day the LORD did just that. All the livestock of the Egyptians died, but not one animal belonging to the Israelites died.
units.rightText: And Jehovah did that thing on the morrow; and all the cattle of Egypt died; but of the cattle of the children of Israel died not one.

units.leftText: Pharaoh sent officials and found that none of the livestock of the Israelites had died. But Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not let the people go. The Sixth Plague: Boils
units.rightText: And Pharaoh sent, and, behold, there was not so much as one of the cattle of the Israelites dead. But the heart of Pharaoh was stubborn, and he did not let the people go.
leftNotes: 9:7 Or made heavy; also in verse 34

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Take handfuls of soot from the furnace; in the sight of Pharaoh, Moses is to toss it into the air.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses and unto Aaron, Take to you handfuls of ashes of the furnace, and let Moses sprinkle it toward heaven in the sight of Pharaoh.

units.leftText: It will become fine dust over all the land of Egypt, and festering boils will break out on man and beast throughout the land.”
units.rightText: And it shall become small dust over all the land of Egypt, and shall be a boil breaking forth with blains upon man and upon beast, throughout all the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: So they took soot from the furnace and stood before Pharaoh. Moses tossed it into the air, and festering boils broke out on man and beast.
units.rightText: And they took ashes of the furnace, and stood before Pharaoh; and Moses sprinkled it up toward heaven; and it became a boil breaking forth with blains upon man and upon beast.

units.leftText: The magicians could not stand before Moses, because the boils had broken out on them and on all the Egyptians.
units.rightText: And the magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils; for the boils were upon the magicians, and upon all the Egyptians.

units.leftText: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said to Moses. The Seventh Plague: Hail
units.rightText: And Jehovah hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he hearkened not unto them, as Jehovah had spoken unto Moses.
leftNotes: 9:12 Or stiffened or strengthened; also in verse 35

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Get up early in the morning, stand before Pharaoh, and tell him that this is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Rise up early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh, and say unto him, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of the Hebrews, Let my people go, that they may serve me.

units.leftText: Otherwise, I will send all My plagues against you and your officials and your people, so you may know that there is no one like Me in all the earth.
units.rightText: For I will this time send all my plagues upon thy heart, and upon thy servants, and upon thy people; that thou mayest know that there is none like me in all the earth.
leftNotes: 9:14 Hebrew against your heart or against your inner man

units.leftText: For by this time I could have stretched out My hand and struck you and your people with a plague to wipe you off the earth.
units.rightText: For now I had put forth my hand, and smitten thee and thy people with pestilence, and thou hadst been cut off from the earth:

units.leftText: But I have raised you up for this very purpose, that I might display My power to you, and that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth.
units.rightText: but in very deed for this cause have I made thee to stand, to show thee my power, and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth.
leftNotes: 9:16 Or have spared you
9:16 LXX in you
9:16 Cited in Romans 9:17|ROM 9:17*

units.leftText: Still, you lord it over My people and do not allow them to go.
units.rightText: As yet exaltest thou thyself against my people, that thou wilt not let them go?

units.leftText: Behold, at this time tomorrow I will rain down the worst hail that has ever fallen on Egypt, from the day it was founded until now.
units.rightText: Behold, to-morrow about this time I will cause it to rain a very grievous hail, such as hath not been in Egypt since the day it was founded even until now.

units.leftText: So give orders now to shelter your livestock and everything you have in the field. Every man or beast that remains in the field and is not brought inside will die when the hail comes down upon them.’”
units.rightText: Now therefore send, hasten in thy cattle and all that thou hast in the field; for every man and beast that shall be found in the field, and shall not be brought home, the hail shall come down upon them, and they shall die.

units.leftText: Those among Pharaoh’s officials who feared the word of the LORD hurried to bring their servants and livestock to shelter,
units.rightText: He that feared the word of Jehovah among the servants of Pharaoh made his servants and his cattle flee into the houses:

units.leftText: but those who disregarded the word of the LORD left their servants and livestock in the field.
units.rightText: and he that regarded not the word of Jehovah left his servants and his cattle in the field.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, so that hail may fall on all the land of Egypt— on man and beast and every plant of the field throughout the land of Egypt.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Stretch forth thy hand toward heaven, that there may be hail in all the land of Egypt, upon man, and upon beast, and upon every herb of the field, throughout the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: So Moses stretched out his staff toward heaven, and the LORD sent thunder and hail, and lightning struck the earth. So the LORD rained down hail upon the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And Moses stretched forth his rod toward heaven: and Jehovah sent thunder and hail, and fire ran down unto the earth; and Jehovah rained hail upon the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: The hail fell and the lightning continued flashing through it. The hail was so severe that nothing like it had ever been seen in all the land of Egypt from the time it became a nation.
units.rightText: So there was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous, such as had not been in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.

units.leftText: Throughout the land of Egypt, the hail struck down everything in the field, both man and beast; it beat down every plant of the field and stripped every tree.
units.rightText: And the hail smote throughout all the land of Egypt all that was in the field, both man and beast; and the hail smote every herb of the field, and brake every tree of the field.

units.leftText: The only place where it did not hail was in the land of Goshen, where the Israelites lived.
units.rightText: Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, was there no hail.

units.leftText: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron. “This time I have sinned,” he said. “The LORD is righteous, and I and my people are wicked.
units.rightText: And Pharaoh sent, and called for Moses and Aaron, and said unto them, I have sinned this time: Jehovah is righteous, and I and my people are wicked.

units.leftText: Pray to the LORD, for there has been enough of God’s thunder and hail. I will let you go; you do not need to stay any longer.”
units.rightText: Entreat Jehovah; for there hath been enough of these mighty thunderings and hail; and I will let you go, and ye shall stay no longer.

units.leftText: Moses said to him, “When I have left the city, I will spread out my hands to the LORD. The thunder will cease, and there will be no more hail, so that you may know that the earth is the LORD’s.
units.rightText: And Moses said unto him, As soon as I am gone out of the city, I will spread abroad my hands unto Jehovah; the thunders shall cease, neither shall there be any more hail; that thou mayest know that the earth is Jehovah’s.

units.leftText: But as for you and your officials, I know that you still do not fear the LORD our God.”
units.rightText: But as for thee and thy servants, I know that ye will not yet fear Jehovah God.

units.leftText: (Now the flax and barley were destroyed, since the barley was ripe and the flax was in bloom;
units.rightText: And the flax and the barley were smitten: for the barley was in the ear, and the flax was in bloom.

units.leftText: but the wheat and spelt were not destroyed, because they are late crops.)
units.rightText: But the wheat and the spelt were not smitten: for they were not grown up.

units.leftText: Then Moses departed from Pharaoh, went out of the city, and spread out his hands to the LORD. The thunder and hail ceased, and the rain no longer poured down on the land.
units.rightText: And Moses went out of the city from Pharaoh, and spread abroad his hands unto Jehovah: and the thunders and hail ceased, and the rain was not poured upon the earth.

units.leftText: When Pharaoh saw that the rain and hail and thunder had ceased, he sinned again and hardened his heart — he and his officials.
units.rightText: And when Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunders were ceased, he sinned yet more, and hardened his heart, he and his servants.

units.leftText: So Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not let the Israelites go, just as the LORD had said through Moses.
units.rightText: And the heart of Pharaoh was hardened, and he did not let the children of Israel go, as Jehovah had spoken by Moses.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the hearts of his officials, that I may perform these miraculous signs of Mine among them,
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh: for I have hardened his heart, and the heart of his servants, that I may show these my signs in the midst of them,
leftNotes: 10:1 Or made heavy

units.leftText: and that you may tell your children and grandchildren how severely I dealt with the Egyptians when I performed miraculous signs among them, so that all of you may know that I am the LORD.”
units.rightText: and that thou mayest tell in the ears of thy son, and of thy son’s son, what things I have wrought upon Egypt, and my signs which I have done among them; that ye may know that I am Jehovah.

units.leftText: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and told him, “This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘How long will you refuse to humble yourself before Me? Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.
units.rightText: And Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharaoh, and said unto him, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of the Hebrews, How long wilt thou refuse to humble thyself before me? let my people go, that they may serve me.

units.leftText: But if you refuse to let My people go, I will bring locusts into your territory tomorrow.
units.rightText: Else, if thou refuse to let my people go, behold, to-morrow will I bring locusts into thy border:

units.leftText: They will cover the face of the land so that no one can see it. They will devour whatever is left after the hail and eat every tree that grows in your fields.
units.rightText: and they shall cover the face of the earth, so that one shall not be able to see the earth: and they shall eat the residue of that which is escaped, which remaineth unto you from the hail, and shall eat every tree which groweth for you out of the field:
