units.leftText: They will fill your houses and the houses of all your officials and every Egyptian— something neither your fathers nor your grandfathers have seen since the day they came into this land.’” Then Moses turned and left Pharaoh’s presence.
units.rightText: and thy houses shall be filled, and the houses of all thy servants, and the houses of all the Egyptians; as neither thy fathers nor thy fathers’ fathers have seen, since the day that they were upon the earth unto this day. And he turned, and went out from Pharaoh.

units.leftText: Pharaoh’s officials asked him, “How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the people go, so that they may worship the LORD their God. Do you not yet realize that Egypt lies in ruins?”
units.rightText: And Pharaoh’s servants said unto him, How long shall this man be a snare unto us? let the men go, that they may serve Jehovah their God: knowest thou not yet that Egypt is destroyed?

units.leftText: So Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. “Go, worship the LORD your God,” he said. “But who exactly will be going?”
units.rightText: And Moses and Aaron were brought again unto Pharaoh: and he said unto them, Go, serve Jehovah your God; but who are they that shall go?

units.leftText: “We will go with our young and old,” Moses replied. “We will go with our sons and daughters, and with our flocks and herds, for we must hold a feast to the LORD.”
units.rightText: And Moses said, We will go with our young and with our old; with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our herds will we go; for we must hold a feast unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then Pharaoh told them, “May the LORD be with you if I ever let you go with your little ones. Clearly you are bent on evil.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, So be Jehovah with you, as I will let you go, and your little ones: look to it; for evil is before you.

units.leftText: No, only the men may go and worship the LORD, since that is what you have been requesting.” And Moses and Aaron were driven from Pharaoh’s presence.
units.rightText: Not so: go now ye that are men, and serve Jehovah; for that is what ye desire. And they were driven out from Pharaoh’s presence.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt, so that the locusts may swarm over it and devour every plant in the land — everything that the hail has left behind.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Stretch out thy hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that they may come up upon the land of Egypt, and eat every herb of the land, even all that the hail hath left.

units.leftText: So Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and throughout that day and night the LORD sent an east wind across the land. By morning the east wind had brought the locusts.
units.rightText: And Moses stretched forth his rod over the land of Egypt, and Jehovah brought an east wind upon the land all that day, and all the night; and when it was morning, the east wind brought the locusts.

units.leftText: The locusts swarmed across the land and settled over the entire territory of Egypt. Never before had there been so many locusts, and never again will there be.
units.rightText: And the locusts went up over all the land of Egypt, and rested in all the borders of Egypt; very grievous were they; before them there were no such locusts as they, neither after them shall be such.

units.leftText: They covered the face of all the land until it was black, and they consumed all the plants on the ground and all the fruit on the trees that the hail had left behind. Nothing green was left on any tree or plant in all the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: For they covered the face of the whole earth, so that the land was darkened; and they did eat every herb of the land, and all the fruit of the trees which the hail had left: and there remained not any green thing, either tree or herb of the field, through all the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: Pharaoh quickly summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you.
units.rightText: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron in haste; and he said, I have sinned against Jehovah your God, and against you.

units.leftText: Now please forgive my sin once more and appeal to the LORD your God, that He may remove this death from me.”
units.rightText: Now therefore forgive, I pray thee, my sin only this once, and entreat Jehovah your God, that he may take away from me this death only.

units.leftText: So Moses left Pharaoh’s presence and appealed to the LORD.
units.rightText: And he went out from Pharaoh, and entreated Jehovah.

units.leftText: And the LORD changed the wind to a very strong west wind that carried off the locusts and blew them into the Red Sea. Not a single locust remained anywhere in Egypt.
units.rightText: And Jehovah turned an exceeding strong west wind, which took up the locusts, and drove them into the Red Sea; there remained not one locust in all the border of Egypt.
leftNotes: 10:19 Or the Sea of Reeds

units.leftText: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not let the Israelites go. The Ninth Plague: Darkness
units.rightText: But Jehovah hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not let the children of Israel go.
leftNotes: 10:20 Or stiffened or strengthened; also in verse 27

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, so that darkness may spread over the land of Egypt — a palpable darkness.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Stretch out thy hand toward heaven, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness which may be felt.

units.leftText: So Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and total darkness covered all the land of Egypt for three days.
units.rightText: And Moses stretched forth his hand toward heaven; and there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days;

units.leftText: No one could see anyone else, and for three days no one left his place. Yet all the Israelites had light in their dwellings.
units.rightText: they saw not one another, neither rose any one from his place for three days: but all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.

units.leftText: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and said, “Go, worship the LORD. Even your little ones may go with you; only your flocks and herds must stay behind.”
units.rightText: And Pharaoh called unto Moses, and said, Go ye, serve Jehovah; only let your flocks and your herds be stayed: let your little ones also go with you.

units.leftText: But Moses replied, “You must also provide us with sacrifices and burnt offerings to present to the LORD our God.
units.rightText: And Moses said, Thou must also give into our hand sacrifices and burnt-offerings, that we may sacrifice unto Jehovah our God.

units.leftText: Even our livestock must go with us; not a hoof will be left behind, for we will need some of them to worship the LORD our God, and we will not know how we are to worship the LORD until we arrive.”
units.rightText: Our cattle also shall go with us; there shall not a hoof be left behind: for thereof must we take to serve Jehovah our God; and we know not with what we must serve Jehovah, until we come thither.

units.leftText: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he was unwilling to let them go.
units.rightText: But Jehovah hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not let them go.

units.leftText: “Depart from me!” Pharaoh said to Moses. “Make sure you never see my face again, for on the day you see my face, you will die.”
units.rightText: And Pharaoh said unto him, Get thee from me, take heed to thyself, see my face no more; for in the day thou seest my face thou shalt die.

units.leftText: “As you say,” Moses replied, “I will never see your face again.”
units.rightText: And Moses said, Thou hast spoken well; I will see thy face again no more.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “I will bring upon Pharaoh and Egypt one more plague. After that, he will allow you to leave this place. And when he lets you go, he will drive you out completely.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Yet one plague more will I bring upon Pharaoh, and upon Egypt; afterwards he will let you go hence: when he shall let you go, he shall surely thrust you out hence altogether.

units.leftText: Now announce to the people that men and women alike should ask their neighbors for articles of silver and gold.”
units.rightText: Speak now in the ears of the people, and let them ask every man of his neighbor, and every woman of her neighbor, jewels of silver, and jewels of gold.

units.leftText: And the LORD gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians. Moreover, Moses himself was highly regarded in Egypt by Pharaoh’s officials and by the people.
units.rightText: And Jehovah gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians. Moreover the man Moses was very great in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh’s servants, and in the sight of the people.

units.leftText: So Moses declared, “This is what the LORD says: ‘About midnight I will go throughout Egypt,
units.rightText: And Moses said, Thus saith Jehovah, About midnight will I go out into the midst of Egypt:

units.leftText: and every firstborn son in the land of Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne, to the firstborn of the servant girl behind the hand mill, as well as the firstborn of all the cattle.
units.rightText: and all the first-born in the land of Egypt shall die, from the first-born of Pharaoh that sitteth upon his throne, even unto the first-born of the maid-servant that is behind the mill; and all the first-born of cattle.

units.leftText: Then a great cry will go out over all the land of Egypt. Such an outcry has never been heard before and will never be heard again.
units.rightText: And there shall be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as there hath not been, nor shall be any more.

units.leftText: But among all the Israelites, not even a dog will snarl at man or beast.’
units.rightText: But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that Jehovah doth make a distinction between the Egyptians and Israel.
leftNotes: 11:7 Some translators close this quotation at the end of the verse.

units.leftText: And all these officials of yours will come and bow before me, saying, ‘Go, you and all the people who follow you!’ After that, I will depart.” And hot with anger, Moses left Pharaoh’s presence.
units.rightText: And all these thy servants shall come down unto me, and bow down themselves unto me, saying, Get thee out, and all the people that follow thee: and after that I will go out. And he went out from Pharaoh in hot anger.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that My wonders may be multiplied in the land of Egypt.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Pharaoh will not hearken unto you; that my wonders may be multiplied in the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: Moses and Aaron did all these wonders before Pharaoh, but the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart so that he would not let the Israelites go out of his land.
units.rightText: And Moses and Aaron did all these wonders before Pharaoh: and Jehovah hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not let the children of Israel go out of his land.
leftNotes: 11:10 Or stiffened or strengthened

units.leftText: Now the LORD said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,

units.leftText: “This month is the beginning of months for you; it shall be the first month of your year.
units.rightText: This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.

units.leftText: Tell the whole congregation of Israel that on the tenth day of this month each man must select a lamb for his family, one per household.
units.rightText: Speak ye unto all the congregation of Israel, saying, In the tenth day of this month they shall take to them every man a lamb, according to their fathers’ houses, a lamb for a household:
leftNotes: 12:3 The Hebrew word can mean lamb or kid; also in verses 4 and 5.

units.leftText: If the household is too small for a whole lamb, they are to share with the nearest neighbor based on the number of people, and apportion the lamb accordingly.
units.rightText: and if the household be too little for a lamb, then shall he and his neighbor next unto his house take one according to the number of the souls; according to every man’s eating ye shall make your count for the lamb.

units.leftText: Your lamb must be an unblemished year-old male, and you may take it from the sheep or the goats.
units.rightText: Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male a year old: ye shall take it from the sheep, or from the goats:

units.leftText: You must keep it until the fourteenth day of the month, when the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel will slaughter the animals at twilight.
units.rightText: and ye shall keep it until the fourteenth day of the same month; and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it at even.
leftNotes: 12:6 Hebrew between the two evenings

units.leftText: They are to take some of the blood and put it on the sides and tops of the doorframes of the houses where they eat the lambs.
units.rightText: And they shall take of the blood, and put it on the two side-posts and on the lintel, upon the houses wherein they shall eat it.
leftNotes: 12:7 Literally on the two doorposts and on the lintel; similarly in verses 22 and 23

units.leftText: They are to eat the meat that night, roasted over the fire, along with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
units.rightText: And they shall eat the flesh in that night, roast with fire, and unleavened bread; with bitter herbs they shall eat it.

units.leftText: Do not eat any of the meat raw or cooked in boiling water, but only roasted over the fire— its head and legs and inner parts.
units.rightText: Eat not of it raw, nor boiled at all with water, but roast with fire; its head with its legs and with the inwards thereof.

units.leftText: Do not leave any of it until morning; before the morning you must burn up any part that is left over.
units.rightText: And ye shall let nothing of it remain until the morning; but that which remaineth of it until the morning ye shall burn with fire.

units.leftText: This is how you are to eat it: You must be fully dressed for travel, with your sandals on your feet and your staff in your hand. You are to eat in haste; it is the LORD’s Passover.
units.rightText: And thus shall ye eat it: with your loins girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and ye shall eat it in haste: it is Jehovah’s passover.
leftNotes: 12:11 Literally Gird up your loins

units.leftText: On that night I will pass through the land of Egypt and strike down every firstborn male, both man and beast, and I will execute judgment against all the gods of Egypt. I am the LORD.
units.rightText: For I will go through the land of Egypt in that night, and will smite all the first-born in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments: I am Jehovah.

units.leftText: The blood on the houses where you are staying will be a sign; when I see the blood, I will pass over you. No plague will fall on you to destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt. The Feast of Unleavened Bread (Leviticus 23:4–8|LEV 23:4-8*; Numbers 28:16–25|NUM 28:16-25*; Deuteronomy 16:1–8|DEU 16:1-8*)
units.rightText: And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and there shall no plague be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: And this day will be a memorial for you, and you are to celebrate it as a feast to the LORD, as a permanent statute for the generations to come.
units.rightText: And this day shall be unto you for a memorial, and ye shall keep it a feast to Jehovah: throughout your generations ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.

units.leftText: For seven days you must eat unleavened bread. On the first day you are to remove the leaven from your houses. Whoever eats anything leavened from the first day through the seventh must be cut off from Israel.
units.rightText: Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread; even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses: for whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.

units.leftText: On the first day you are to hold a sacred assembly, and another on the seventh day. You must not do any work on those days, except to prepare the meals — that is all you may do.
units.rightText: And in the first day there shall be to you a holy convocation, and in the seventh day a holy convocation; no manner of work shall be done in them, save that which every man must eat, that only may be done by you.

units.leftText: So you are to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread, for on this very day I brought your divisions out of the land of Egypt. You must keep this day as a permanent statute for the generations to come.
units.rightText: And ye shall observe the feast of unleavened bread; for in this selfsame day have I brought your hosts out of the land of Egypt: therefore shall ye observe this day throughout your generations by an ordinance for ever.
leftNotes: 12:17 That is, the seven-day period after the Passover during which no leaven may be eaten

units.leftText: In the first month you are to eat unleavened bread, from the evening of the fourteenth day until the evening of the twenty-first day.
units.rightText: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at even, ye shall eat unleavened bread, until the one and twentieth day of the month at even.

units.leftText: For seven days there must be no leaven found in your houses. If anyone eats something leavened, that person, whether a foreigner or native of the land, must be cut off from the congregation of Israel.
units.rightText: Seven days shall there be no leaven found in your houses: for whosoever eateth that which is leavened, that soul shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether he be a sojourner, or one that is born in the land.

units.leftText: You are not to eat anything leavened; eat unleavened bread in all your homes.”
units.rightText: Ye shall eat nothing leavened; in all your habitations shall ye eat unleavened bread.

units.leftText: Then Moses summoned all the elders of Israel and told them, “Go at once and select for yourselves a lamb for each family, and slaughter the Passover lamb.
units.rightText: Then Moses called for all the elders of Israel, and said unto them, Draw out, and take you lambs according to your families, and kill the passover.

units.leftText: Take a cluster of hyssop, dip it into the blood in the basin, and brush the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe. None of you shall go out the door of his house until morning.
units.rightText: And ye shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and strike the lintel and the two side-posts with the blood that is in the basin; and none of you shall go out of the door of his house until the morning.

units.leftText: When the LORD passes through to strike down the Egyptians, He will see the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe and will pass over that doorway; so He will not allow the destroyer to enter your houses and strike you down.
units.rightText: For Jehovah will pass through to smite the Egyptians; and when he seeth the blood upon the lintel, and on the two side-posts, Jehovah will pass over the door, and will not suffer the destroyer to come in unto your houses to smite you.

units.leftText: And you are to keep this command as a permanent statute for you and your descendants.
units.rightText: And ye shall observe this thing for an ordinance to thee and to thy sons for ever.

units.leftText: When you enter the land that the LORD will give you as He promised, you are to keep this service.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, when ye are come to the land which Jehovah will give you, according as he hath promised, that ye shall keep this service.

units.leftText: When your children ask you, ‘What does this service mean to you?’
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, when your children shall say unto you, What mean ye by this service?

units.leftText: you are to reply, ‘It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD, who passed over the houses of the Israelites in Egypt when He struck down the Egyptians and spared our homes.’”
units.rightText: that ye shall say, It is the sacrifice of Jehovah’s passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he smote the Egyptians, and delivered our houses. And the people bowed the head and worshipped.

units.leftText: And the Israelites went and did just what the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron. The Tenth Plague: Death of the Firstborn
units.rightText: And the children of Israel went and did so; as Jehovah had commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they.

units.leftText: Now at midnight the LORD struck down every firstborn male in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sat on his throne, to the firstborn of the prisoner in the dungeon, as well as all the firstborn among the livestock.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at midnight, that Jehovah smote all the first-born in the land of Egypt, from the first-born of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the first-born of the captive that was in the dungeon; and all the first-born of cattle.

units.leftText: During the night Pharaoh got up — he and all his officials and all the Egyptians — and there was loud wailing in Egypt; for there was no house without someone dead. The Exodus Begins
units.rightText: And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for there was not a house where there was not one dead.

units.leftText: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron by night and said, “Get up, leave my people, both you and the Israelites! Go, worship the LORD as you have requested.
units.rightText: And he called for Moses and Aaron by night, and said, Rise up, get you forth from among my people, both ye and the children of Israel; and go, serve Jehovah, as ye have said.

units.leftText: Take your flocks and herds as well, just as you have said, and depart! And bless me also.”
units.rightText: Take both your flocks and your herds, as ye have said, and be gone; and bless me also.

units.leftText: And in order to send them out of the land quickly, the Egyptians urged the people on. “For otherwise,” they said, “we are all going to die!”
units.rightText: And the Egyptians were urgent upon the people, to send them out of the land in haste; for they said, We are all dead men.

units.leftText: So the people took their dough before it was leavened, carrying it on their shoulders in kneading bowls wrapped in clothing.
units.rightText: And the people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneading-troughs being bound up in their clothes upon their shoulders.

units.leftText: Furthermore, the Israelites acted on Moses’ word and asked the Egyptians for articles of silver and gold, and for clothing.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel did according to the word of Moses; and they asked of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment:

units.leftText: And the LORD gave the people such favor in the sight of the Egyptians that they granted their request. In this way they plundered the Egyptians.
units.rightText: and Jehovah gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they let them have what they asked. And they despoiled the Egyptians.

units.leftText: The Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Succoth with about 600,000 men on foot, besides women and children.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot that were men, besides children.
leftNotes: 12:37 Succoth means booths or shelters or tabernacles.

units.leftText: And a mixed multitude also went up with them, along with great droves of livestock, both flocks and herds.
units.rightText: And a mixed multitude went up also with them; and flocks, and herds, even very much cattle.

units.leftText: Since their dough had no leaven, the people baked what they had brought out of Egypt into unleavened loaves. For when they had been driven out of Egypt, they could not delay and had not prepared any provisions for themselves.
units.rightText: And they baked unleavened cakes of the dough which they brought forth out of Egypt; for it was not leavened, because they were thrust out of Egypt, and could not tarry, neither had they prepared for themselves any victuals.

units.leftText: Now the duration of the Israelites’ stay in Egypt was 430 years.
units.rightText: Now the time that the children of Israel dwelt in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years.
leftNotes: 12:40 MT; SP in Canaan and Egypt; LXX in Egypt and Canaan

units.leftText: At the end of the 430 years, to the very day, all the LORD’s divisions went out of the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at the end of four hundred and thirty years, even the selfsame day it came to pass, that all the hosts of Jehovah went out from the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: Because the LORD kept a vigil that night to bring them out of the land of Egypt, this same night is to be a vigil to the LORD, to be observed by all the Israelites for the generations to come. Instructions for the Passover
units.rightText: It is a night to be much observed unto Jehovah for bringing them out from the land of Egypt: this is that night of Jehovah, to be much observed of all the children of Israel throughout their generations.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the statute of the Passover: No foreigner is to eat of it.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses and Aaron, This is the ordinance of the passover: there shall no foreigner eat thereof;

units.leftText: But any slave who has been purchased may eat of it, after you have circumcised him.
units.rightText: but every man’s servant that is bought for money, when thou hast circumcised him, then shall he eat thereof.

units.leftText: A temporary resident or hired hand shall not eat the Passover.
units.rightText: A sojourner and a hired servant shall not eat thereof.

units.leftText: It must be eaten inside one house. You are not to take any of the meat outside the house, and you may not break any of the bones.
units.rightText: In one house shall it be eaten; thou shalt not carry forth aught of the flesh abroad out of the house; neither shall ye break a bone thereof.

units.leftText: The whole congregation of Israel must celebrate it.
units.rightText: All the congregation of Israel shall keep it.

units.leftText: If a foreigner resides with you and wants to celebrate the LORD’s Passover, all the males in the household must be circumcised; then he may come near to celebrate it, and he shall be like a native of the land. But no uncircumcised man may eat of it.
units.rightText: And when a stranger shall sojourn with thee, and will keep the passover to Jehovah, let all his males be circumcised, and then let him come near and keep it; and he shall be as one that is born in the land: but no uncircumcised person shall eat thereof.

units.leftText: The same law shall apply to both the native and the foreigner who resides among you.”
units.rightText: One law shall be to him that is home-born, and unto the stranger that sojourneth among you.

units.leftText: Then all the Israelites did this — they did just as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron.
units.rightText: Thus did all the children of Israel; as Jehovah commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they.

units.leftText: And on that very day the LORD brought the Israelites out of the land of Egypt by their divisions.
units.rightText: And it came to pass the selfsame day, that Jehovah did bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their hosts.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Consecrate to Me every firstborn male. The firstborn from every womb among the Israelites belongs to Me, both of man and beast.”
units.rightText: Sanctify unto me all the first-born, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of beast: it is mine.
leftNotes: 13:2 Cited in Luke 2:23|LUK 2:23*

units.leftText: So Moses told the people, “Remember this day, the day you came out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery; for the LORD brought you out of it by the strength of His hand. And nothing leavened shall be eaten.
units.rightText: And Moses said unto the people, Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand Jehovah brought you out from this place: there shall no leavened bread be eaten.

units.leftText: Today, in the month of Abib, you are leaving.
units.rightText: This day ye go forth in the month Abib.
leftNotes: 13:4 Abib was the first month of the ancient Hebrew lunar calendar, usually occurring within the months of March and April.

units.leftText: And when the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites — the land He swore to your fathers that He would give you, a land flowing with milk and honey — you shall keep this service in this month.
units.rightText: And it shall be, when Jehovah shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite, which he sware unto thy fathers to give thee, a land flowing with milk and honey, that thou shalt keep this service in this month.

units.leftText: For seven days you are to eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a feast to the LORD.
units.rightText: Seven days thou shalt eat unleavened bread, and in the seventh day shall be a feast to Jehovah.

units.leftText: Unleavened bread shall be eaten during those seven days. Nothing leavened may be found among you, nor shall leaven be found anywhere within your borders.
units.rightText: Unleavened bread shall be eaten throughout the seven days; and there shall no leavened bread be seen with thee, neither shall there be leaven seen with thee, in all thy borders.

units.leftText: And on that day you are to explain to your son, ‘This is because of what the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt.’
units.rightText: And thou shalt tell thy son in that day, saying, It is because of that which Jehovah did for me when I came forth out of Egypt.

units.leftText: It shall be a sign for you on your hand and a reminder on your forehead that the Law of the LORD is to be on your lips. For with a mighty hand the LORD brought you out of Egypt.
units.rightText: And it shall be for a sign unto thee upon thy hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes, that the law of Jehovah may be in thy mouth: for with a strong hand hath Jehovah brought thee out of Egypt.

units.leftText: Therefore you shall keep this statute at the appointed time year after year.
units.rightText: Thou shalt therefore keep this ordinance in its season from year to year.

units.leftText: And after the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites and gives it to you, as He swore to you and your fathers,
units.rightText: And it shall be, when Jehovah shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanite, as he sware unto thee and to thy fathers, and shall give it thee,

units.leftText: you are to present to the LORD the firstborn male of every womb. All the firstborn males of your livestock belong to the LORD.
units.rightText: that thou shalt set apart unto Jehovah all that openeth the womb, and every firstling which thou hast that cometh of a beast; the males shall be Jehovah’s.

units.leftText: You must redeem every firstborn donkey with a lamb, and if you do not redeem it, you are to break its neck. And every firstborn of your sons you must redeem.
units.rightText: And every firstling of an ass thou shalt redeem with a lamb; and if thou wilt not redeem it, then thou shalt break its neck: and all the first-born of man among thy sons shalt thou redeem.

units.leftText: In the future, when your son asks you, ‘What does this mean?’ you are to tell him, ‘With a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
units.rightText: And it shall be, when thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What is this? that thou shalt say unto him, By strength of hand Jehovah brought us out from Egypt, from the house of bondage:

units.leftText: And when Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, the LORD killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both of man and beast. This is why I sacrifice to the LORD the firstborn male of every womb, but I redeem all the firstborn of my sons.’
units.rightText: and it came to pass, when Pharaoh would hardly let us go, that Jehovah slew all the first-born in the land of Egypt, both the first-born of man, and the first-born of beast: therefore I sacrifice to Jehovah all that openeth the womb, being males; but all the first-born of my sons I redeem.

units.leftText: So it shall serve as a sign on your hand and a symbol on your forehead, for with a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt.” The Pillars of Cloud and Fire
units.rightText: And it shall be for a sign upon thy hand, and for frontlets between thine eyes: for by strength of hand Jehovah brought us forth out of Egypt.

units.leftText: When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them along the road through the land of the Philistines, though it was shorter. For God said, “If the people face war, they might change their minds and return to Egypt.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that God led them not by the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt:

units.leftText: So God led the people around by the way of the wilderness toward the Red Sea. And the Israelites left the land of Egypt arrayed for battle.
units.rightText: but God led the people about, by the way of the wilderness by the Red Sea: and the children of Israel went up armed out of the land of Egypt.
leftNotes: 13:18 Or the Sea of Reeds
13:18 LXX left the land of Egypt in the fifth generation

units.leftText: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him because Joseph had made the sons of Israel swear a solemn oath when he said, “God will surely attend to you, and then you must carry my bones with you from this place.”
units.rightText: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.

units.leftText: They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham on the edge of the wilderness.
units.rightText: And they took their journey from Succoth, and encamped in Etham, in the edge of the wilderness.

units.leftText: And the LORD went before them in a pillar of cloud to guide their way by day, and in a pillar of fire to give them light by night, so that they could travel by day or night.
units.rightText: And Jehovah went before them by day in a pillar of cloud, to lead them the way, and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; that they might go by day and by night:

units.leftText: Neither the pillar of cloud by day nor the pillar of fire by night left its place before the people.
units.rightText: the pillar of cloud by day, and the pillar of fire by night, departed not from before the people.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Tell the Israelites to turn back and encamp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea. You are to encamp by the sea, directly opposite Baal-zephon.
units.rightText: Speak unto the children of Israel, that they turn back and encamp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, before Baal-zephon: over against it shall ye encamp by the sea.

units.leftText: For Pharaoh will say of the Israelites, ‘They are wandering the land in confusion; the wilderness has boxed them in.’
units.rightText: And Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel, They are entangled in the land, the wilderness hath shut them in.

units.leftText: And I will harden Pharaoh’s heart so that he will pursue them. But I will gain honor by means of Pharaoh and all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD.” So this is what the Israelites did.
units.rightText: And I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and he shall follow after them; and I will get me honor upon Pharaoh, and upon all his host: and the Egyptians shall know that I am Jehovah. And they did so.
leftNotes: 14:4 Or stiffen or strengthen; similarly in verses 8 and 17

units.leftText: When the king of Egypt was told that the people had fled, Pharaoh and his officials changed their minds about them and said, “What have we done? We have released Israel from serving us.”
units.rightText: And it was told the king of Egypt that the people were fled: and the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was changed towards the people, and they said, What is this we have done, that we have let Israel go from serving us?

units.leftText: So Pharaoh prepared his chariot and took his army with him.
units.rightText: And he made ready his chariot, and took his people with him:

units.leftText: He took 600 of the best chariots, and all the other chariots of Egypt, with officers over all of them.
units.rightText: and he took six hundred chosen chariots, and all the chariots of Egypt, and captains over all of them.

units.leftText: And the LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt so that he pursued the Israelites, who were marching out defiantly.
units.rightText: And Jehovah hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued after the children of Israel: for the children of Israel went out with a high hand.
leftNotes: 14:8 Or marching out boldly; literally marching out with an upraised hand

units.leftText: The Egyptians— all Pharaoh’s horses and chariots, horsemen and troops— pursued the Israelites and overtook them as they camped by the sea near Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon.
units.rightText: And the Egyptians pursued after them, all the horses and chariots of Pharaoh, and his horsemen, and his army, and overtook them encamping by the sea, beside Pi-hahiroth, before Baal-zephon.

units.leftText: As Pharaoh approached, the Israelites looked up and saw the Egyptians marching after them, and they were terrified and cried out to the LORD.
units.rightText: And when Pharaoh drew nigh, the children of Israel lifted up their eyes, and, behold, the Egyptians were marching after them; and they were sore afraid: and the children of Israel cried out unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: They said to Moses, “Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you brought us into the wilderness to die? What have you done to us by bringing us out of Egypt?
units.rightText: And they said unto Moses, Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness? wherefore hast thou dealt thus with us, to bring us forth out of Egypt?

units.leftText: Did we not say to you in Egypt, ‘Leave us alone so that we may serve the Egyptians’? For it would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.”
units.rightText: Is not this the word that we spake unto thee in Egypt, saying, Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians? For it were better for us to serve the Egyptians, than that we should die in the wilderness.

units.leftText: But Moses told the people, “Do not be afraid. Stand firm and you will see the LORD’s salvation, which He will accomplish for you today; for the Egyptians you see today, you will never see again.
units.rightText: And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of Jehovah, which he will work for you to-day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to-day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.

units.leftText: The LORD will fight for you; you need only to be still.” Parting the Red Sea
units.rightText: Jehovah will fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Why are you crying out to Me? Tell the Israelites to go forward.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Wherefore criest thou unto me? speak unto the children of Israel, that they go forward.

units.leftText: And as for you, lift up your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it, so that the Israelites can go through the sea on dry ground.
units.rightText: And lift thou up thy rod, and stretch out thy hand over the sea, and divide it: and the children of Israel shall go into the midst of the sea on dry ground.

units.leftText: And I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians so that they will go in after them. Then I will gain honor by means of Pharaoh and all his army and chariots and horsemen.
units.rightText: And I, behold, I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians, and they shall go in after them: and I will get me honor upon Pharaoh, and upon all his host, upon his chariots, and upon his horsemen.

units.leftText: The Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I am honored through Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen.”
units.rightText: And the Egyptians shall know that I am Jehovah, when I have gotten me honor upon Pharaoh, upon his chariots, and upon his horsemen.

units.leftText: And the angel of God, who had gone before the camp of Israel, withdrew and went behind them. The pillar of cloud also moved from before them and stood behind them,
units.rightText: And the angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, removed and went behind them; and the pillar of cloud removed from before them, and stood behind them:
leftNotes: 14:19 Or Angel

units.leftText: so that it came between the camps of Egypt and Israel. The cloud was there in the darkness, but it lit up the night. So all night long neither camp went near the other.
units.rightText: and it came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel; and there was the cloud and the darkness, yet gave it light by night: and the one came not near the other all the night.
leftNotes: 14:20 LXX and the night passed

units.leftText: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and all that night the LORD drove back the sea with a strong east wind that turned it into dry land. So the waters were divided,
units.rightText: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and Jehovah caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all the night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.

units.leftText: and the Israelites went through the sea on dry ground, with walls of water on their right and on their left.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.

units.leftText: And the Egyptians chased after them— all Pharaoh’s horses, chariots, and horsemen— and followed them into the sea.
units.rightText: And the Egyptians pursued, and went in after them into the midst of the sea, all Pharaoh’s horses, his chariots, and his horsemen.

units.leftText: At morning watch, however, the LORD looked down on the army of the Egyptians from the pillar of fire and cloud, and He threw their camp into confusion.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the morning watch, that Jehovah looked forth upon the host of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and of cloud, and discomfited the host of the Egyptians.

units.leftText: He caused their chariot wheels to wobble, so that they had difficulty driving. “Let us flee from the Israelites,” said the Egyptians, “for the LORD is fighting for them against Egypt!”
units.rightText: And he took off their chariot wheels, and they drove them heavily; so that the Egyptians said, Let us flee from the face of Israel; for Jehovah fighteth for them against the Egyptians.
leftNotes: 14:25 Or to swerve or to come off or to bind; see also SP, LXX, and Syriac.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the sea, so that the waters may flow back over the Egyptians and their chariots and horsemen.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Stretch out thy hand over the sea, that the waters may come again upon the Egyptians, upon their chariots, and upon their horsemen.

units.leftText: So Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and at daybreak the sea returned to its normal state. As the Egyptians were retreating, the LORD swept them into the sea.
units.rightText: And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to its strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it; and Jehovah overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.

units.leftText: The waters flowed back and covered the chariots and horsemen — the entire army of Pharaoh that had chased the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them survived.
units.rightText: And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, even all the host of Pharaoh that went in after them into the sea; there remained not so much as one of them.

units.leftText: But the Israelites had walked through the sea on dry ground, with walls of water on their right and on their left.
units.rightText: But the children of Israel walked upon dry land in the midst of the sea; and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.

units.leftText: That day the LORD saved Israel from the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the shore.
units.rightText: Thus Jehovah saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians; and Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea-shore.

units.leftText: When Israel saw the great power that the LORD had exercised over the Egyptians, the people feared the LORD and believed in Him and in His servant Moses.
units.rightText: And Israel saw the great work which Jehovah did upon the Egyptians, and the people feared Jehovah: and they believed in Jehovah, and in his servant Moses.

units.leftText: Then Moses and the Israelites sang this song to the LORD: “I will sing to the LORD, for He is highly exalted. The horse and rider He has thrown into the sea.
units.rightText: Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song unto Jehovah, and spake, saying, I will sing unto Jehovah, for he hath triumphed gloriously: The horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.

units.leftText: The LORD is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation. He is my God, and I will praise Him, my father’s God, and I will exalt Him.
units.rightText: Jehovah is my strength and song, And he is become my salvation: This is my God, and I will praise him; My father’s God, and I will exalt him.

units.leftText: The LORD is a warrior, the LORD is His name.
units.rightText: Jehovah is a man of war: Jehovah is his name.

units.leftText: Pharaoh’s chariots and army He has cast into the sea; the finest of his officers are drowned in the Red Sea.
units.rightText: Pharaoh’s chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea; And his chosen captains are sunk in the Red Sea.
leftNotes: 15:4 Or the Sea of Reeds; also in verse 22

units.leftText: The depths have covered them; they sank there like a stone.
units.rightText: The deeps cover them: They went down into the depths like a stone.

units.leftText: Your right hand, O LORD, is majestic in power; Your right hand, O LORD, has shattered the enemy.
units.rightText: Thy right hand, O Jehovah, is glorious in power, Thy right hand, O Jehovah, dasheth in pieces the enemy.

units.leftText: You overthrew Your adversaries by Your great majesty. You unleashed Your burning wrath; it consumed them like stubble.
units.rightText: And in the greatness of thine excellency thou overthrowest them that rise up against thee: Thou sendest forth thy wrath, it consumeth them as stubble.

units.leftText: At the blast of Your nostrils the waters piled up; like a wall the currents stood firm; the depths congealed in the heart of the sea.
units.rightText: And with the blast of thy nostrils the waters were piled up, The floods stood upright as a heap; The deeps were congealed in the heart of the sea.

units.leftText: The enemy declared, ‘I will pursue, I will overtake. I will divide the spoils; I will gorge myself on them. I will draw my sword; my hand will destroy them.’
units.rightText: The enemy said, I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoil; My desire shall be satisfied upon them; I will draw my sword, my hand shall destroy them.

units.leftText: But You blew with Your breath, and the sea covered them. They sank like lead in the mighty waters.
units.rightText: Thou didst blow with thy wind, the sea covered them: They sank as lead in the mighty waters.

units.leftText: Who among the gods is like You, O LORD? Who is like You — majestic in holiness, revered with praises, performing wonders?
units.rightText: Who is like unto thee, O Jehovah, among the gods? Who is like thee, glorious in holiness, Fearful in praises, doing wonders?

units.leftText: You stretched out Your right hand, and the earth swallowed them up.
units.rightText: Thou stretchedst out thy right hand, The earth swallowed them.

units.leftText: With loving devotion You will lead the people You have redeemed; with Your strength You will guide them to Your holy dwelling.
units.rightText: Thou in thy lovingkindness hast led the people that thou hast redeemed: Thou hast guided them in thy strength to thy holy habitation.
leftNotes: 15:13 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: The nations will hear and tremble; anguish will grip the dwellers of Philistia.
units.rightText: The peoples have heard, they tremble: Pangs have taken hold on the inhabitants of Philistia.

units.leftText: Then the chiefs of Edom will be dismayed; trembling will seize the leaders of Moab; those who dwell in Canaan will melt away,
units.rightText: Then were the chiefs of Edom dismayed; The mighty men of Moab, trembling taketh hold upon them: All the inhabitants of Canaan are melted away.

units.leftText: and terror and dread will fall on them. By the power of Your arm they will be as still as a stone until Your people pass by, O LORD, until the people You have bought pass by.
units.rightText: Terror and dread falleth upon them; By the greatness of thine arm they are as still as a stone; Till thy people pass over, O Jehovah, Till the people pass over that thou hast purchased.

units.leftText: You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of Your inheritance — the place, O LORD, You have prepared for Your dwelling, the sanctuary, O Lord, Your hands have established.
units.rightText: Thou wilt bring them in, and plant them in the mountain of thine inheritance, The place, O Jehovah, which thou hast made for thee to dwell in, The sanctuary, O Lord, which thy hands have established.

units.leftText: The LORD will reign forever and ever!”
units.rightText: Jehovah shall reign for ever and ever.

units.leftText: For when Pharaoh’s horses, chariots, and horsemen went into the sea, the LORD brought the waters of the sea back over them. But the Israelites walked through the sea on dry ground.
units.rightText: For the horses of Pharaoh went in with his chariots and with his horsemen into the sea, and Jehovah brought back the waters of the sea upon them; but the children of Israel walked on dry land in the midst of the sea.

units.leftText: Then Miriam the prophetess, Aaron’s sister, took a tambourine in her hand, and all the women followed her with tambourines and dancing.
units.rightText: And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances.

units.leftText: And Miriam sang back to them: “Sing to the LORD, for He is highly exalted; the horse and rider He has thrown into the sea.” The Waters of Marah
units.rightText: And Miriam answered them, Sing ye to Jehovah, for he hath triumphed gloriously; The horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.

units.leftText: Then Moses led Israel from the Red Sea, and they went out into the Desert of Shur. For three days they walked in the desert without finding water.
units.rightText: And Moses led Israel onward from the Red Sea, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water.

units.leftText: And when they came to Marah, they could not drink the water there because it was bitter. (That is why it was named Marah.)
units.rightText: And when they came to Marah, they could not drink of the waters of Marah, for they were bitter: therefore the name of it was called Marah.
leftNotes: 15:23 Marah means bitter.

units.leftText: So the people grumbled against Moses, saying, “What are we to drink?”
units.rightText: And the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink?

units.leftText: And Moses cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a log. And when he cast it into the waters, they were sweetened.
units.rightText: And he cried unto Jehovah; and Jehovah showed him a tree, and he cast it into the waters, and the waters were made sweet. There he made for them a statute and an ordinance, and there he proved them;

units.leftText: saying, “If you will listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God, and do what is right in His eyes, and pay attention to His commands, and keep all His statutes, then I will not bring on you any of the diseases I inflicted on the Egyptians. For I am the LORD who heals you.”
units.rightText: and he said, If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of Jehovah thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his eyes, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of the diseases upon thee, which I have put upon the Egyptians: for I am Jehovah that healeth thee.

units.leftText: Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there by the waters.
units.rightText: And they came to Elim, where were twelve springs of water, and threescore and ten palm-trees: and they encamped there by the waters.

units.leftText: On the fifteenth day of the second month after they had left the land of Egypt, the whole congregation of Israel set out from Elim and came to the Desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai.
units.rightText: And they took their journey from Elim, and all the congregation of the children of Israel came unto the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after their departing out of the land of Egypt.
leftNotes: 16:1 The geographical name Sin is related to Sinai and should not be mistaken for the English word sin.

units.leftText: And there in the desert the whole congregation of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron.
units.rightText: And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron in the wilderness:

units.leftText: “If only we had died by the LORD’s hand in the land of Egypt!” they said. “There we sat by pots of meat and ate our fill of bread, but you have brought us into this desert to starve this whole assembly to death!”
units.rightText: and the children of Israel said unto them, Would that we had died by the hand of Jehovah in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh-pots, when we did eat bread to the full; for ye have brought us forth into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Behold, I will rain down bread from heaven for you. Each day the people are to go out and gather enough for that day. In this way I will test whether or not they will follow My instructions.
units.rightText: Then said Jehovah unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a day’s portion every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or not.

units.leftText: Then on the sixth day, when they prepare what they bring in, it will be twice as much as they gather on the other days.”
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass on the sixth day, that they shall prepare that which they bring in, and it shall be twice as much as they gather daily.

units.leftText: So Moses and Aaron said to all the Israelites, “This evening you will know that it was the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt,
units.rightText: And Moses and Aaron said unto all the children of Israel, At even, then ye shall know that Jehovah hath brought you out from the land of Egypt;

units.leftText: and in the morning you will see the LORD’s glory, because He has heard your grumbling against Him. For who are we, that you should grumble against us?”
units.rightText: and in the morning, then ye shall see the glory of Jehovah; for that he heareth your murmurings against Jehovah: and what are we, that ye murmur against us?

units.leftText: And Moses added, “The LORD will give you meat to eat this evening and bread to fill you in the morning, for He has heard your grumbling against Him. Who are we? Your grumblings are not against us but against the LORD.”
units.rightText: And Moses said, This shall be, when Jehovah shall give you in the evening flesh to eat, and in the morning bread to the full; for that Jehovah heareth your murmurings which ye murmur against him: and what are we? your murmurings are not against us, but against Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then Moses said to Aaron, “Tell the whole congregation of Israel, ‘Come before the LORD, for He has heard your grumbling.’”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Aaron, Say unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, Come near before Jehovah; for he hath heard your murmurings.

units.leftText: And as Aaron was speaking to the whole congregation of Israel, they looked toward the desert, and there in a cloud the glory of the LORD appeared.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as Aaron spake unto the whole congregation of the children of Israel, that they looked toward the wilderness, and, behold, the glory of Jehovah appeared in the cloud.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “I have heard the grumbling of the Israelites. Tell them, ‘At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be filled with bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.’”
units.rightText: I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel: speak unto them, saying, At even ye shall eat flesh, and in the morning ye shall be filled with bread: and ye shall know that I am Jehovah your God.
leftNotes: 16:12 Hebrew Between the two evenings

units.leftText: That evening quail came and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at even, that the quails came up, and covered the camp: and in the morning the dew lay round about the camp.

units.leftText: When the layer of dew had evaporated, there were thin flakes on the desert floor, as fine as frost on the ground.
units.rightText: And when the dew that lay was gone up, behold, upon the face of the wilderness a small round thing, small as the hoar-frost on the ground.

units.leftText: When the Israelites saw it, they asked one another, “What is it?” For they did not know what it was.
units.rightText: And when the children of Israel saw it, they said one to another, What is it? for they knew not what it was. And Moses said unto them, It is the bread which Jehovah hath given you to eat.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Each one is to gather as much as he needs. You may take an omer for each person in your tent.’”
units.rightText: This is the thing which Jehovah hath commanded, Gather ye of it every man according to his eating; an omer a head, according to the number of your persons, shall ye take it, every man for them that are in his tent.
leftNotes: 16:16 An omer is approximately 2 dry quarts or 2.2 liters; also in verses 18, 32, 33, and 36.

units.leftText: So the Israelites did this. Some gathered more, and some less.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel did so, and gathered some more, some less.

units.leftText: When they measured it by the omer, he who gathered much had no excess, and he who gathered little had no shortfall. Each one gathered as much as he needed to eat.
units.rightText: And when they measured it with an omer, he that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack; they gathered every man according to his eating.
leftNotes: 16:18 Cited in 2 Corinthians 8:15|2CO 8:15*

units.leftText: Then Moses said to them, “No one may keep any of it until morning.”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto them, Let no man leave of it till the morning.

units.leftText: But they did not listen to Moses; some people left part of it until morning, and it became infested with maggots and began to smell. So Moses was angry with them.
units.rightText: Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and became foul: and Moses was wroth with them.

units.leftText: Every morning each one gathered as much as was needed, and when the sun grew hot, it melted away. The Sabbath Observed (Genesis 2:1–3|GEN 2:1-3*; Hebrews 4:1–11|HEB 4:1-11*)
units.rightText: And they gathered it morning by morning, every man according to his eating: and when the sun waxed hot, it melted.

units.leftText: On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much food — two omers per person — and all the leaders of the congregation came and reported this to Moses.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, that on the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for each one: and all the rulers of the congregation came and told Moses.
leftNotes: 16:22 2 omers is approximately 4 dry quarts or 4.4 liters per person.

units.leftText: He told them, “This is what the LORD has said: ‘Tomorrow is to be a day of complete rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. So bake what you want to bake, and boil what you want to boil. Then set aside whatever remains and keep it until morning.’”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, This is that which Jehovah hath spoken, To-morrow is a solemn rest, a holy sabbath unto Jehovah: bake that which ye will bake, and boil that which ye will boil; and all that remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.

units.leftText: So they set it aside until morning as Moses had commanded, and it did not smell or contain any maggots.
units.rightText: And they laid it up till the morning, as Moses bade: and it did not become foul, neither was there any worm therein.

units.leftText: “Eat it today,” Moses said, “because today is a Sabbath to the LORD. Today you will not find anything in the field.
units.rightText: And Moses said, Eat that to-day; for to-day is a sabbath unto Jehovah: to-day ye shall not find it in the field.

units.leftText: For six days you may gather, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, it will not be there.”
units.rightText: Six days ye shall gather it; but on the seventh day is the sabbath, in it there shall be none.

units.leftText: Yet on the seventh day some of the people went out to gather, but they did not find anything.
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the seventh day, that there went out some of the people to gather, and they found none.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “How long will you refuse to keep My commandments and instructions?
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, How long refuse ye to keep my commandments and my laws?

units.leftText: Understand that the LORD has given you the Sabbath; that is why on the sixth day He will give you bread for two days. On the seventh day, everyone must stay where he is; no one may leave his place.”
units.rightText: See, for that Jehovah hath given you the sabbath, therefore he giveth you on the sixth day the bread of two days; abide ye every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.

units.leftText: So the people rested on the seventh day. The Jar of Manna
units.rightText: So the people rested on the seventh day.

units.leftText: Now the house of Israel called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.
units.rightText: And the house of Israel called the name thereof Manna: and it was like coriander seed, white; and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey.
leftNotes: 16:31 Manna sounds like the Hebrew for What is it? (see verse 15).

units.leftText: Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Keep an omer of manna for the generations to come, so that they may see the bread I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.’”
units.rightText: And Moses said, This is the thing which Jehovah hath commanded, Let an omerful of it be kept throughout your generations, that they may see the bread wherewith I fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you forth from the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: So Moses told Aaron, “Take a jar and fill it with an omer of manna. Then place it before the LORD to be preserved for the generations to come.”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Aaron, Take a pot, and put an omerful of manna therein, and lay it up before Jehovah, to be kept throughout your generations.

units.leftText: And Aaron placed it in front of the Testimony, to be preserved just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
units.rightText: As Jehovah commanded Moses, so Aaron laid it up before the Testimony, to be kept.
leftNotes: 16:34 The Testimony refers to the stone tablets in the ark of the covenant inscribed with the Ten Commandments.

units.leftText: The Israelites ate manna forty years, until they came to a land where they could settle; they ate manna until they reached the border of Canaan.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel did eat the manna forty years, until they came to a land inhabited; they did eat the manna, until they came unto the borders of the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: (Now an omer is a tenth of an ephah.)
units.rightText: Now an omer is the tenth part of an ephah.
leftNotes: 16:36 An ephah was a dry measure having the capacity of about 20 dry quarts or 22 liters.

units.leftText: Then the whole congregation of Israel left the Desert of Sin, moving from place to place as the LORD commanded. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.
units.rightText: And all the congregation of the children of Israel journeyed from the wilderness of Sin, by their journeys, according to the commandment of Jehovah, and encamped in Rephidim: and there was no water for the people to drink.
leftNotes: 17:1 The geographical name Sin is related to Sinai and should not be mistaken for the English word sin.

units.leftText: So the people contended with Moses, “Give us water to drink.” “Why do you contend with me?” Moses replied. “Why do you test the LORD?”
units.rightText: Wherefore the people strove with Moses, and said, Give us water that we may drink. And Moses said unto them, Why strive ye with me? wherefore do ye tempt Jehovah?

units.leftText: But the people thirsted for water there, and they grumbled against Moses: “Why have you brought us out of Egypt — to make us and our children and livestock die of thirst?”
units.rightText: And the people thirsted there for water; and the people murmured against Moses, and said, Wherefore hast thou brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst?

units.leftText: Then Moses cried out to the LORD, “What should I do with these people? A little more and they will stone me!”
units.rightText: And Moses cried unto Jehovah, saying, What shall I do unto this people? they are almost ready to stone me.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Moses, “Walk on ahead of the people and take some of the elders of Israel with you. Take along in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Pass on before the people, and take with thee of the elders of Israel; and thy rod, wherewith thou smotest the river, take in thy hand, and go.

units.leftText: Behold, I will stand there before you by the rock at Horeb. And when you strike the rock, water will come out of it for the people to drink.”
units.rightText: Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink. And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.
leftNotes: 17:6 Horeb is another name for Sinai.

units.leftText: He named the place Massah and Meribah because the Israelites quarreled, and because they tested the LORD, saying, “Is the LORD among us or not?” The Defeat of the Amalekites
units.rightText: And he called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the striving of the children of Israel, and because they tempted Jehovah, saying, Is Jehovah among us, or not?
leftNotes: 17:7 Massah means testing.
17:7 Meribah means quarreling.

units.leftText: After this, the Amalekites came and attacked the Israelites at Rephidim.
units.rightText: Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim.

units.leftText: So Moses said to Joshua, “Choose some of our men and go out to fight the Amalekites. Tomorrow I will stand on the hilltop with the staff of God in my hand.”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Joshua, Choose us out men, and go out, fight with Amalek: to-morrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the rod of God in my hand.

units.leftText: Joshua did as Moses had instructed him and fought against the Amalekites, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
units.rightText: So Joshua did as Moses had said to him, and fought with Amalek: and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.

units.leftText: As long as Moses held up his hands, Israel prevailed; but when he lowered them, Amalek prevailed.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed; and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.

units.leftText: When Moses’ hands grew heavy, they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Then Aaron and Hur held his hands up, one on each side, so that his hands remained steady until the sun went down.
units.rightText: But Moses’ hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.

units.leftText: So Joshua overwhelmed Amalek and his army with the sword.
units.rightText: And Joshua discomfited Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Write this on a scroll as a reminder and recite it to Joshua, because I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven.”
units.rightText: and Jehovah said unto Moses, Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: that I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.

units.leftText: And Moses built an altar and named it The LORD Is My Banner.
units.rightText: And Moses built an altar, and called the name of it Jehovah-nissi;
leftNotes: 17:15 Hebrew YHWH Nissi

units.leftText: “Indeed,” he said, “a hand was lifted up toward the throne of the LORD. The LORD will war against Amalek from generation to generation.”
units.rightText: and he said, Jehovah hath sworn: Jehovah will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.

units.leftText: Now Moses’ father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, heard about all that God had done for Moses and His people Israel, and how the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
units.rightText: Now Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses’ father-in-law, heard of all that God had done for Moses, and for Israel his people, how that Jehovah had brought Israel out of Egypt.
leftNotes: 18:1 Moses’ father-in-law Jethro was also called Reuel; see Exodus 2:18|EXO 2:18*.

units.leftText: After Moses had sent back his wife Zipporah, his father-in-law Jethro had received her,
units.rightText: And Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took Zipporah, Moses’ wife, after he had sent her away,

units.leftText: along with her two sons. One son was named Gershom, for Moses had said, “I have been a foreigner in a foreign land.”
units.rightText: and her two sons; of whom the name of the one was Gershom; for he said, I have been a sojourner in a foreign land:
leftNotes: 18:3 Gershom sounds like the Hebrew for sojourner.

units.leftText: The other son was named Eliezer, for Moses had said, “The God of my father was my helper and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.”
units.rightText: and the name of the other was Eliezer; for he said, The God of my father was my help, and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.
leftNotes: 18:4 Eliezer means God is my helper.

units.leftText: Moses’ father-in-law Jethro, along with Moses’ wife and sons, came to him in the desert, where he was encamped at the mountain of God.
units.rightText: And Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, came with his sons and his wife unto Moses into the wilderness where he was encamped, at the mount of God:

units.leftText: He sent word to Moses, “I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you with your wife and her two sons.”
units.rightText: and he said unto Moses, I, thy father-in-law Jethro, am come unto thee, and thy wife, and her two sons with her.

units.leftText: So Moses went out to meet his father-in-law and bowed down and kissed him. They greeted each other and went into the tent.
units.rightText: And Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, and did obeisance, and kissed him: and they asked each other of their welfare; and they came into the tent.

units.leftText: Then Moses recounted to his father-in-law all that the LORD had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel’s sake, all the hardships they had encountered along the way, and how the LORD had delivered them.
units.rightText: And Moses told his father-in-law all that Jehovah had done unto Pharaoh and to the Egyptians for Israel’s sake, all the travail that had come upon them by the way, and how Jehovah delivered them.

units.leftText: And Jethro rejoiced over all the good things the LORD had done for Israel, whom He had rescued from the hand of the Egyptians.
units.rightText: And Jethro rejoiced for all the goodness which Jehovah had done to Israel, in that he had delivered them out of the hand of the Egyptians.

units.leftText: Jethro declared, “Blessed be the LORD, who has delivered you from the hand of the Egyptians and of Pharaoh, and who has delivered the people from the hand of the Egyptians.
units.rightText: And Jethro said, Blessed be Jehovah, who hath delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of Pharaoh; who hath delivered the people from under the hand of the Egyptians.

units.leftText: Now I know that the LORD is greater than all other gods, for He did this when they treated Israel with arrogance.”
units.rightText: Now I know that Jehovah is greater than all gods; yea, in the thing wherein they dealt proudly against them.

units.leftText: Then Moses’ father-in-law Jethro brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God, and Aaron came with all the elders of Israel to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law in the presence of God. Jethro Advises Moses (Deuteronomy 1:9–18|DEU 1:9-18*)
units.rightText: And Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took a burnt-offering and sacrifices for God: and Aaron came, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before God.

units.leftText: The next day Moses took his seat to judge the people, and they stood around him from morning until evening.
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the morrow, that Moses sat to judge the people: and the people stood about Moses from the morning unto the evening.

units.leftText: When his father-in-law saw all that Moses was doing for the people, he asked, “What is this that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone as judge, with all the people standing around you from morning till evening?”
units.rightText: And when Moses’ father-in-law saw all that he did to the people, he said, What is this thing that thou doest to the people? why sittest thou thyself alone, and all the people stand about thee from morning unto even?

units.leftText: “Because the people come to me to inquire of God,” Moses replied.
units.rightText: And Moses said unto his father-in-law, Because the people come unto me to inquire of God:

units.leftText: “Whenever they have a dispute, it is brought to me to judge between one man and another, and I make known to them the statutes and laws of God.”
units.rightText: when they have a matter, they come unto me; and I judge between a man and his neighbor, and I make them know the statutes of God, and his laws.

units.leftText: But Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “What you are doing is not good.
units.rightText: And Moses’ father-in-law said unto him, The thing that thou doest is not good.

units.leftText: Surely you and these people with you will wear yourselves out, because the task is too heavy for you. You cannot handle it alone.
units.rightText: Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for the thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.

units.leftText: Now listen to me; I will give you some advice, and may God be with you. You must be the people’s representative before God and bring their causes to Him.
units.rightText: Hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel, and God be with thee: be thou for the people to God-ward, and bring thou the causes unto God:

units.leftText: Teach them the statutes and laws, and show them the way to live and the work they must do.
units.rightText: and thou shalt teach them the statutes and the laws, and shalt show them the way wherein they must walk, and the work that they must do.

units.leftText: Furthermore, select capable men from among the people — God-fearing, trustworthy men who are averse to dishonest gain. Appoint them over the people as leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens.
units.rightText: Moreover thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating unjust gain; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens:

units.leftText: Have these men judge the people at all times. Then they can bring you any major issue, but all minor cases they can judge on their own, so that your load may be lightened as they share it with you.
units.rightText: and let them judge the people at all seasons: and it shall be, that every great matter they shall bring unto thee, but every small matter they shall judge themselves: so shall it be easier for thyself, and they shall bear the burden with thee.
