units.leftText: If you follow this advice and God so directs you, then you will be able to endure, and all these people can go home in peace.”
units.rightText: If thou shalt do this thing, and God command thee so, then thou shalt be able to endure, and all this people also shall go to their place in peace.

units.leftText: Moses listened to his father-in-law and did everything he said.
units.rightText: So Moses hearkened to the voice of his father-in-law, and did all that he had said.

units.leftText: So Moses chose capable men from all Israel and made them heads over the people as leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens.
units.rightText: And Moses chose able men out of all Israel, and made them heads over the people, rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.

units.leftText: And they judged the people at all times; they would bring the difficult cases to Moses, but any minor issue they would judge themselves.
units.rightText: And they judged the people at all seasons: the hard causes they brought unto Moses, but every small matter they judged themselves.

units.leftText: Then Moses sent his father-in-law on his way, and Jethro returned to his own land.
units.rightText: And Moses let his father-in-law depart; and he went his way into his own land.

units.leftText: In the third month, on the same day of the month that the Israelites had left the land of Egypt, they came to the Wilderness of Sinai.
units.rightText: In the third month after the children of Israel were gone forth out of the land of Egypt, the same day came they into the wilderness of Sinai.
leftNotes: 19:1 Hebrew In the third month, on the same day; that is, two months after leaving Egypt; see Numbers 33:3|NUM 33:3*.

units.leftText: After they had set out from Rephidim, they entered the Wilderness of Sinai, and Israel camped there in front of the mountain.
units.rightText: And when they were departed from Rephidim, and were come to the wilderness of Sinai, they encamped in the wilderness; and there Israel encamped before the mount.

units.leftText: Then Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain, “This is what you are to tell the house of Jacob and explain to the sons of Israel:
units.rightText: And Moses went up unto God, and Jehovah called unto him out of the mountain, saying, Thus shalt thou say to the house of Jacob, and tell the children of Israel:

units.leftText: ‘You have seen for yourselves what I did to Egypt, and how I carried you on eagles’ wings and brought you to Myself.
units.rightText: Ye have seen what I did unto the Egyptians, and how I bare you on eagles’ wings, and brought you unto myself.

units.leftText: Now if you will indeed obey My voice and keep My covenant, you will be My treasured possession out of all the nations — for the whole earth is Mine.
units.rightText: Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be mine own possession from among all peoples: for all the earth is mine:

units.leftText: And unto Me you shall be a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.’ These are the words that you are to speak to the Israelites.”
units.rightText: and ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.

units.leftText: So Moses went back and summoned the elders of the people and set before them all these words that the LORD had commanded him.
units.rightText: And Moses came and called for the elders of the people, and set before them all these words which Jehovah commanded him.

units.leftText: And all the people answered together, “We will do everything that the LORD has spoken.” So Moses brought their words back to the LORD.
units.rightText: And all the people answered together, and said, All that Jehovah hath spoken we will do. And Moses reported the words of the people unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Behold, I will come to you in a dense cloud, so that the people will hear when I speak with you, and they will always put their trust in you.” And Moses relayed to the LORD what the people had said.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Lo, I come unto thee in a thick cloud, that the people may hear when I speak with thee, and may also believe thee for ever. And Moses told the words of the people unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow. They must wash their clothes
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Go unto the people, and sanctify them to-day and to-morrow, and let them wash their garments,

units.leftText: and be prepared by the third day, for on the third day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.
units.rightText: and be ready against the third day; for the third day Jehovah will come down in the sight of all the people upon mount Sinai.

units.leftText: And you are to set up a boundary for the people around the mountain and tell them, ‘Be careful not to go up on the mountain or touch its base. Whoever touches the mountain shall surely be put to death.
units.rightText: And thou shalt set bounds unto the people round about, saying, Take heed to yourselves, that ye go not up into the mount, or touch the border of it: whosoever toucheth the mount shall be surely put to death:

units.leftText: No hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned or shot with arrows — whether man or beast, he must not live.’ Only when the ram’s horn sounds a long blast may they approach the mountain. ”
units.rightText: no hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned, or shot through; whether it be beast or man, he shall not live: when the trumpet soundeth long, they shall come up to the mount.
leftNotes: 19:13 Cited in Hebrews 12:20|HEB 12:20*
19:13 Or may they go up on the mountain

units.leftText: When Moses came down from the mountain to the people, he consecrated them, and they washed their clothes.
units.rightText: And Moses went down from the mount unto the people, and sanctified the people; and they washed their garments.

units.leftText: “Be prepared for the third day,” he said to the people. “Do not draw near to a woman.” The LORD Visits Sinai
units.rightText: And he said unto the people, Be ready against the third day: come not near a woman.

units.leftText: On the third day, when morning came, there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud was upon the mountain, and a very loud blast of the ram’s horn went out, so that all the people in the camp trembled.
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the third day, when it was morning, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud upon the mount, and the voice of a trumpet exceeding loud; and all the people that were in the camp trembled.

units.leftText: Then Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet with God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
units.rightText: And Moses brought forth the people out of the camp to meet God; and they stood at the nether part of the mount.

units.leftText: Mount Sinai was completely enveloped in smoke, because the LORD had descended on it in fire. And the smoke rose like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked violently.
units.rightText: And mount Sinai, the whole of it, smoked, because Jehovah descended upon it in fire; and the smoke thereof ascended as the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mount quaked greatly.

units.leftText: And as the sound of the ram’s horn grew louder and louder, Moses spoke and God answered him in the thunder.
units.rightText: And when the voice of the trumpet waxed louder and louder, Moses spake, and God answered him by a voice.

units.leftText: The LORD descended to the top of Mount Sinai and called Moses to the summit. So Moses went up,
units.rightText: And Jehovah came down upon mount Sinai, to the top of the mount: and Jehovah called Moses to the top of the mount; and Moses went up.

units.leftText: and the LORD said to him, “Go down and warn the people not to break through to see the LORD, lest many of them perish.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Go down, charge the people, lest they break through unto Jehovah to gaze, and many of them perish.

units.leftText: Even the priests who approach the LORD must consecrate themselves, or the LORD will break out against them.”
units.rightText: And let the priests also, that come near to Jehovah, sanctify themselves, lest Jehovah break forth upon them.

units.leftText: But Moses said to the LORD, “The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, for You solemnly warned us, ‘Put a boundary around the mountain and set it apart as holy.’”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Jehovah, The people cannot come up to mount Sinai: for thou didst charge us, saying, Set bounds about the mount, and sanctify it.

units.leftText: And the LORD replied, “Go down and bring Aaron with you. But the priests and the people must not break through to come up to the LORD, or He will break out against them.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto him, Go, get thee down; and thou shalt come up, thou, and Aaron with thee: but let not the priests and the people break through to come up unto Jehovah, lest he break forth upon them.

units.leftText: So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.
units.rightText: So Moses went down unto the people, and told them.

units.leftText: And God spoke all these words:
units.rightText: And God spake all these words, saying,

units.leftText: “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
units.rightText: I am Jehovah thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

units.leftText: You shall have no other gods before Me.
units.rightText: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.
leftNotes: 20:3 Or besides Me

units.leftText: You shall not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not make unto thee a graven image, nor any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:

units.leftText: You shall not bow down to them or worship them; for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on their children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me,
units.rightText: thou shalt not bow down thyself unto them, nor serve them; for I Jehovah thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, upon the third and upon the fourth generation of them that hate me,

units.leftText: but showing loving devotion to a thousand generations of those who love Me and keep My commandments.
units.rightText: and showing lovingkindness unto thousands of them that love me and keep my commandments.
leftNotes: 20:6 Or to thousands

units.leftText: You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain, for the LORD will not leave anyone unpunished who takes His name in vain.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not take the name of Jehovah thy God in vain; for Jehovah will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.

units.leftText: Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy.
units.rightText: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.

units.leftText: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,
units.rightText: Six days shalt thou labor, and do all thy work;

units.leftText: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God, on which you must not do any work— neither you, nor your son or daughter, nor your manservant or maidservant or livestock, nor the foreigner within your gates.
units.rightText: but the seventh day is a sabbath unto Jehovah thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy man-servant, nor thy maid-servant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:

units.leftText: For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth and the sea and all that is in them, but on the seventh day He rested. Therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and set it apart as holy.
units.rightText: for in six days Jehovah made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: wherefore Jehovah blessed the sabbath day, and hallowed it.

units.leftText: Honor your father and mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
units.rightText: Honor thy father and thy mother, that thy days may be long in the land which Jehovah thy God giveth thee.
leftNotes: 20:12 Cited in Matthew 15:4|MAT 15:4*, Matthew 19:19, Mark 7:10, Luke 18:20, and Ephesians 6:2–3

units.leftText: You shall not murder.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not kill.
leftNotes: 20:13 Cited in Matthew 5:21|MAT 5:21*, Matthew 19:18, Mark 10:19, Luke 18:20, Romans 13:9, and James 2:11

units.leftText: You shall not commit adultery.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not commit adultery.
leftNotes: 20:14 Cited in Matthew 5:27|MAT 5:27*, Matthew 19:18, Mark 10:19, Luke 18:20, Romans 13:9, and James 2:11

units.leftText: You shall not steal.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not steal.
leftNotes: 20:15 Cited in Matthew 19:18|MAT 19:18*, Mark 10:19, Luke 18:20, and Romans 13:9

units.leftText: You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbor.
leftNotes: 20:16 Cited in Matthew 19:18|MAT 19:18*, Mark 10:19, and Luke 18:20

units.leftText: You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, or his manservant or maidservant, or his ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.” Moses Comforts the People (Deuteronomy 5:22–33|DEU 5:22-33*; Hebrews 12:18–29|HEB 12:18-29*)
units.rightText: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbor’s wife, nor his man-servant, nor his maid-servant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor anything that is thy neighbor’s.
leftNotes: 20:17 Cited in Romans 7:7|ROM 7:7* and Romans 13:9

units.leftText: When all the people witnessed the thunder and lightning, the sounding of the ram’s horn, and the mountain enveloped in smoke, they trembled and stood at a distance.
units.rightText: And all the people perceived the thunderings, and the lightnings, and the voice of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking: and when the people saw it, they trembled, and stood afar off.

units.leftText: “Speak to us yourself and we will listen,” they said to Moses. “But do not let God speak to us, or we will die.”
units.rightText: And they said unto Moses, Speak thou with us, and we will hear; but let not God speak with us, lest we die.

units.leftText: “Do not be afraid,” Moses replied. “For God has come to test you, so that the fear of Him may be before you, to keep you from sinning.”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto the people, Fear not: for God is come to prove you, and that his fear may be before you, that ye sin not.

units.leftText: And the people stood at a distance as Moses approached the thick darkness where God was. Idolatry Forbidden (1 Corinthians 10:14–22|1CO 10:14-22*)
units.rightText: And the people stood afar off, and Moses drew near unto the thick darkness where God was.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “This is what you are to tell the Israelites: ‘You have seen for yourselves that I have spoken to you from heaven.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Thus thou shalt say unto the children of Israel, Ye yourselves have seen that I have talked with you from heaven.

units.leftText: You are not to make any gods alongside Me; you are not to make for yourselves gods of silver or gold.
units.rightText: Ye shall not make other gods with me; gods of silver, or gods of gold, ye shall not make unto you.

units.leftText: You are to make for Me an altar of earth, and sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and peace offerings, your sheep and goats and cattle. In every place where I cause My name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
units.rightText: An altar of earth thou shalt make unto me, and shalt sacrifice thereon thy burnt-offerings, and thy peace-offerings, thy sheep, and thine oxen: in every place where I record my name I will come unto thee and I will bless thee.

units.leftText: Now if you make an altar of stones for Me, you must not build it with stones shaped by tools; for if you use a chisel on it, you will defile it.
units.rightText: And if thou make me an altar of stone, thou shalt not build it of hewn stones; for if thou lift up thy tool upon it, thou hast polluted it.

units.leftText: And you must not go up to My altar on steps, lest your nakedness be exposed on it.’[’’]
units.rightText: Neither shalt thou go up by steps unto mine altar, that thy nakedness be not uncovered thereon.

units.leftText: “These are the ordinances that you are to set before them:
units.rightText: Now these are the ordinances which thou shalt set before them.

units.leftText: If you buy a Hebrew servant, he is to serve you for six years. But in the seventh year, he shall go free without paying anything.
units.rightText: If thou buy a Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve: and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing.

units.leftText: If he arrived alone, he is to leave alone; if he arrived with a wife, she is to leave with him.
units.rightText: If he come in by himself, he shall go out by himself: if he be married, then his wife shall go out with him.

units.leftText: If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the woman and her children shall belong to her master, and only the man shall go free.
units.rightText: If his master give him a wife and she bear him sons or daughters; the wife and her children shall be her master’s, and he shall go out by himself.

units.leftText: But if the servant declares, ‘I love my master and my wife and children; I do not want to go free,’
units.rightText: But if the servant shall plainly say, I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free:

units.leftText: then his master is to bring him before the judges. And he shall take him to the door or doorpost and pierce his ear with an awl. Then he shall serve his master for life.
units.rightText: then his master shall bring him unto God, and shall bring him to the door, or unto the door-post; and his master shall bore his ear through with an awl; and he shall serve him for ever.
leftNotes: 21:6 Or before God

units.leftText: And if a man sells his daughter as a servant, she is not to go free as the menservants do.
units.rightText: And if a man sell his daughter to be a maid-servant, she shall not go out as the men-servants do.

units.leftText: If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master who had designated her for himself, he must allow her to be redeemed. He has no right to sell her to foreigners, since he has broken faith with her.
units.rightText: If she please not her master, who hath espoused her to himself, then shall he let her be redeemed: to sell her unto a foreign people he shall have no power, seeing he hath dealt deceitfully with her.
leftNotes: 21:8 Or so that he does not designate her for himself

units.leftText: And if he chooses her for his son, he must deal with her as with a daughter.
units.rightText: And if he espouse her unto his son, he shall deal with her after the manner of daughters.

units.leftText: If he takes another wife, he must not reduce the food, clothing, or marital rights of his first wife.
units.rightText: If he take him another wife; her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage, shall he not diminish.

units.leftText: If, however, he does not provide her with these three things, she is free to go without monetary payment. Personal Injury Laws
units.rightText: And if he do not these three things unto her, then shall she go out for nothing, without money.

units.leftText: Whoever strikes and kills a man must surely be put to death.
units.rightText: He that smiteth a man, so that he dieth, shall surely be put to death.

units.leftText: If, however, he did not lie in wait, but God allowed it to happen, then I will appoint for you a place where he may flee.
units.rightText: And if a man lie not in wait, but God deliver him into his hand; then I will appoint thee a place whither he shall flee.

units.leftText: But if a man schemes and acts willfully against his neighbor to kill him, you must take him away from My altar to be put to death.
units.rightText: And if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbor, to slay him with guile; thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die.

units.leftText: Whoever strikes his father or mother must surely be put to death.
units.rightText: And he that smiteth his father, or his mother, shall be surely put to death.

units.leftText: Whoever kidnaps another man must be put to death, whether he sells him or the man is found in his possession.
units.rightText: And he that stealeth a man, and selleth him, or if he be found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.

units.leftText: Anyone who curses his father or mother must surely be put to death.
units.rightText: And he that curseth his father or his mother, shall surely be put to death.
leftNotes: 21:17 Or dishonors or reviles
21:17 Cited in Matthew 15:4|MAT 15:4* and Mark 7:10

units.leftText: If men are quarreling and one strikes the other with a stone or a fist, and he does not die but is confined to bed,
units.rightText: And if men contend, and one smite the other with a stone, or with his fist, and he die not, but keep his bed;

units.leftText: then the one who struck him shall go unpunished, as long as the other can get up and walk around outside with his staff. Nevertheless, he must compensate the man for his lost work and see that he is completely healed.
units.rightText: if he rise again, and walk abroad upon his staff, then shall he that smote him be quit: only he shall pay for the loss of his time, and shall cause him to be thoroughly healed.

units.leftText: If a man strikes his manservant or maidservant with a rod, and the servant dies by his hand, he shall surely be punished.
units.rightText: And if a man smite his servant, or his maid, with a rod, and he die under his hand; he shall surely be punished.

units.leftText: However, if the servant gets up after a day or two, the owner shall not be punished, since the servant is his property.
units.rightText: Notwithstanding, if he continue a day or two, he shall not be punished: for he is his money.

units.leftText: If men who are fighting strike a pregnant woman and her child is born prematurely, but there is no further injury, he shall surely be fined as the woman’s husband demands and as the court allows.
units.rightText: And if men strive together, and hurt a woman with child, so that her fruit depart, and yet no harm follow; he shall be surely fined, according as the woman’s husband shall lay upon him; and he shall pay as the judges determine.
leftNotes: 21:22 Literally and her children come out

units.leftText: But if a serious injury results, then you must require a life for a life —
units.rightText: But if any harm follow, then thou shalt give life for life,

units.leftText: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
units.rightText: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
leftNotes: 21:24 Cited in Matthew 5:38|MAT 5:38*

units.leftText: burn for burn, wound for wound, and stripe for stripe.
units.rightText: burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.

units.leftText: If a man strikes and blinds the eye of his manservant or maidservant, he must let the servant go free as compensation for the eye.
units.rightText: And if a man smite the eye of his servant, or the eye of his maid, and destroy it; he shall let him go free for his eye’s sake.

units.leftText: And if he knocks out the tooth of his manservant or maidservant, he must let the servant go free as compensation for the tooth.
units.rightText: And if he smite out his man-servant’s tooth, or his maid-servant’s tooth, he shall let him go free for his tooth’s sake.

units.leftText: If an ox gores a man or woman to death, the ox must surely be stoned, and its meat must not be eaten. But the owner of the ox shall not be held responsible.
units.rightText: And if an ox gore a man or a woman to death, the ox shall be surely stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the ox shall be quit.
leftNotes: 21:28 Or a bull; also in verses 29–36

units.leftText: But if the ox has a habit of goring, and its owner has been warned yet does not restrain it, and it kills a man or woman, then the ox must be stoned and its owner must also be put to death.
units.rightText: But if the ox was wont to gore in time past, and it hath been testified to its owner, and he hath not kept it in, but it hath killed a man or a woman; the ox shall be stoned, and its owner also shall be put to death.

units.leftText: If payment is demanded of him instead, he may redeem his life by paying the full amount demanded of him.
units.rightText: If there be laid on him a ransom, then he shall give for the redemption of his life whatsoever is laid upon him.

units.leftText: If the ox gores a son or a daughter, it shall be done to him according to the same rule.
units.rightText: Whether it have gored a son, or have gored a daughter, according to this judgment shall it be done unto him.

units.leftText: If the ox gores a manservant or maidservant, the owner must pay thirty shekels of silver to the master of that servant, and the ox must be stoned.
units.rightText: If the ox gore a man-servant or a maid-servant, there shall be given unto their master thirty shekels of silver, and the ox shall be stoned.
leftNotes: 21:32 30 shekels is approximately 12 ounces or 342 grams of silver.

units.leftText: If a man opens or digs a pit and fails to cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
units.rightText: And if a man shall open a pit, or if a man shall dig a pit and not cover it, and an ox or an ass fall therein,

units.leftText: the owner of the pit shall make restitution; he must pay its owner, and the dead animal will be his.
units.rightText: the owner of the pit shall make it good; he shall give money unto the owner thereof, and the dead beast shall be his.

units.leftText: If a man’s ox injures his neighbor’s ox and it dies, they must sell the live one and divide the proceeds; they also must divide the dead animal.
units.rightText: And if one man’s ox hurt another’s, so that it dieth, then they shall sell the live ox, and divide the price of it; and the dead also they shall divide.

units.leftText: But if it was known that the ox had a habit of goring, yet its owner failed to restrain it, he shall pay full compensation, ox for ox, and the dead animal will be his.[’’]
units.rightText: Or if it be known that the ox was wont to gore in time past, and its owner hath not kept it in; he shall surely pay ox for ox, and the dead beast shall be his own.

units.leftText: “If a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters or sells it, he must repay five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep.
units.rightText: If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall pay five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.
leftNotes: 22:1 Or a bull or a cow; also in verses 4, 9, and 10

units.leftText: If a thief is caught breaking in and is beaten to death, no one shall be guilty of bloodshed.
units.rightText: If the thief be found breaking in, and be smitten so that he dieth, there shall be no bloodguiltiness for him.

units.leftText: But if it happens after sunrise, there is guilt for his bloodshed.
units.rightText: If the sun be risen upon him, there shall be bloodguiltiness for him; he shall make restitution: if he have nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.

units.leftText: If what was stolen is actually found alive in his possession— whether ox or donkey or sheep— he must pay back double.
units.rightText: If the theft be found in his hand alive, whether it be ox, or ass, or sheep, he shall pay double.

units.leftText: If a man grazes his livestock in a field or vineyard and allows them to stray so that they graze in someone else’s field, he must make restitution from the best of his own field or vineyard.
units.rightText: If a man shall cause a field or vineyard to be eaten, and shall let his beast loose, and it feed in another man’s field; of the best of his own field, and of the best of his own vineyard, shall he make restitution.

units.leftText: If a fire breaks out and spreads to thornbushes so that it consumes stacked or standing grain, or the whole field, the one who started the fire must make full restitution.
units.rightText: If fire break out, and catch in thorns, so that the shocks of grain, or the standing grain, or the field are consumed; he that kindled the fire shall surely make restitution.

units.leftText: If a man gives his neighbor money or goods for safekeeping and they are stolen from the neighbor’s house, the thief, if caught, must pay back double.
units.rightText: If a man shall deliver unto his neighbor money or stuff to keep, and it be stolen out of the man’s house; if the thief be found, he shall pay double.

units.leftText: If the thief is not found, the owner of the house must appear before the judges to determine whether he has taken his neighbor’s property.
units.rightText: If the thief be not found, then the master of the house shall come near unto God, to see whether he have not put his hand unto his neighbor’s goods.
leftNotes: 22:8 Or before God; also in verse 9

units.leftText: In all cases of illegal possession of an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any lost item that someone claims, ‘This is mine,’ both parties shall bring their cases before the judges. The one whom the judges find guilty must pay back double to his neighbor.
units.rightText: For every matter of trespass, whether it be for ox, for ass, for sheep, for raiment, or for any manner of lost thing, whereof one saith, This is it, the cause of both parties shall come before God; he whom God shall condemn shall pay double unto his neighbor.
leftNotes: 22:9 Or whom God condemns

units.leftText: If a man gives a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any other animal to be cared for by his neighbor, but it dies or is injured or stolen while no one is watching,
units.rightText: If a man deliver unto his neighbor an ass, or an ox, or a sheep, or any beast, to keep; and it die, or be hurt, or driven away, no man seeing it:

units.leftText: an oath before the LORD shall be made between the parties to determine whether or not the man has taken his neighbor’s property. The owner must accept the oath and require no restitution.
units.rightText: the oath of Jehovah shall be between them both, whether he hath not put his hand unto his neighbor’s goods; and the owner thereof shall accept it, and he shall not make restitution.

units.leftText: But if the animal was actually stolen from the neighbor, he must make restitution to the owner.
units.rightText: But if it be stolen from him, he shall make restitution unto the owner thereof.

units.leftText: If the animal was torn to pieces, he shall bring it as evidence; he need not make restitution for the torn carcass.
units.rightText: If it be torn in pieces, let him bring it for witness: he shall not make good that which was torn.

units.leftText: If a man borrows an animal from his neighbor and it is injured or dies while its owner is not present, he must make full restitution.
units.rightText: And if a man borrow aught of his neighbor, and it be hurt, or die, the owner thereof not being with it, he shall surely make restitution.

units.leftText: If the owner was present, no restitution is required. If the animal was rented, the fee covers the loss. Laws of Social Responsibility
units.rightText: If the owner thereof be with it, he shall not make it good: if it be a hired thing, it came for its hire.

units.leftText: If a man seduces a virgin who is not pledged in marriage and sleeps with her, he must pay the full dowry for her to be his wife.
units.rightText: And if a man entice a virgin that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall surely pay a dowry for her to be his wife.

units.leftText: If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, the man still must pay an amount comparable to the bridal price of a virgin.
units.rightText: If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.

units.leftText: You must not allow a sorceress to live.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not suffer a sorceress to live.

units.leftText: Whoever lies with an animal must surely be put to death.
units.rightText: Whosoever lieth with a beast shall surely be put to death.

units.leftText: If anyone sacrifices to any god other than the LORD alone, he must be set apart for destruction.
units.rightText: He that sacrificeth unto any god, save unto Jehovah only, shall be utterly destroyed.
leftNotes: 22:20 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering.

units.leftText: You must not exploit or oppress a foreign resident, for you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And a sojourner shalt thou not wrong, neither shalt thou oppress him: for ye were sojourners in the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: You must not mistreat any widow or orphan.
units.rightText: Ye shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child.

units.leftText: If you do mistreat them, and they cry out to Me in distress, I will surely hear their cry.
units.rightText: If thou afflict them at all, and they cry at all unto me, I will surely hear their cry;

units.leftText: My anger will be kindled, and I will kill you with the sword; then your wives will become widows and your children will be fatherless.
units.rightText: and my wrath shall wax hot, and I will kill you with the sword; and your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.

units.leftText: If you lend money to one of My people among you who is poor, you must not act as a creditor to him; you are not to charge him interest.
units.rightText: If thou lend money to any of my people with thee that is poor, thou shalt not be to him as a creditor; neither shall ye lay upon him interest.

units.leftText: If you take your neighbor’s cloak as collateral, return it to him by sunset,
units.rightText: If thou at all take thy neighbor’s garment to pledge, thou shalt restore it unto him before the sun goeth down:

units.leftText: because his cloak is the only covering he has for his body. What else will he sleep in? And if he cries out to Me, I will hear, for I am compassionate.
units.rightText: for that is his only covering, it is his garment for his skin: wherein shall he sleep? and it shall come to pass, when he crieth unto me, that I will hear; for I am gracious.

units.leftText: You must not blaspheme God or curse the ruler of your people.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not revile God, nor curse a ruler of thy people.
leftNotes: 22:28 LXX or speak evil about the ruler of your people; cited in Acts 23:5|ACT 23:5*

units.leftText: You must not hold back offerings from your granaries or vats. You are to give Me the firstborn of your sons.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not delay to offer of thy harvest, and of the outflow of thy presses. The first-born of thy sons shalt thou give unto me.

units.leftText: You shall do likewise with your cattle and your sheep. Let them stay with their mothers for seven days, but on the eighth day you are to give them to Me.
units.rightText: Likewise shalt thou do with thine oxen, and with thy sheep: seven days it shall be with its dam; on the eighth day thou shalt give it me.

units.leftText: You are to be My holy people. You must not eat the meat of a mauled animal found in the field; you are to throw it to the dogs.[’’]
units.rightText: And ye shall be holy men unto me: therefore ye shall not eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field; ye shall cast it to the dogs.

units.leftText: “You shall not spread a false report. Do not join the wicked by being a malicious witness.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not take up a false report: put not thy hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness.

units.leftText: You shall not follow the crowd in wrongdoing. When you testify in a lawsuit, do not pervert justice by siding with the crowd.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; neither shalt thou speak in a cause to turn aside after a multitude to wrest justice:

units.leftText: And do not show favoritism to a poor man in his lawsuit.
units.rightText: neither shalt thou favor a poor man in his cause.

units.leftText: If you encounter your enemy’s stray ox or donkey, you must return it to him.
units.rightText: If thou meet thine enemy’s ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again.

units.leftText: If you see the donkey of one who hates you fallen under its load, do not leave it there; you must help him with it.
units.rightText: If thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, thou shalt forbear to leave him, thou shalt surely release it with him.

units.leftText: You shall not deny justice to the poor in their lawsuits.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not wrest the justice due to thy poor in his cause.

units.leftText: Stay far away from a false accusation. Do not kill the innocent or the just, for I will not acquit the guilty.
units.rightText: Keep thee far from a false matter; and the innocent and righteous slay thou not: for I will not justify the wicked.

units.leftText: Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the righteous.
units.rightText: And thou shalt take no bribe: for a bribe blindeth them that have sight, and perverteth the words of the righteous.

units.leftText: Do not oppress a foreign resident, since you yourselves know how it feels to be foreigners; for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt. Sabbath Laws (Leviticus 25:1–7|LEV 25:1-7*; Deuteronomy 15:1–6|DEU 15:1-6*)
units.rightText: And a sojourner shalt thou not oppress: for ye know the heart of a sojourner, seeing ye were sojourners in the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: For six years you are to sow your land and gather its produce,
units.rightText: And six years thou shalt sow thy land, and shalt gather in the increase thereof:

units.leftText: but in the seventh year you must let it rest and lie fallow, so that the poor among your people may eat from the field and the wild animals may consume what they leave. Do the same with your vineyard and olive grove.
units.rightText: but the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie fallow; that the poor of thy people may eat: and what they leave the beast of the field shall eat. In like manner thou shalt deal with thy vineyard, and with thy oliveyard.

units.leftText: For six days you are to do your work, but on the seventh day you must cease, so that your ox and your donkey may rest and the son of your maidservant may be refreshed, as well as the foreign resident.
units.rightText: Six days thou shalt do thy work, and on the seventh day thou shalt rest; that thine ox and thine ass may have rest, and the son of thy handmaid, and the sojourner, may be refreshed.

units.leftText: Pay close attention to everything I have said to you. You must not invoke the names of other gods; they must not be heard on your lips. The Three Feasts of Pilgrimage (Leviticus 23:1–3|LEV 23:1-3*)
units.rightText: And in all things that I have said unto you take ye heed: and make no mention of the name of other gods, neither let it be heard out of thy mouth.

units.leftText: Three times a year you are to celebrate a feast to Me.
units.rightText: Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year.

units.leftText: You are to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread as I commanded you: At the appointed time in the month of Abib you are to eat unleavened bread for seven days, because that was the month you came out of Egypt. No one may appear before Me empty-handed.
units.rightText: The feast of unleavened bread shalt thou keep: seven days thou shalt eat unleavened bread, as I commanded thee, at the time appointed in the month Abib (for in it thou camest out from Egypt); and none shall appear before me empty:
leftNotes: 23:15 That is, the seven-day period after the Passover during which no leaven may be eaten; see Exodus 12:14–20|EXO 12:14-20*.
23:15 Abib was the first month of the ancient Hebrew lunar calendar, usually occurring within the months of March and April.

units.leftText: You are also to keep the Feast of Harvest with the firstfruits of the produce from what you sow in the field. And keep the Feast of Ingathering at the end of the year, when you gather your produce from the field.
units.rightText: and the feast of harvest, the first-fruits of thy labors, which thou sowest in the field: and the feast of ingathering, at the end of the year, when thou gatherest in thy labors out of the field.
leftNotes: 23:16 That is, Shavuot, the late spring feast of pilgrimage to Jerusalem; it is also known as the Feast of Weeks(see Exodus 34:22|EXO 34:22*) or the Feast of Pentecost(see Acts 2:1|ACT 2:1*).
23:16 That is, Sukkot, the autumn feast of pilgrimage to Jerusalem; it is later called the Feast of Tabernacles (or Booths or Shelters).

units.leftText: Three times a year all your males are to appear before the Lord GOD.
units.rightText: Three times in the year all thy males shall appear before the Lord Jehovah.

units.leftText: You must not offer the blood of My sacrifices with anything leavened, nor may the fat of My feast remain until morning.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread; neither shall the fat of my feast remain all night until the morning.

units.leftText: Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God. You must not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk. God’s Angel to Lead (Deuteronomy 7:12–26|DEU 7:12-26*)
units.rightText: The first of the first-fruits of thy ground thou shalt bring into the house of Jehovah thy God. Thou shalt not boil a kid in its mother’s milk.

units.leftText: Behold, I am sending an angel before you to protect you along the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared.
units.rightText: Behold, I send an angel before thee, to keep thee by the way, and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared.

units.leftText: Pay attention to him and listen to his voice; do not defy him, for he will not forgive rebellion, since My Name is in him.
units.rightText: Take ye heed before him, and hearken unto his voice; provoke him not; for he will not pardon your transgression: for my name is in him.

units.leftText: But if you will listen carefully to his voice and do everything I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and a foe to your foes.
units.rightText: But if thou shalt indeed hearken unto his voice, and do all that I speak; then I will be an enemy unto thine enemies, and an adversary unto thine adversaries.

units.leftText: For My angel will go before you and bring you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will annihilate them.
units.rightText: For mine angel shall go before thee, and bring thee in unto the Amorite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Canaanite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite: and I will cut them off.

units.leftText: You must not bow down to their gods or serve them or follow their practices. Instead, you are to demolish them and smash their sacred stones to pieces.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor do after their works; but thou shalt utterly overthrow them, and break in pieces their pillars.

units.leftText: So you shall serve the LORD your God, and He will bless your bread and your water. And I will take away sickness from among you.
units.rightText: And ye shall serve Jehovah your God, and he will bless thy bread, and thy water; and I will take sickness away from the midst of thee.
leftNotes: 23:25 LXX and Vulgate I will bless

units.leftText: No woman in your land will miscarry or be barren; I will fulfill the number of your days.
units.rightText: There shall none cast her young, nor be barren, in thy land: the number of thy days I will fulfil.

units.leftText: I will send My terror ahead of you and throw into confusion every nation you encounter. I will make all your enemies turn and run.
units.rightText: I will send my terror before thee, and will discomfit all the people to whom thou shalt come, and I will make all thine enemies turn their backs unto thee.

units.leftText: I will send the hornet before you to drive the Hivites and Canaanites and Hittites out of your way.
units.rightText: And I will send the hornet before thee, which shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before thee.

units.leftText: I will not drive them out before you in a single year; otherwise the land would become desolate and wild animals would multiply against you.
units.rightText: I will not drive them out from before thee in one year, lest the land become desolate, and the beasts of the field multiply against thee.

units.leftText: Little by little I will drive them out ahead of you, until you become fruitful and possess the land.
units.rightText: By little and little I will drive them out from before thee, until thou be increased, and inherit the land.

units.leftText: And I will establish your borders from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the desert to the Euphrates. For I will deliver the inhabitants into your hand, and you will drive them out before you.
units.rightText: And I will set thy border from the Red Sea even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness unto the River: for I will deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hand: and thou shalt drive them out before thee.
leftNotes: 23:31 Or the Sea of Reeds
23:31 Hebrew the River

units.leftText: You shall make no covenant with them or with their gods.
units.rightText: Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods.

units.leftText: They must not remain in your land, lest they cause you to sin against Me. For if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare to you.”
units.rightText: They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me; for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Come up to the LORD — you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of Israel’s elders — and you are to worship at a distance.
units.rightText: And he said unto Moses, Come up unto Jehovah, thou, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel; and worship ye afar off:

units.leftText: Moses alone shall approach the LORD, but the others must not come near. And the people may not go up with him.”
units.rightText: and Moses alone shall come near unto Jehovah; but they shall not come near; neither shall the people go up with him.

units.leftText: When Moses came and told the people all the words and ordinances of the LORD, they all responded with one voice: “All the words that the LORD has spoken, we will do.”
units.rightText: And Moses came and told the people all the words of Jehovah, and all the ordinances: and all the people answered with one voice, and said, All the words which Jehovah hath spoken will we do.

units.leftText: And Moses wrote down all the words of the LORD.
units.rightText: And Moses wrote all the words of Jehovah, and rose up early in the morning, and builded an altar under the mount, and twelve pillars, according to the twelve tribes of Israel.

units.leftText: Then he sent out some young men of Israel, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed young bulls as peace offerings to the LORD.
units.rightText: And he sent young men of the children of Israel, who offered burnt-offerings, and sacrificed peace-offerings of oxen unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: Moses took half of the blood and put it in bowls, and the other half he splattered on the altar.
units.rightText: And Moses took half of the blood, and put it in basins; and half of the blood he sprinkled on the altar.

units.leftText: Then he took the Book of the Covenant and read it to the people, who replied, “All that the LORD has spoken we will do, and we will be obedient.”
units.rightText: And he took the book of the covenant, and read in the audience of the people: and they said, All that Jehovah hath spoken will we do, and be obedient.

units.leftText: So Moses took the blood, splattered it on the people, and said, “This is the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you in accordance with all these words.”
units.rightText: And Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which Jehovah hath made with you concerning all these words.
leftNotes: 24:8 Cited in Hebrews 9:20|HEB 9:20*

units.leftText: Then Moses went up with Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel,
units.rightText: Then went up Moses, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel:

units.leftText: and they saw the God of Israel. Under His feet was a work like a pavement made of sapphire, as clear as the sky itself.
units.rightText: and they saw the God of Israel; and there was under his feet as it were a paved work of sapphire stone, and as it were the very heaven for clearness.

units.leftText: But God did not lay His hand on the nobles of Israel; they saw Him, and they ate and drank. Moses on the Mountain
units.rightText: And upon the nobles of the children of Israel he laid not his hand: and they beheld God, and did eat and drink.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Come up to Me on the mountain and stay here, so that I may give you the tablets of stone, with the law and commandments I have written for their instruction.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Come up to me into the mount, and be there: and I will give thee the tables of stone, and the law and the commandment, which I have written, that thou mayest teach them.

units.leftText: So Moses set out with Joshua his attendant and went up on the mountain of God.
units.rightText: And Moses rose up, and Joshua his minister: and Moses went up into the mount of God.

units.leftText: And he said to the elders, “Wait here for us until we return to you. Aaron and Hur are here with you. Whoever has a dispute can go to them.”
units.rightText: And he said unto the elders, Tarry ye here for us, until we come again unto you: and, behold, Aaron and Hur are with you: whosoever hath a cause, let him come near unto them.

units.leftText: When Moses went up on the mountain, the cloud covered it,
units.rightText: And Moses went up into the mount, and the cloud covered the mount.

units.leftText: and the glory of the LORD settled on Mount Sinai. For six days the cloud covered it, and on the seventh day the LORD called to Moses from within the cloud.
units.rightText: And the glory of Jehovah abode upon mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days: and the seventh day he called unto Moses out of the midst of the cloud.

units.leftText: And the sight of the glory of the LORD was like a consuming fire on the mountaintop in the eyes of the Israelites.
units.rightText: And the appearance of the glory of Jehovah was like devouring fire on the top of the mount in the eyes of the children of Israel.

units.leftText: Moses entered the cloud as he went up on the mountain, and he remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
units.rightText: And Moses entered into the midst of the cloud, and went up into the mount: and Moses was in the mount forty days and forty nights.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Tell the Israelites to bring Me an offering. You are to receive My offering from every man whose heart compels him.
units.rightText: Speak unto the children of Israel, that they take for me an offering: of every man whose heart maketh him willing ye shall take my offering.

units.leftText: This is the offering you are to accept from them: gold, silver, and bronze;
units.rightText: And this is the offering which ye shall take of them: gold, and silver, and brass,

units.leftText: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen and goat hair;
units.rightText: and blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats’ hair,

units.leftText: ram skins dyed red and fine leather; acacia wood;
units.rightText: and rams’ skins dyed red, and sealskins, and acacia wood,
leftNotes: 25:5 Possibly the hides of large aquatic mammals

units.leftText: olive oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
units.rightText: oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil, and for the sweet incense,

units.leftText: and onyx stones and gemstones to be mounted on the ephod and breastpiece.
units.rightText: onyx stones, and stones to be set, for the ephod, and for the breastplate.

units.leftText: And they are to make a sanctuary for Me, so that I may dwell among them.
units.rightText: And let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them.

units.leftText: You must make the tabernacle and design all its furnishings according to the pattern I show you. The Ark of the Covenant (Exodus 37:1–5|EXO 37:1-5*)
units.rightText: According to all that I show thee, the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all the furniture thereof, even so shall ye make it.

units.leftText: And they are to construct an ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
units.rightText: And they shall make an ark of acacia wood: two cubits and a half shall be the length thereof, and a cubit and a half the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof.
leftNotes: 25:10 The ark was approximately 3.75 feet long, 2.25 feet wide, and 2.25 feet high (114.3 centimeters long, 68.6 centimeters wide, and 68.6 centimeters high).

units.leftText: Overlay it with pure gold both inside and out, and make a gold molding around it.
units.rightText: And thou shalt overlay it with pure gold, within and without shalt thou overlay it, and shalt make upon it a crown of gold round about.

units.leftText: Cast four gold rings for it and fasten them to its four feet, two rings on one side and two on the other.
units.rightText: And thou shalt cast four rings of gold for it, and put them in the four feet thereof; and two rings shall be on the one side of it, and two rings on the other side of it.

units.leftText: And make poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make staves of acacia wood, and overlay them with gold.

units.leftText: Insert the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, in order to carry it.
units.rightText: And thou shalt put the staves into the rings on the sides of the ark, wherewith to bear the ark.

units.leftText: The poles are to remain in the rings of the ark; they must not be removed.
units.rightText: The staves shall be in the rings of the ark: they shall not be taken from it.

units.leftText: And place inside the ark the Testimony, which I will give you. The Mercy Seat (Exodus 37:6–9|EXO 37:6-9*)
units.rightText: And thou shalt put into the ark the testimony which I shall give thee.
leftNotes: 25:16 The Testimony refers to the stone tablets in the ark of the covenant inscribed with the Ten Commandments; also in verses 21 and 22.

units.leftText: And you are to construct a mercy seat of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make a mercy-seat of pure gold: two cubits and a half shall be the length thereof, and a cubit and a half the breadth thereof.
leftNotes: 25:17 Or an atonement cover; here and throughout Exodus
25:17 The mercy seat was approximately 3.75 feet long and 2.25 feet wide (114.3 centimeters long and 68.6 centimeters wide).

units.leftText: Make two cherubim of hammered gold at the ends of the mercy seat,
units.rightText: And thou shalt make two cherubim of gold; of beaten work shalt thou make them, at the two ends of the mercy-seat.

units.leftText: one cherub on one end and one on the other, all made from one piece of gold.
units.rightText: And make one cherub at the one end, and one cherub at the other end: of one piece with the mercy-seat shall ye make the cherubim on the two ends thereof.

units.leftText: And the cherubim are to have wings that spread upward, overshadowing the mercy seat. The cherubim are to face each other, looking toward the mercy seat.
units.rightText: And the cherubim shall spread out their wings on high, covering the mercy-seat with their wings, with their faces one to another; toward the mercy-seat shall the faces of the cherubim be.

units.leftText: Set the mercy seat atop the ark and put the Testimony that I will give you into the ark.
units.rightText: And thou shalt put the mercy-seat above upon the ark; and in the ark thou shalt put the testimony that I shall give thee.

units.leftText: And I will meet with you there above the mercy seat, between the two cherubim that are over the ark of the Testimony; I will speak with you about all that I command you regarding the Israelites. The Table of Showbread (Exodus 37:10–16|EXO 37:10-16*; Leviticus 24:5–9|LEV 24:5-9*)
units.rightText: And there I will meet with thee, and I will commune with thee from above the mercy-seat, from between the two cherubim which are upon the ark of the testimony, of all things which I will give thee in commandment unto the children of Israel.
leftNotes: 25:22 That is, the ark of the covenant

units.leftText: You are also to make a table of acacia wood two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make a table of acacia wood: two cubits shall be the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof.
leftNotes: 25:23 The table was approximately 3 feet long, 1.5 feet wide, and 2.25 feet high (91.4 centimeters long, 45.7 centimeters wide, and 68.6 centimeters high).

units.leftText: Overlay it with pure gold and make a gold molding around it.
units.rightText: And thou shalt overlay it with pure gold, and make thereto a crown of gold round about.

units.leftText: And make a rim around it a handbreadth wide and put a gold molding on the rim.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make unto it a border of a handbreadth round about; and thou shalt make a golden crown to the border thereof round about.
leftNotes: 25:25 A handbreadth is approximately 2.9 inches or 7.4 centimeters.

units.leftText: Make four gold rings for the table and fasten them to the four corners at its four legs.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make for it four rings of gold, and put the rings in the four corners that are on the four feet thereof.

units.leftText: The rings are to be close to the rim, to serve as holders for the poles used to carry the table.
units.rightText: Close by the border shall the rings be, for places for the staves to bear the table.

units.leftText: Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold, so that the table may be carried with them.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make the staves of acacia wood, and overlay them with gold, that the table may be borne with them.

units.leftText: You are also to make the plates and dishes, as well as the pitchers and bowls for pouring drink offerings. Make them out of pure gold.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make the dishes thereof, and the spoons thereof, and the flagons thereof, and the bowls thereof, wherewith to pour out: of pure gold shalt thou make them.

units.leftText: And place the Bread of the Presence on the table before Me at all times. The Lampstand (Exodus 37:17–24|EXO 37:17-24*; Numbers 8:1–4|NUM 8:1-4*)
units.rightText: And thou shalt set upon the table showbread before me alway.

units.leftText: Then you are to make a lampstand of pure, hammered gold. It shall be made of one piece, including its base and shaft, its cups, and its buds and petals.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make a candlestick of pure gold: of beaten work shall the candlestick be made, even its base, and its shaft; its cups, its knops, and its flowers, shall be of one piece with it:

units.leftText: Six branches are to extend from the sides of the lampstand — three on one side and three on the other.
units.rightText: and there shall be six branches going out of the sides thereof; three branches of the candlestick out of the one side thereof, and three branches of the candlestick out of the other side thereof:

units.leftText: There are to be three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the first branch, each with buds and petals, three on the next branch, and the same for all six branches that extend from the lampstand.
units.rightText: three cups made like almond-blossoms in one branch, a knop and a flower; and three cups made like almond-blossoms in the other branch, a knop and a flower: so for the six branches going out of the candlestick:

units.leftText: And on the lampstand there shall be four cups shaped like almond blossoms with buds and petals.
units.rightText: and in the candlestick four cups made like almond-blossoms, the knops thereof, and the flowers thereof;

units.leftText: For the six branches that extend from the lampstand, a bud must be under the first pair of branches, a bud under the second pair, and a bud under the third pair.
units.rightText: and a knop under two branches of one piece with it, and a knop under two branches of one piece with it, and a knop under two branches of one piece with it, for the six branches going out of the candlestick.

units.leftText: The buds and branches are to be all of one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.
units.rightText: Their knops and their branches shall be of one piece with it; the whole of it one beaten work of pure gold.

units.leftText: Make seven lamps and set them up on the lampstand so that they illuminate the area in front of it.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make the lamps thereof, seven: and they shall light the lamps thereof, to give light over against it.

units.leftText: The wick trimmers and their trays must be of pure gold.
units.rightText: And the snuffers thereof, and the snuffdishes thereof, shall be of pure gold.

units.leftText: The lampstand and all these utensils shall be made from a talent of pure gold.
units.rightText: Of a talent of pure gold shall it be made, with all these vessels.
leftNotes: 25:39 A talent is approximately 75.4 pounds or 34.2 kilograms of gold.

units.leftText: See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain. [’’]
units.rightText: And see that thou make them after their pattern, which hath been showed thee in the mount.
leftNotes: 25:40 Cited in Hebrews 8:5|HEB 8:5*

units.leftText: “You are to construct the tabernacle itself with ten curtains of finely spun linen, each with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and cherubim skillfully worked into them.
units.rightText: Moreover thou shalt make the tabernacle with ten curtains; of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, with cherubim the work of the skilful workman shalt thou make them.

units.leftText: Each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide — all curtains the same size.
units.rightText: The length of each curtain shall be eight and twenty cubits, and the breadth of each curtain four cubits: all the curtains shall have one measure.
leftNotes: 26:2 Each of the ten curtains was approximately 42 feet long and 6 feet wide (12.8 meters long and 1.8 meters wide).

units.leftText: Five of the curtains are to be joined together, and the other five joined as well.
units.rightText: Five curtains shall be coupled together one to another; and the other five curtains shall be coupled one to another.

units.leftText: Make loops of blue material on the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and do the same for the end curtain in the second set.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make loops of blue upon the edge of the one curtain from the selvedge in the coupling; and likewise shalt thou make in the edge of the curtain that is outmost in the second coupling.

units.leftText: Make fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the second set, so that the loops line up opposite one another.
units.rightText: Fifty loops shalt thou make in the one curtain, and fifty loops shalt thou make in the edge of the curtain that is in the second coupling; the loops shall be opposite one to another.

units.leftText: Make fifty gold clasps as well, and join the curtains together with the clasps, so that the tabernacle will be a unit. The Eleven Curtains of Goat Hair (Exodus 36:14–19|EXO 36:14-19*)
units.rightText: And thou shalt make fifty clasps of gold, and couple the curtains one to another with the clasps: and the tabernacle shall be one whole.

units.leftText: You are to make curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle — eleven curtains in all.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make curtains of goats’ hair for a tent over the tabernacle: eleven curtains shalt thou make them.

units.leftText: Each of the eleven curtains is to be the same size — thirty cubits long and four cubits wide.
units.rightText: The length of each curtain shall be thirty cubits, and the breadth of each curtain four cubits: the eleven curtains shall have one measure.
leftNotes: 26:8 Each of the eleven curtains was approximately 45 feet long and 6 feet wide (13.7 meters long and 1.8 meters wide).

units.leftText: Join five of the curtains into one set and the other six into another. Then fold the sixth curtain over double at the front of the tent.
units.rightText: And thou shalt couple five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves, and shalt double over the sixth curtain in the forefront of the tent.

units.leftText: Make fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and fifty loops along the edge of the corresponding curtain in the second set.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain that is outmost in the coupling, and fifty loops upon the edge of the curtain which is outmost in the second coupling.

units.leftText: Make fifty bronze clasps and put them through the loops to join the tent together as a unit.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make fifty clasps of brass, and put the clasps into the loops, and couple the tent together, that it may be one.

units.leftText: As for the overlap that remains of the tent curtains, the half curtain that is left over shall hang down over the back of the tabernacle.
units.rightText: And the overhanging part that remaineth of the curtains of the tent, the half curtain that remaineth, shall hang over the back of the tabernacle.

units.leftText: And the tent curtains will be a cubit longer on either side, and the excess will hang over the sides of the tabernacle to cover it.
units.rightText: And the cubit on the one side, and the cubit on the other side, of that which remaineth in the length of the curtains of the tent, shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle on this side and on that side, to cover it.
leftNotes: 26:13 A cubit is approximately 18 inches or 45.7 centimeters.

units.leftText: Also make a covering for the tent out of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather. The Frames and Bases (Exodus 36:20–34|EXO 36:20-34*)
units.rightText: And thou shalt make a covering for the tent of rams’ skins dyed red, and a covering of sealskins above.
leftNotes: 26:14 Possibly the hides of large aquatic mammals

units.leftText: You are to construct upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make the boards for the tabernacle of acacia wood, standing up.

units.leftText: Each frame is to be ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
units.rightText: Ten cubits shall be the length of a board, and a cubit and a half the breadth of each board.
leftNotes: 26:16 Each frame was approximately 15 feet long and 2.25 feet wide (4.6 meters long and 68.6 centimeters wide).

units.leftText: Two tenons must be connected to each other for each frame. Make all the frames of the tabernacle in this way.
units.rightText: Two tenons shall there be in each board, joined one to another: thus shalt thou make for all the boards of the tabernacle.
leftNotes: 26:17 That is, projecting pieces of wood made for insertion into another piece; similarly in verse 19.

units.leftText: Construct twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle,
units.rightText: And thou shalt make the boards for the tabernacle, twenty boards for the south side southward.

units.leftText: with forty silver bases under the twenty frames — two bases for each frame, one under each tenon.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make forty sockets of silver under the twenty boards; two sockets under one board for its two tenons, and two sockets under another board for its two tenons:

units.leftText: For the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, make twenty frames
units.rightText: and for the second side of the tabernacle, on the north side, twenty boards,

units.leftText: and forty silver bases — two bases under each frame.
units.rightText: and their forty sockets of silver; two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.

units.leftText: Make six frames for the rear of the tabernacle, the west side,
units.rightText: And for the hinder part of the tabernacle westward thou shalt make six boards.

units.leftText: and two frames for the two back corners of the tabernacle,
units.rightText: And two boards shalt thou make for the corners of the tabernacle in the hinder part.

units.leftText: coupled together from bottom to top and fitted into a single ring. These will serve as the two corners.
units.rightText: And they shall be double beneath, and in like manner they shall be entire unto the top thereof unto one ring: thus shall it be for them both; they shall be for the two corners.

units.leftText: So there are to be eight frames and sixteen silver bases — two under each frame.
units.rightText: And there shall be eight boards, and their sockets of silver, sixteen sockets; two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.

units.leftText: You are also to make five crossbars of acacia wood for the frames on one side of the tabernacle,
units.rightText: And thou shalt make bars of acacia wood: five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,

units.leftText: five for those on the other side, and five for those on the rear side of the tabernacle, to the west.
units.rightText: and five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the side of the tabernacle, for the hinder part westward.

units.leftText: The central crossbar in the middle of the frames shall extend from one end to the other.
units.rightText: And the middle bar in the midst of the boards shall pass through from end to end.

units.leftText: Overlay the frames with gold and make gold rings to hold the crossbars. Also overlay the crossbars with gold.
units.rightText: And thou shalt overlay the boards with gold, and make their rings of gold for places for the bars: and thou shalt overlay the bars with gold.

units.leftText: So you are to set up the tabernacle according to the pattern shown you on the mountain. The Veil (Exodus 36:35–36|EXO 36:35-36*)
units.rightText: And thou shalt rear up the tabernacle according to the fashion thereof which hath been showed thee in the mount.

units.leftText: Make a veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen, with cherubim skillfully worked into it.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make a veil of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen: with cherubim the work of the skilful workman shall it be made:

units.leftText: Hang it with gold hooks on four posts of acacia wood, overlaid with gold and standing on four silver bases.
units.rightText: and thou shalt hang it upon four pillars of acacia overlaid with gold; their hooks shall be of gold, upon four sockets of silver.

units.leftText: And hang the veil from the clasps and place the ark of the Testimony behind the veil. So the veil will separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.
units.rightText: And thou shalt hang up the veil under the clasps, and shalt bring in thither within the veil the ark of the testimony: and the veil shall separate unto you between the holy place and the most holy.
leftNotes: 26:33 That is, the ark of the covenant; also in verse 34
26:33 Or the Holy of Holies; also in verse 34

units.leftText: Put the mercy seat on the ark of the Testimony in the Most Holy Place.
units.rightText: And thou shalt put the mercy-seat upon the ark of the testimony in the most holy place.

units.leftText: And place the table outside the veil on the north side of the tabernacle, and put the lampstand opposite the table, on the south side. The Curtain for the Entrance (Exodus 36:37–38|EXO 36:37-38*)
units.rightText: And thou shalt set the table without the veil, and the candlestick over against the table on the side of the tabernacle toward the south: and thou shalt put the table on the north side.

units.leftText: For the entrance to the tent, you are to make a curtain embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make a screen for the door of the Tent, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, the work of the embroiderer.

units.leftText: Make five posts of acacia wood for the curtain, overlay them with gold, use hooks of gold, and cast five bronze bases for them.[’’]
units.rightText: And thou shalt make for the screen five pillars of acacia, and overlay them with gold: their hooks shall be of gold: and thou shalt cast five sockets of brass for them.

units.leftText: “You are to build an altar of acacia wood. The altar must be square, five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long, and five cubits broad; the altar shall be foursquare: and the height thereof shall be three cubits.
leftNotes: 27:1 The altar was approximately 7.5 feet in length and width, and 4.5 feet high (2.3 meters in length and width, and 1.4 meters high).

units.leftText: Make a horn on each of its four corners, so that the horns are of one piece, and overlay it with bronze.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make the horns of it upon the four corners thereof; the horns thereof shall be of one piece with it: and thou shalt overlay it with brass.

units.leftText: Make all its utensils of bronze — its pots for removing ashes, its shovels, its sprinkling bowls, its meat forks, and its firepans.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make its pots to take away its ashes, and its shovels, and its basins, and its flesh-hooks, and its firepans: all the vessels thereof thou shalt make of brass.

units.leftText: Construct for it a grate of bronze mesh, and make a bronze ring at each of the four corners of the mesh.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make for it a grating of network of brass: and upon the net shalt thou make four brazen rings in the four corners thereof.

units.leftText: Set the grate beneath the ledge of the altar, so that the mesh comes halfway up the altar.
units.rightText: And thou shalt put it under the ledge round the altar beneath, that the net may reach halfway up the altar.

units.leftText: Additionally, make poles of acacia wood for the altar and overlay them with bronze.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make staves for the altar, staves of acacia wood, and overlay them with brass.

units.leftText: The poles are to be inserted into the rings so that the poles are on two sides of the altar when it is carried.
units.rightText: And the staves thereof shall be put into the rings, and the staves shall be upon the two sides of the altar, in bearing it.

units.leftText: Construct the altar with boards so that it is hollow. It is to be made just as you were shown on the mountain. The Courtyard (Exodus 38:9–20|EXO 38:9-20*)
units.rightText: Hollow with planks shalt thou make it: as it hath been showed thee in the mount, so shall they make it.

units.leftText: You are also to make a courtyard for the tabernacle. On the south side of the courtyard make curtains of finely spun linen, a hundred cubits long on one side,
units.rightText: And thou shalt make the court of the tabernacle: for the south side southward there shall be hangings for the court of fine twined linen a hundred cubits long for one side:
leftNotes: 27:9 100 cubits is approximately 150 feet or 45.7 meters; also in verse 11.

units.leftText: with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands on the posts.
units.rightText: and the pillars thereof shall be twenty, and their sockets twenty, of brass; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets shall be of silver.

units.leftText: Likewise there are to be curtains on the north side, a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and with silver hooks and bands on the posts.
units.rightText: And likewise for the north side in length there shall be hangings a hundred cubits long, and the pillars thereof twenty, and their sockets twenty, of brass; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of silver.

units.leftText: The curtains on the west side of the courtyard shall be fifty cubits wide, with ten posts and ten bases.
units.rightText: And for the breadth of the court on the west side shall be hangings of fifty cubits; their pillars ten, and their sockets ten.
leftNotes: 27:12 50 cubits is approximately 75 feet or 22.9 meters; also in verse 13.

units.leftText: The east side of the courtyard, toward the sunrise, is to be fifty cubits wide.
units.rightText: And the breadth of the court on the east side eastward shall be fifty cubits.

units.leftText: Make the curtains on one side fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases,
units.rightText: The hangings for the one side of the gate shall be fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three.
leftNotes: 27:14 15 cubits is approximately 22.5 feet or 6.9 meters; also in verse 15.

units.leftText: and the curtains on the other side fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases.
units.rightText: And for the other side shall be hangings of fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three.

units.leftText: The gate of the courtyard shall be twenty cubits long, with a curtain embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen. It shall have four posts and four bases.
units.rightText: And for the gate of the court shall be a screen of twenty cubits, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, the work of the embroiderer; their pillars four, and their sockets four.
leftNotes: 27:16 20 cubits is approximately 30 feet or 9.1 meters.

units.leftText: All the posts around the courtyard shall have silver bands, silver hooks, and bronze bases.
units.rightText: All the pillars of the court round about shall be filleted with silver; their hooks of silver, and their sockets of brass.

units.leftText: The entire courtyard shall be a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide, with curtains of finely spun linen five cubits high, and with bronze bases.
