units.rightText: The length of the court shall be a hundred cubits, and the breadth fifty every where, and the height five cubits, of fine twined linen, and their sockets of brass.
leftNotes: 27:18 The courtyard was approximately 150 feet long and 75 feet wide (45.7 meters long and 22.9 meters wide).
27:18 5 cubits is approximately 7.5 feet or 2.3 meters.

units.leftText: All the utensils of the tabernacle for every use, including all its tent pegs and the tent pegs of the courtyard, shall be made of bronze. The Oil for the Lamps (Leviticus 24:1–4|LEV 24:1-4*)
units.rightText: All the instruments of the tabernacle in all the service thereof, and all the pins thereof, and all the pins of the court, shall be of brass.

units.leftText: And you are to command the Israelites to bring you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, to keep the lamps burning continually.
units.rightText: And thou shalt command the children of Israel, that they bring unto thee pure olive oil beaten for the light, to cause a lamp to burn continually.

units.leftText: In the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil that is in front of the Testimony, Aaron and his sons are to tend the lamps before the LORD from evening until morning. This is to be a permanent statute for the Israelites for the generations to come.[’’]
units.rightText: In the tent of meeting, without the veil which is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall keep it in order from evening to morning before Jehovah: it shall be a statute for ever throughout their generations on the behalf of the children of Israel.
leftNotes: 27:21 The Testimony refers to the stone tablets in the ark of the covenant inscribed with the Ten Commandments.

units.leftText: “Next, have your brother Aaron brought to you from among the Israelites, along with his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar, to serve Me as priests.
units.rightText: And bring thou near unto thee Aaron thy brother, and his sons with him, from among the children of Israel, that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office, even Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s sons.

units.leftText: Make holy garments for your brother Aaron, to give him glory and splendor.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make holy garments for Aaron thy brother, for glory and for beauty.

units.leftText: You are to instruct all the skilled craftsmen, whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom, to make garments for Aaron’s consecration, so that he may serve Me as priest.
units.rightText: And thou shalt speak unto all that are wise-hearted, whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom, that they make Aaron’s garments to sanctify him, that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office.

units.leftText: These are the garments that they shall make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a woven tunic, a turban, and a sash. They are to make these holy garments for your brother Aaron and his sons, so that they may serve Me as priests.
units.rightText: And these are the garments which they shall make: a breastplate, and an ephod, and a robe, and a coat of checker work, a mitre, and a girdle: and they shall make holy garments for Aaron thy brother, and his sons, that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office.

units.leftText: They shall use gold, along with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen. The Ephod (Exodus 39:1–7|EXO 39:1-7*)
units.rightText: And they shall take the gold, and the blue, and the purple, and the scarlet, and the fine linen.

units.leftText: They are to make the ephod of finely spun linen embroidered with gold, and with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
units.rightText: And they shall make the ephod of gold, of blue, and purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen, the work of the skilful workman.

units.leftText: It shall have two shoulder pieces attached at two of its corners, so it can be fastened.
units.rightText: It shall have two shoulder-pieces joined to the two ends thereof, that it may be joined together.

units.leftText: And the skillfully woven waistband of the ephod must be of one piece, of the same workmanship — with gold, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and with finely spun linen.
units.rightText: And the skilfully woven band, which is upon it, wherewith to gird it on, shall be like the work thereof and of the same piece; of gold, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen.

units.leftText: Take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel:
units.rightText: And thou shalt take two onyx stones, and grave on them the names of the children of Israel:

units.leftText: six of their names on one stone and the remaining six on the other, in the order of their birth.
units.rightText: six of their names on the one stone, and the names of the six that remain on the other stone, according to their birth.

units.leftText: Engrave the names of the sons of Israel on the two stones the way a gem cutter engraves a seal. Then mount the stones in gold filigree settings.
units.rightText: With the work of an engraver in stone, like the engravings of a signet, shalt thou engrave the two stones, according to the names of the children of Israel: thou shalt make them to be inclosed in settings of gold.

units.leftText: Fasten both stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel. Aaron is to bear their names on his two shoulders as a memorial before the LORD.
units.rightText: And thou shalt put the two stones upon the shoulder-pieces of the ephod, to be stones of memorial for the children of Israel: and Aaron shall bear their names before Jehovah upon his two shoulders for a memorial.

units.leftText: Fashion gold filigree settings
units.rightText: And thou shalt make settings of gold,

units.leftText: and two chains of pure gold, made of braided cord work; and attach these chains to the settings. The Breastpiece (Exodus 39:8–21|EXO 39:8-21*)
units.rightText: and two chains of pure gold; like cords shalt thou make them, of wreathen work: and thou shalt put the wreathen chains on the settings.

units.leftText: You are also to make a breastpiece of judgment with the same workmanship as the ephod. Construct it with gold, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and with finely spun linen.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make a breastplate of judgment, the work of the skilful workman; like the work of the ephod thou shalt make it; of gold, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, shalt thou make it.

units.leftText: It must be square when folded over double, a span long and a span wide.
units.rightText: Foursquare it shall be and double; a span shall be the length thereof, and a span the breadth thereof.
leftNotes: 28:16 The breastpiece, when folded over, was approximately 9 inches or 22.9 centimeters in both length and width.

units.leftText: And mount on it a setting of gemstones, four rows of stones: In the first row there shall be a ruby, a topaz, and an emerald;
units.rightText: And thou shalt set in it settings of stones, four rows of stones: a row of sardius, topaz, and carbuncle shall be the first row;
leftNotes: 28:17 The precise identification of some of these gemstones is uncertain.

units.leftText: in the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond;
units.rightText: and the second row an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond;

units.leftText: in the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
units.rightText: and the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;

units.leftText: and in the fourth row a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper.
units.rightText: and the fourth row a beryl, and an onyx, and a jasper: they shall be inclosed in gold in their settings.

units.leftText: The twelve stones are to correspond to the names of the sons of Israel, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
units.rightText: And the stones shall be according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names; like the engravings of a signet, every one according to his name, they shall be for the twelve tribes.

units.leftText: For the breastpiece, make braided chains like cords of pure gold.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make upon the breastplate chains like cords, of wreathen work of pure gold.

units.leftText: You are also to make two gold rings and fasten them to the two corners of the breastpiece.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make upon the breastplate two rings of gold, and shalt put the two rings on the two ends of the breastplate.

units.leftText: Then fasten the two gold chains to the two gold rings at the corners of the breastpiece,
units.rightText: And thou shalt put the two wreathen chains of gold in the two rings at the ends of the breastplate.

units.leftText: and fasten the other ends of the two chains to the two filigree settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
units.rightText: And the other two ends of the two wreathen chains thou shalt put on the two settings, and put them on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod in the forepart thereof.

units.leftText: Make two more gold rings and attach them to the other two corners of the breastpiece, on the inside edge next to the ephod.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make two rings of gold, and thou shalt put them upon the two ends of the breastplate, upon the edge thereof, which is toward the side of the ephod inward.

units.leftText: Make two additional gold rings and attach them to the bottom of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, on its front, near its seam just above its woven waistband.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make two rings of gold, and shalt put them on the two shoulder-pieces of the ephod underneath, in the forepart thereof, close by the coupling thereof, above the skilfully woven band of the ephod.

units.leftText: The rings of the breastpiece shall be tied to the rings of the ephod with a cord of blue yarn, so that the breastpiece is above the waistband of the ephod and does not swing out from the ephod.
units.rightText: And they shall bind the breastplate by the rings thereof unto the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue, that it may be upon the skilfully woven band of the ephod, and that the breastplate be not loosed from the ephod.

units.leftText: Whenever Aaron enters the Holy Place, he shall bear the names of the sons of Israel over his heart on the breastpiece of judgment, as a continual reminder before the LORD.
units.rightText: And Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the breastplate of judgment upon his heart, when he goeth in unto the holy place, for a memorial before Jehovah continually.

units.leftText: And place the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece of judgment, so that they will also be over Aaron’s heart whenever he comes before the LORD. Aaron will continually carry the judgment of the sons of Israel over his heart before the LORD. Additional Priestly Garments (Exodus 39:22–31|EXO 39:22-31*)
units.rightText: And thou shalt put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim; and they shall be upon Aaron’s heart, when he goeth in before Jehovah: and Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart before Jehovah continually.
leftNotes: 28:30 Literally Lights and Perfections

units.leftText: You are to make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth,
units.rightText: And thou shalt make the robe of the ephod all of blue.

units.leftText: with an opening at its top in the center. Around the opening shall be a woven collar with an opening like that of a garment, so that it will not tear.
units.rightText: And it shall have a hole for the head in the midst thereof: it shall have a binding of woven work round about the hole of it, as it were the hole of a coat of mail, that it be not rent.
leftNotes: 28:32 The meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain; possibly a coat of mail.

units.leftText: Make pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn all the way around the lower hem, with gold bells between them,
units.rightText: And upon the skirts of it thou shalt make pomegranates of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, round about the skirts thereof; and bells of gold between them round about:

units.leftText: alternating the gold bells and pomegranates around the lower hem of the robe.
units.rightText: a golden bell and a pomegranate, a golden bell and a pomegranate, upon the skirts of the robe round about.

units.leftText: Aaron must wear the robe whenever he ministers, and its sound will be heard when he enters or exits the sanctuary before the LORD, so that he will not die.
units.rightText: And it shall be upon Aaron to minister: and the sound thereof shall be heard when he goeth in unto the holy place before Jehovah, and when he cometh out, that he die not.

units.leftText: You are to make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it as on a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make a plate of pure gold, and grave upon it, like the engravings of a signet, HOLY TO JEHOVAH.
leftNotes: 28:36 That is, the LORD

units.leftText: Fasten to it a blue cord to mount it on the turban; it shall be on the front of the turban.
units.rightText: And thou shalt put it on a lace of blue, and it shall be upon the mitre; upon the forefront of the mitre it shall be.

units.leftText: And it will be worn on Aaron’s forehead, so that he may bear the iniquity of the holy things that the sons of Israel consecrate with regard to all their holy gifts. It shall always be on his forehead, so that they may be acceptable before the LORD.
units.rightText: And it shall be upon Aaron’s forehead, and Aaron shall bear the iniquity of the holy things, which the children of Israel shall hallow in all their holy gifts; and it shall be always upon his forehead, that they may be accepted before Jehovah.

units.leftText: You are to weave the tunic with fine linen, make the turban of fine linen, and fashion an embroidered sash.
units.rightText: And thou shalt weave the coat in checker work of fine linen, and thou shalt make a mitre of fine linen, and thou shalt make a girdle, the work of the embroiderer.

units.leftText: Make tunics, sashes, and headbands for Aaron’s sons, to give them glory and splendor.
units.rightText: And for Aaron’s sons thou shalt make coats, and thou shalt make for them girdles, and head-tires shalt thou make for them, for glory and for beauty.

units.leftText: After you put these garments on your brother Aaron and his sons, anoint them, ordain them, and consecrate them so that they may serve Me as priests.
units.rightText: And thou shalt put them upon Aaron thy brother, and upon his sons with him, and shalt anoint them, and consecrate them, and sanctify them, that they may minister unto me in the priest’s office.

units.leftText: Make linen undergarments to cover their bare flesh, extending from waist to thigh.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make them linen breeches to cover the flesh of their nakedness; from the loins even unto the thighs they shall reach:

units.leftText: Aaron and his sons must wear them whenever they enter the Tent of Meeting or approach the altar to minister in the Holy Place, so that they will not incur guilt and die. This is to be a permanent statute for Aaron and his descendants.[’’]
units.rightText: and they shall be upon Aaron, and upon his sons, when they go in unto the tent of meeting, or when they come near unto the altar to minister in the holy place; that they bear not iniquity, and die: it shall be a statute for ever unto him and unto his seed after him.

units.leftText: “Now this is what you are to do to consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests: Take a young bull and two rams without blemish,
units.rightText: And this is the thing that thou shalt do unto them to hallow them, to minister unto me in the priest’s office: take one young bullock and two rams without blemish,

units.leftText: along with unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil. Make them out of fine wheat flour,
units.rightText: and unleavened bread, and cakes unleavened mingled with oil, and wafers unleavened anointed with oil: of fine wheaten flour shalt thou make them.

units.leftText: put them in a basket, and present them in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.
units.rightText: And thou shalt put them into one basket, and bring them in the basket, with the bullock and the two rams.

units.leftText: Then present Aaron and his sons at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water.
units.rightText: And Aaron and his sons thou shalt bring unto the door of the tent of meeting, and shalt wash them with water.

units.leftText: Take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod itself, and the breastplate. Fasten the ephod on him with its woven waistband.
units.rightText: And thou shalt take the garments, and put upon Aaron the coat, and the robe of the ephod, and the ephod, and the breastplate, and gird him with the skilfully woven band of the ephod;

units.leftText: Put the turban on his head and attach the holy diadem to the turban.
units.rightText: and thou shalt set the mitre upon his head, and put the holy crown upon the mitre.

units.leftText: Then take the anointing oil and anoint him by pouring it on his head.
units.rightText: Then shalt thou take the anointing oil, and pour it upon his head, and anoint him.

units.leftText: Present his sons as well and clothe them with tunics.
units.rightText: And thou shalt bring his sons, and put coats upon them.

units.leftText: Wrap the sashes around Aaron and his sons and tie headbands on them. The priesthood shall be theirs by a permanent statute. In this way you are to ordain Aaron and his sons. The Order of the Sacrifices (Leviticus 8:22–36|LEV 8:22-36*)
units.rightText: And thou shalt gird them with girdles, Aaron and his sons, and bind head-tires on them: and they shall have the priesthood by a perpetual statute: and thou shalt consecrate Aaron and his sons.

units.leftText: You are to present the bull at the front of the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head.
units.rightText: And thou shalt bring the bullock before the tent of meeting: and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon the head of the bullock.

units.leftText: And you shall slaughter the bull before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: And thou shalt kill the bullock before Jehovah, at the door of the tent of meeting.

units.leftText: Take some of the blood of the bull and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger; then pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
units.rightText: And thou shalt take of the blood of the bullock, and put it upon the horns of the altar with thy finger; and thou shalt pour out all the blood at the base of the altar.

units.leftText: Take all the fat that covers the entrails and the lobe of the liver, and both kidneys with the fat on them, and burn them on the altar.
units.rightText: And thou shalt take all the fat that covereth the inwards, and the caul upon the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and burn them upon the altar.

units.leftText: But burn the flesh of the bull and its hide and dung outside the camp; it is a sin offering.
units.rightText: But the flesh of the bullock, and its skin, and its dung, shalt thou burn with fire without the camp: it is a sin-offering.
leftNotes: 29:14 Or purification offering; also in verse 36

units.leftText: Take one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.
units.rightText: Thou shalt also take the one ram; and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon the head of the ram.

units.leftText: You are to slaughter the ram, take its blood, and splatter it on all sides of the altar.
units.rightText: And thou shalt slay the ram, and thou shalt take its blood, and sprinkle it round about upon the altar.

units.leftText: Cut the ram into pieces, wash the entrails and legs, and place them with its head and other pieces.
units.rightText: And thou shalt cut the ram into its pieces, and wash its inwards, and its legs, and put them with its pieces, and with its head.

units.leftText: Then burn the entire ram on the altar; it is a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: And thou shalt burn the whole ram upon the altar: it is a burnt-offering unto Jehovah; it is a sweet savor, an offering made by fire unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: Take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head.
units.rightText: And thou shalt take the other ram; and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon the head of the ram.

units.leftText: Slaughter the ram, take some of its blood, and put it on the right earlobes of Aaron and his sons, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Splatter the remaining blood on all sides of the altar.
units.rightText: Then shalt thou kill the ram, and take of its blood, and put it upon the tip of the right ear of Aaron, and upon the tip of the right ear of his sons, and upon the thumb of their right hand, and upon the great toe of their right foot, and sprinkle the blood upon the altar round about.

units.leftText: And take some of the blood on the altar and some of the anointing oil and sprinkle it on Aaron and his garments, as well as on his sons and their garments. Then he and his garments will be consecrated, as well as his sons and their garments.
units.rightText: And thou shalt take of the blood that is upon the altar, and of the anointing oil, and sprinkle it upon Aaron, and upon his garments, and upon his sons, and upon the garments of his sons with him: and he shall be hallowed, and his garments, and his sons, and his sons’ garments with him.

units.leftText: Take the fat from the ram, the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver, both kidneys with the fat on them, and the right thigh (since this is a ram for ordination),
units.rightText: Also thou shalt take of the ram the fat, and the fat tail, and the fat that covereth the inwards, and the caul of the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and the right thigh (for it is a ram of consecration),

units.leftText: along with one loaf of bread, one cake of bread made with oil, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the LORD.
units.rightText: and one loaf of bread, and one cake of oiled bread, and one wafer, out of the basket of unleavened bread that is before Jehovah:

units.leftText: Put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons and wave them before the LORD as a wave offering.
units.rightText: and thou shalt put the whole upon the hands of Aaron, and upon the hands of his sons, and shalt wave them for a wave-offering before Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then take them from their hands and burn them on the altar atop the burnt offering as a pleasing aroma before the LORD; it is a food offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: And thou shalt take them from their hands, and burn them on the altar upon the burnt-offering, for a sweet savor before Jehovah: it is an offering made by fire unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: Take the breast of the ram of Aaron’s ordination and wave it before the LORD as a wave offering, and it will be your portion.
units.rightText: And thou shalt take the breast of Aaron’s ram of consecration, and wave it for a wave-offering before Jehovah: and it shall be thy portion.

units.leftText: Consecrate for Aaron and his sons the breast of the wave offering that is waved and the thigh of the heave offering that is lifted up from the ram of ordination.
units.rightText: And thou shalt sanctify the breast of the wave-offering, and the thigh of the heave-offering, which is waved, and which is heaved up, of the ram of consecration, even of that which is for Aaron, and of that which is for his sons:

units.leftText: This will belong to Aaron and his sons as a regular portion from the Israelites, for it is the heave offering the Israelites will make to the LORD from their peace offerings.
units.rightText: and it shall be for Aaron and his sons as their portion for ever from the children of Israel; for it is a heave-offering: and it shall be a heave-offering from the children of Israel of the sacrifices of their peace-offerings, even their heave-offering unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: The holy garments that belong to Aaron will belong to his sons after him, so they can be anointed and ordained in them.
units.rightText: And the holy garments of Aaron shall be for his sons after him, to be anointed in them, and to be consecrated in them.

units.leftText: The son who succeeds him as priest and enters the Tent of Meeting to minister in the Holy Place must wear them for seven days. Food for the Priests
units.rightText: Seven days shall the son that is priest in his stead put them on, when he cometh into the tent of meeting to minister in the holy place.

units.leftText: You are to take the ram of ordination and boil its flesh in a holy place.
units.rightText: And thou shalt take the ram of consecration, and boil its flesh in a holy place.

units.leftText: At the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, Aaron and his sons are to eat the meat of the ram and the bread that is in the basket.
units.rightText: And Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram, and the bread that is in the basket, at the door of the tent of meeting.

units.leftText: They must eat those things by which atonement was made for their ordination and consecration. But no outsider may eat them, because these things are sacred.
units.rightText: And they shall eat those things wherewith atonement was made, to consecrate and to sanctify them: but a stranger shall not eat thereof, because they are holy.

units.leftText: And if any of the meat of ordination or any bread is left until the morning, you are to burn up the remainder. It must not be eaten, because it is sacred.
units.rightText: And if aught of the flesh of the consecration, or of the bread, remain unto the morning, then thou shalt burn the remainder with fire: it shall not be eaten, because it is holy.

units.leftText: This is what you are to do for Aaron and his sons based on all that I have commanded you, taking seven days to ordain them.
units.rightText: And thus shalt thou do unto Aaron, and to his sons, according to all that I have commanded thee: seven days shalt thou consecrate them.

units.leftText: Sacrifice a bull as a sin offering each day for atonement. Purify the altar by making atonement for it, and anoint it to consecrate it.
units.rightText: And every day shalt thou offer the bullock of sin-offering for atonement: and thou shalt cleanse the altar, when thou makest atonement for it; and thou shalt anoint it, to sanctify it.

units.leftText: For seven days you shall make atonement for the altar and consecrate it. Then the altar will become most holy; whatever touches the altar will be holy. The Daily Offerings (Numbers 28:1–8|NUM 28:1-8*)
units.rightText: Seven days thou shalt make atonement for the altar, and sanctify it: and the altar shall be most holy; whatsoever toucheth the altar shall be holy.

units.leftText: This is what you are to offer regularly on the altar, each day: two lambs that are a year old.
units.rightText: Now this is that which thou shalt offer upon the altar: two lambs a year old day by day continually.

units.leftText: Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight.
units.rightText: The one lamb thou shalt offer in the morning; and the other lamb thou shalt offer at even:
leftNotes: 29:39 Hebrew between the two evenings; also in verse 41

units.leftText: With the first lamb offer a tenth of an ephah of fine flour, mixed with a quarter hin of oil from pressed olives, and a drink offering of a quarter hin of wine.
units.rightText: and with the one lamb a tenth part of an ephah of fine flour mingled with the fourth part of a hin of beaten oil, and the fourth part of a hin of wine for a drink-offering.
leftNotes: 29:40 A tenth of an ephah is approximately 2 dry quarts or 2.2 liters (probably about 2.6 pounds or 1.2 kilograms of flour).
29:40 Hebrew a quarter hin of pressed oil; that is, approximately 0.97 quarts or 0.92 liters

units.leftText: And offer the second lamb at twilight with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, as a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: And the other lamb thou shalt offer at even, and shalt do thereto according to the meal-offering of the morning, and according to the drink-offering thereof, for a sweet savor, an offering made by fire unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: For the generations to come, this burnt offering shall be made regularly at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting before the LORD, where I will meet you to speak with you.
units.rightText: It shall be a continual burnt-offering throughout your generations at the door of the tent of meeting before Jehovah, where I will meet with you, to speak there unto thee.

units.leftText: I will also meet with the Israelites there, and that place will be consecrated by My glory.
units.rightText: And there I will meet with the children of Israel; and the Tent shall be sanctified by my glory.

units.leftText: So I will consecrate the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and I will consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests. God Will Dwell among the People
units.rightText: And I will sanctify the tent of meeting, and the altar: Aaron also and his sons will I sanctify, to minister to me in the priest’s office.

units.leftText: Then I will dwell among the Israelites and be their God.
units.rightText: And I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will be their God.

units.leftText: And they will know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt so that I might dwell among them. I am the LORD their God.[’’]
units.rightText: And they shall know that I am Jehovah their God, that brought them forth out of the land of Egypt, that I might dwell among them: I am Jehovah their God.

units.leftText: “You are also to make an altar of acacia wood for the burning of incense.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make an altar to burn incense upon: of acacia wood shalt thou make it.

units.leftText: It is to be square, a cubit long, a cubit wide, and two cubits high. Its horns must be of one piece.
units.rightText: A cubit shall be the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof; foursquare shall it be; and two cubits shall be the height thereof: the horns thereof shall be of one piece with it.
leftNotes: 30:2 The altar was approximately 1.5 feet in length and width, and 3 feet high (45.7 centimeters in length and width, and 91.4 centimeters high).

units.leftText: Overlay with pure gold the top and all the sides and horns, and make a molding of gold around it.
units.rightText: And thou shalt overlay it with pure gold, the top thereof, and the sides thereof round about, and the horns thereof; and thou shalt make unto it a crown of gold round about.

units.leftText: And make two gold rings below the molding on opposite sides to hold the poles used to carry it.
units.rightText: And two golden rings shalt thou make for it under the crown thereof; upon the two ribs thereof, upon the two sides of it shalt thou make them; and they shall be for places for staves wherewith to bear it.

units.leftText: Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make the staves of acacia wood, and overlay them with gold.

units.leftText: Place the altar in front of the veil that is before the ark of the Testimony — before the mercy seat that is over the Testimony— where I will meet with you.
units.rightText: And thou shalt put it before the veil that is by the ark of the testimony, before the mercy-seat that is over the testimony, where I will meet with thee.
leftNotes: 30:6 That is, the ark of the covenant; also in verse 26

units.leftText: And Aaron is to burn fragrant incense on it every morning when he tends the lamps.
units.rightText: And Aaron shall burn thereon incense of sweet spices: every morning, when he dresseth the lamps, he shall burn it.

units.leftText: When Aaron sets up the lamps at twilight, he must burn the incense perpetually before the LORD for the generations to come.
units.rightText: And when Aaron lighteth the lamps at even, he shall burn it, a perpetual incense before Jehovah throughout your generations.
leftNotes: 30:8 Hebrew between the two evenings

units.leftText: On this altar you must not offer unauthorized incense or a burnt offering or grain offering; nor are you to pour a drink offering on it.
units.rightText: Ye shall offer no strange incense thereon, nor burnt-offering, nor meal-offering; and ye shall pour no drink-offering thereon.
leftNotes: 30:9 Or strange

units.leftText: Once a year Aaron shall make atonement on the horns of the altar. Throughout your generations he shall make atonement on it annually with the blood of the sin offering of atonement. The altar is most holy to the LORD.” The Census Offering (2 Samuel 24:1–9|2SA 24:1-9*; 1 Chronicles 21:1–6|1CH 21:1-6*)
units.rightText: And Aaron shall make atonement upon the horns of it once in the year; with the blood of the sin-offering of atonement once in the year shall he make atonement for it throughout your generations: it is most holy unto Jehovah.
leftNotes: 30:10 Or purification offering

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “When you take a census of the Israelites to number them, each man must pay the LORD a ransom for his life when he is counted. Then no plague will come upon them when they are numbered.
units.rightText: When thou takest the sum of the children of Israel, according to those that are numbered of them, then shall they give every man a ransom for his soul unto Jehovah, when thou numberest them; that there be no plague among them, when thou numberest them.

units.leftText: Everyone who crosses over to those counted must pay a half shekel, according to the sanctuary shekel, which weighs twenty gerahs. This half shekel is an offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: This they shall give, every one that passeth over unto them that are numbered, half a shekel after the shekel of the sanctuary; (the shekel is twenty gerahs), half a shekel for an offering to Jehovah.
leftNotes: 30:13 A half shekel is approximately 0.2 ounces or 5.7 grams; also in verse 15.
30:13 20 gerahs is equivalent to one shekel (approximately 0.4 ounces or 11.4 grams).

units.leftText: Everyone twenty years of age or older who crosses over must give this offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: Every one that passeth over unto them that are numbered, from twenty years old and upward, shall give the offering of Jehovah.

units.leftText: In making the offering to the LORD to atone for your lives, the rich shall not give more than a half shekel, nor shall the poor give less.
units.rightText: The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less, than the half shekel, when they give the offering of Jehovah, to make atonement for your souls.

units.leftText: Take the atonement money from the Israelites and use it for the service of the Tent of Meeting. It will serve as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD to make atonement for your lives.” The Bronze Basin (Exodus 38:8|EXO 38:8*)
units.rightText: And thou shalt take the atonement money from the children of Israel, and shalt appoint it for the service of the tent of meeting; that it may be a memorial for the children of Israel before Jehovah, to make atonement for your souls.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “You are to make a bronze basin with a bronze stand for washing. Set it between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and put water in it,
units.rightText: Thou shalt also make a laver of brass, and the base thereof of brass, whereat to wash. And thou shalt put it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and thou shalt put water therein.

units.leftText: with which Aaron and his sons are to wash their hands and feet.
units.rightText: And Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet thereat:

units.leftText: Whenever they enter the Tent of Meeting or approach the altar to minister by presenting a food offering to the LORD, they must wash with water so that they will not die.
units.rightText: when they go into the tent of meeting, they shall wash with water, that they die not; or when they come near to the altar to minister, to burn an offering made by fire unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: Thus they are to wash their hands and feet so that they will not die; this shall be a permanent statute for Aaron and his descendants for the generations to come.” The Anointing Oil
units.rightText: So they shall wash their hands and their feet, that they die not: and it shall be a statute for ever to them, even to him and to his seed throughout their generations.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: Moreover Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Take the finest spices: 500 shekels of liquid myrrh, half that amount (250 shekels) of fragrant cinnamon, 250 shekels of fragrant cane,
units.rightText: Take thou also unto thee the chief spices: of flowing myrrh five hundred shekels, and of sweet cinnamon half so much, even two hundred and fifty, and of sweet calamus two hundred and fifty,
leftNotes: 30:23 500 shekels is approximately 12.6 pounds or 5.7 kilograms of myrrh.
30:23 250 shekels is approximately 6.3 pounds or 2.9 kilograms of cinnamon.
30:23 250 shekels is approximately 6.3 pounds or 2.9 kilograms of cane.

units.leftText: 500 shekels of cassia — all according to the sanctuary shekel — and a hin of olive oil.
units.rightText: and of cassia five hundred, after the shekel of the sanctuary, and of olive oil a hin;
leftNotes: 30:24 500 shekels is approximately 12.6 pounds or 5.7 kilograms of cassia.
30:24 A hin is approximately 0.97 gallons or 3.67 liters of olive oil.

units.leftText: Prepare from these a sacred anointing oil, a fragrant blend, the work of a perfumer; it will be a sacred anointing oil.
units.rightText: and thou shalt make it a holy anointing oil, a perfume compounded after the art of the perfumer: it shall be a holy anointing oil.

units.leftText: Use this oil to anoint the Tent of Meeting, the ark of the Testimony,
units.rightText: And thou shalt anoint therewith the tent of meeting, and the ark of the testimony,

units.leftText: the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, the altar of incense,
units.rightText: and the table and all the vessels thereof, and the candlestick and the vessels thereof, and the altar of incense,

units.leftText: the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand.
units.rightText: and the altar of burnt-offering with all the vessels thereof, and the laver and the base thereof.

units.leftText: You are to consecrate them so that they will be most holy. Whatever touches them shall be holy.
units.rightText: And thou shalt sanctify them, that they may be most holy: whatsoever toucheth them shall be holy.

units.leftText: Anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them to serve Me as priests.
units.rightText: And thou shalt anoint Aaron and his sons, and sanctify them, that they may minister unto me in the priest’s office.

units.leftText: And you are to tell the Israelites, ‘This will be My sacred anointing oil for the generations to come.
units.rightText: And thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel, saying, This shall be a holy anointing oil unto me throughout your generations.

units.leftText: It must not be used to anoint an ordinary man, and you must not make anything like it with the same formula. It is holy, and it must be holy to you.
units.rightText: Upon the flesh of man shall it not be poured, neither shall ye make any like it, according to the composition thereof: it is holy, and it shall be holy unto you.

units.leftText: Anyone who mixes perfume like it or puts it on an outsider shall be cut off from his people.’” The Incense
units.rightText: Whosoever compoundeth any like it, or whosoever putteth any of it upon a stranger, he shall be cut off from his people.

units.leftText: The LORD also said to Moses, “Take fragrant spices — gum resin, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense — in equal measures,
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Take unto thee sweet spices, stacte, and onycha, and galbanum; sweet spices with pure frankincense: of each shall there be a like weight;

units.leftText: and make a fragrant blend of incense, the work of a perfumer, seasoned with salt, pure and holy.
units.rightText: and thou shalt make of it incense, a perfume after the art of the perfumer, seasoned with salt, pure and holy:

units.leftText: Grind some of it into fine powder and place it in front of the Testimony in the Tent of Meeting, where I will meet with you. It shall be most holy to you.
units.rightText: and thou shalt beat some of it very small, and put of it before the testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with thee: it shall be unto you most holy.
leftNotes: 30:36 The Testimony refers to the stone tablets in the ark of the covenant inscribed with the Ten Commandments.

units.leftText: You are never to use this formula to make incense for yourselves; you shall regard it as holy to the LORD.
units.rightText: And the incense which thou shalt make, according to the composition thereof ye shall not make for yourselves: it shall be unto thee holy for Jehovah.

units.leftText: Anyone who makes something like it to enjoy its fragrance shall be cut off from his people.”
units.rightText: Whosoever shall make like unto that, to smell thereof, he shall be cut off from his people.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “See, I have called by name Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
units.rightText: See, I have called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah:

units.leftText: And I have filled him with the Spirit of God, with skill, ability, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship,
units.rightText: and I have filled him with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship,

units.leftText: to design artistic works in gold, silver, and bronze,
units.rightText: to devise skilful works, to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass,

units.leftText: to cut gemstones for settings, and to carve wood, so that he may be a master of every craft.
units.rightText: and in cutting of stones for setting, and in carving of wood, to work in all manner of workmanship.

units.leftText: Moreover, I have selected Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, as his assistant.
units.rightText: And I, behold, I have appointed with him Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan; and in the heart of all that are wise-hearted I have put wisdom, that they may make all that I have commanded thee:

units.leftText: the Tent of Meeting, the ark of the Testimony and the mercy seat upon it, and all the other furnishings of the tent—
units.rightText: the tent of meeting, and the ark of the testimony, and the mercy-seat that is thereupon, and all the furniture of the Tent,
leftNotes: 31:7 That is, the ark of the covenant

units.leftText: the table with its utensils, the pure gold lampstand with all its utensils, the altar of incense,
units.rightText: and the table and its vessels, and the pure candlestick with all its vessels, and the altar of incense,

units.leftText: the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the basin with its stand—
units.rightText: and the altar of burnt-offering with all its vessels, and the laver and its base,

units.leftText: as well as the woven garments, both the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons to serve as priests,
units.rightText: and the finely wrought garments, and the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest’s office,

units.leftText: in addition to the anointing oil and fragrant incense for the Holy Place. They are to make them according to all that I have commanded you.” The Sign of the Sabbath (Numbers 15:32–36|NUM 15:32-36*)
units.rightText: and the anointing oil, and the incense of sweet spices for the holy place: according to all that I have commanded thee shall they do.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Tell the Israelites, ‘Surely you must keep My Sabbaths, for this will be a sign between Me and you for the generations to come, so that you may know that I am the LORD who sanctifies you.
units.rightText: Speak thou also unto the children of Israel, saying, Verily ye shall keep my sabbaths: for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations; that ye may know that I am Jehovah who sanctifieth you.

units.leftText: Keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you. Anyone who profanes it must surely be put to death. Whoever does any work on that day must be cut off from among his people.
units.rightText: Ye shall keep the sabbath therefore; for it is holy unto you: every one that profaneth it shall surely be put to death; for whosoever doeth any work therein, that soul shall be cut off from among his people.

units.leftText: For six days work may be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to the LORD. Whoever does any work on the Sabbath day must surely be put to death.
units.rightText: Six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day is a sabbath of solemn rest, holy to Jehovah: whosoever doeth any work on the sabbath day, he shall surely be put to death.

units.leftText: The Israelites must keep the Sabbath, celebrating it as a permanent covenant for the generations to come.
units.rightText: Wherefore the children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant.

units.leftText: It is a sign between Me and the Israelites forever; for in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, but on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed.’” Moses Receives the Tablets
units.rightText: It is a sign between me and the children of Israel for ever: for in six days Jehovah made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed.

units.leftText: When the LORD had finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, He gave him the two tablets of the Testimony, tablets of stone inscribed by the finger of God.
units.rightText: And he gave unto Moses, when he had made an end of communing with him upon mount Sinai, the two tables of the testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God.

units.leftText: Now when the people saw that Moses was delayed in coming down from the mountain, they gathered around Aaron and said, “Come, make us gods who will go before us. As for this Moses who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him!”
units.rightText: And when the people saw that Moses delayed to come down from the mount, the people gathered themselves together unto Aaron, and said unto him, Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we know not what is become of him.
leftNotes: 32:1 Cited in Acts 7:40|ACT 7:40*

units.leftText: So Aaron told them, “Take off the gold earrings that are on your wives and sons and daughters, and bring them to me.”
units.rightText: And Aaron said unto them, Break off the golden rings, which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters, and bring them unto me.

units.leftText: Then all the people took off their gold earrings and brought them to Aaron.
units.rightText: And all the people brake off the golden rings which were in their ears, and brought them unto Aaron.

units.leftText: He took the gold from their hands, and with an engraving tool he fashioned it into a molten calf. And they said, “These, O Israel, are your gods, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt!”
units.rightText: And he received it at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, and made it a molten calf: and they said, These are thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: When Aaron saw this, he built an altar before the calf and proclaimed: “Tomorrow shall be a feast to the LORD.”
units.rightText: And when Aaron saw this, he built an altar before it; and Aaron made proclamation, and said, To-morrow shall be a feast to Jehovah.

units.leftText: So the next day they arose, offered burnt offerings, and presented peace offerings. And the people sat down to eat and drink and got up to indulge in revelry.
units.rightText: And they rose up early on the morrow, and offered burnt-offerings, and brought peace-offerings; and the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.
leftNotes: 32:6 Or to play; cited in 1 Corinthians 10:7|1CO 10:7*

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go down at once, for your people, whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves.
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, Go, get thee down; for thy people, that thou broughtest up out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves:

units.leftText: How quickly they have turned aside from the way that I commanded them! They have made for themselves a molten calf and have bowed down to it. They have sacrificed to it and said, ‘These, O Israel, are your gods, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.’”
units.rightText: they have turned aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them: they have made them a molten calf, and have worshipped it, and have sacrificed unto it, and said, These are thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: The LORD also said to Moses, “I have seen this people, and they are indeed a stiff-necked people.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people:

units.leftText: Now leave Me alone, so that My anger may burn against them and consume them. Then I will make you into a great nation.”
units.rightText: now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation.

units.leftText: But Moses sought the favor of the LORD his God, saying, “O LORD, why does Your anger burn against Your people, whom You brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and a mighty hand?
units.rightText: And Moses besought Jehovah his God, and said, Jehovah, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, that thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power and with a mighty hand?

units.leftText: Why should the Egyptians declare, ‘He brought them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them from the face of the earth’? Turn from Your fierce anger and relent from doing harm to Your people.
units.rightText: Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, saying, For evil did he bring them forth, to slay them in the mountains, and to consume them from the face of the earth? Turn from thy fierce wrath, and repent of this evil against thy people.

units.leftText: Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, to whom You swore by Your very self when You declared, ‘I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky, and I will give your descendants all this land that I have promised, and it shall be their inheritance forever.’”
units.rightText: Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, thy servants, to whom thou swarest by thine own self, and saidst unto them, I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and all this land that I have spoken of will I give unto your seed, and they shall inherit it for ever.

units.leftText: So the LORD relented from the calamity He had threatened to bring on His people.
units.rightText: And Jehovah repented of the evil which he said he would do unto his people.

units.leftText: Then Moses turned and went down the mountain with the two tablets of the Testimony in his hands. They were inscribed on both sides, front and back.
units.rightText: And Moses turned, and went down from the mount, with the two tables of the testimony in his hand; tables that were written on both their sides; on the one side and on the other were they written.

units.leftText: The tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.
units.rightText: And the tables were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, graven upon the tables.

units.leftText: When Joshua heard the sound of the people shouting, he said to Moses, “The sound of war is in the camp.”
units.rightText: And when Joshua heard the noise of the people as they shouted, he said unto Moses, There is a noise of war in the camp.

units.leftText: But Moses replied: “It is neither the cry of victory nor the cry of defeat; I hear the sound of singing!”
units.rightText: And he said, It is not the voice of them that shout for mastery, neither is it the voice of them that cry for being overcome; but the noise of them that sing do I hear.

units.leftText: As Moses approached the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, he burned with anger and threw the tablets out of his hands, shattering them at the base of the mountain.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as soon as he came nigh unto the camp, that he saw the calf and the dancing: and Moses’ anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount.

units.leftText: Then he took the calf they had made, burned it in the fire, ground it to powder, and scattered the powder over the face of the water. Then he forced the Israelites to drink it.
units.rightText: And he took the calf which they had made, and burnt it with fire, and ground it to powder, and strewed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it.

units.leftText: “What did this people do to you,” Moses asked Aaron, “that you have led them into so great a sin?”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Aaron, What did this people unto thee, that thou hast brought a great sin upon them?

units.leftText: “Do not be enraged, my lord,” Aaron replied. “You yourself know that the people are intent on evil.
units.rightText: And Aaron said, Let not the anger of my lord wax hot: thou knowest the people, that they are set on evil.

units.leftText: They told me, ‘Make us gods who will go before us. As for this Moses who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him!’
units.rightText: For they said unto me, Make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we know not what is become of him.

units.leftText: So I said to them, ‘Whoever has gold, let him take it off,’ and they gave it to me. And when I threw it into the fire, out came this calf!”
units.rightText: And I said unto them, Whosoever hath any gold, let them break it off: so they gave it me; and I cast it into the fire, and there came out this calf.

units.leftText: Moses saw that the people were out of control, for Aaron had let them run wild and become a laughingstock to their enemies.
units.rightText: And when Moses saw that the people were broken loose, (for Aaron had let them loose for a derision among their enemies,)
leftNotes: 32:25 Or and become an object of derision

units.leftText: So Moses stood at the entrance to the camp and said, “Whoever is for the LORD, come to me.” And all the Levites gathered around him.
units.rightText: then Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and said, Whoso is on Jehovah’s side, let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him.

units.leftText: He told them, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Each of you men is to fasten his sword to his side, go back and forth through the camp from gate to gate, and slay his brother, his friend, and his neighbor.’”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, Put ye every man his sword upon his thigh, and go to and fro from gate to gate throughout the camp, and slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbor.

units.leftText: The Levites did as Moses commanded, and that day about three thousand of the people fell dead.
units.rightText: And the sons of Levi did according to the word of Moses: and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men.

units.leftText: Afterward, Moses said, “Today you have been ordained for service to the LORD, since each man went against his son and his brother; so the LORD has bestowed a blessing on you this day.”
units.rightText: And Moses said, Consecrate yourselves to-day to Jehovah, yea, every man against his son, and against his brother; that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day.
leftNotes: 32:29 Or have ordained yourselves

units.leftText: The next day Moses said to the people, “You have committed a great sin. Now I will go up to the LORD; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the morrow, that Moses said unto the people, Ye have sinned a great sin: and now I will go up unto Jehovah; peradventure I shall make atonement for your sin.

units.leftText: So Moses returned to the LORD and said, “Oh, what a great sin these people have committed! They have made gods of gold for themselves.
units.rightText: And Moses returned unto Jehovah, and said, Oh, this people have sinned a great sin, and have made them gods of gold.

units.leftText: Yet now, if You would only forgive their sin.... But if not, please blot me out of the book that You have written.”
units.rightText: Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin—; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written.

units.leftText: The LORD replied to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against Me, I will blot out of My book.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.

units.leftText: Now go, lead the people to the place I described. Behold, My angel shall go before you. But on the day I settle accounts, I will punish them for their sin.”
units.rightText: And now go, lead the people unto the place of which I have spoken unto thee: behold, mine angel shall go before thee; nevertheless in the day when I visit, I will visit their sin upon them.

units.leftText: And the LORD sent a plague on the people because of what they had done with the calf that Aaron had made.
units.rightText: And Jehovah smote the people, because they made the calf, which Aaron made.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Leave this place, you and the people you brought up out of the land of Egypt, and go to the land that I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob when I said, ‘I will give it to your descendants.’
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, Depart, go up hence, thou and the people that thou hast brought up out of the land of Egypt, unto the land of which I sware unto Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, Unto thy seed will I give it:

units.leftText: And I will send an angel before you, and I will drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
units.rightText: and I will send an angel before thee; and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite:

units.leftText: Go up to a land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go with you, because you are a stiff-necked people; otherwise, I might destroy you on the way.”
units.rightText: unto a land flowing with milk and honey: for I will not go up in the midst of thee, for thou art a stiffnecked people, lest I consume thee in the way.

units.leftText: When the people heard this bad news, they went into mourning, and no one put on any of his jewelry.
units.rightText: And when the people heard these evil tidings, they mourned: and no man did put on him his ornaments.

units.leftText: For the LORD had said to Moses, “Tell the Israelites, ‘You are a stiff-necked people. If I should go with you for a single moment, I would destroy you. Now take off your jewelry, and I will decide what to do with you.’”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Say unto the children of Israel, Ye are a stiffnecked people; if I go up into the midst of thee for one moment, I shall consume thee: therefore now put off thy ornaments from thee, that I may know what to do unto thee.

units.leftText: So the Israelites stripped themselves of their jewelry from Mount Horeb onward. The Tent of Meeting
units.rightText: And the children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from mount Horeb onward.
leftNotes: 33:6 That is, from Mount Sinai onward, or possibly a mountain in the range containing Mount Sinai

units.leftText: Now Moses used to take the tent and pitch it at a distance outside the camp. He called it the Tent of Meeting, and anyone inquiring of the LORD would go to the Tent of Meeting outside the camp.
units.rightText: Now Moses used to take the tent and to pitch it without the camp, afar off from the camp; and he called it, The tent of meeting. And it came to pass, that every one that sought Jehovah went out unto the tent of meeting, which was without the camp.

units.leftText: Then, whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would stand at the entrances to their own tents and watch Moses until he entered the tent.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Moses went out unto the Tent, that all the people rose up, and stood, every man at his tent door, and looked after Moses, until he was gone into the Tent.

units.leftText: As Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and remain at the entrance, and the LORD would speak with Moses.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Moses entered into the Tent, the pillar of cloud descended, and stood at the door of the Tent: and Jehovah spake with Moses.

units.leftText: When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance to the tent, they would stand up and worship, each one at the entrance to his own tent.
units.rightText: And all the people saw the pillar of cloud stand at the door of the Tent: and all the people rose up and worshipped, every man at his tent door.

units.leftText: Thus the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his young assistant Joshua son of Nun would not leave the tent. The Promise of God’s Presence
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend. And he turned again into the camp: but his minister Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the Tent.

units.leftText: Then Moses said to the LORD, “Look, You have been telling me, ‘Lead this people up,’ but You have not let me know whom You will send with me. Yet You have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have found favor in My sight.’
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Jehovah, See, thou sayest unto me, Bring up this people: and thou hast not let me know whom thou wilt send with me. Yet thou hast said, I know thee by name, and thou hast also found favor in my sight.

units.leftText: Now if indeed I have found favor in Your sight, please let me know Your ways, that I may know You and find favor in Your sight. Remember that this nation is Your people.”
units.rightText: Now therefore, I pray thee, if I have found favor in thy sight, show me now thy ways, that I may know thee, to the end that I may find favor in thy sight: and consider that this nation is thy people.

units.leftText: And the LORD answered, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”
units.rightText: And he said, My presence shall go with thee, and I will give thee rest.

units.leftText: “If Your Presence does not go with us,” Moses replied, “do not lead us up from here.
units.rightText: And he said unto him, If thy presence go not with me, carry us not up hence.

units.leftText: For how then can it be known that Your people and I have found favor in Your sight, unless You go with us? How else will we be distinguished from all the other people on the face of the earth?”
units.rightText: For wherein now shall it be known that I have found favor in thy sight, I and thy people? is it not in that thou goest with us, so that we are separated, I and thy people, from all the people that are upon the face of the earth?

units.leftText: So the LORD said to Moses, “I will do this very thing you have asked, for you have found favor in My sight, and I know you by name.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, I will do this thing also that thou hast spoken; for thou hast found favor in my sight, and I know thee by name.

units.leftText: Then Moses said, “Please show me Your glory.”
units.rightText: And he said, Show me, I pray thee, thy glory.

units.leftText: “I will cause all My goodness to pass before you,” the LORD replied, “and I will proclaim My name — the LORD — in your presence. I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.”
units.rightText: And he said, I will make all my goodness pass before thee, and will proclaim the name of Jehovah before thee; and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I will show mercy.
leftNotes: 33:19 Cited in Romans 9:15|ROM 9:15*

units.leftText: But He added, “You cannot see My face, for no one can see Me and live.”
units.rightText: And he said, Thou canst not see my face; for man shall not see me and live.

units.leftText: The LORD continued, “There is a place near Me where you are to stand upon a rock,
units.rightText: And Jehovah said, Behold, there is a place by me, and thou shalt stand upon the rock:

units.leftText: and when My glory passes by, I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with My hand until I have passed by.
units.rightText: and it shall come to pass, while my glory passeth by, that I will put thee in a cleft of the rock, and will cover thee with my hand until I have passed by:

units.leftText: Then I will take My hand away, and you will see My back; but My face must not be seen.”
units.rightText: and I will take away my hand, and thou shalt see my back; but my face shall not be seen.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Chisel out two stone tablets like the originals, and I will write on them the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Hew thee two tables of stone like unto the first: and I will write upon the tables the words that were on the first tables, which thou brakest.

units.leftText: Be ready in the morning, and come up on Mount Sinai to present yourself before Me on the mountaintop.
units.rightText: And be ready by the morning, and come up in the morning unto mount Sinai, and present thyself there to me on the top of the mount.

units.leftText: No one may go up with you; in fact, no one may be seen anywhere on the mountain — not even the flocks or herds may graze in front of the mountain.”
units.rightText: And no man shall come up with thee; neither let any man be seen throughout all the mount; neither let the flocks nor herds feed before that mount.

units.leftText: So Moses chiseled out two stone tablets like the originals. He rose early in the morning, and taking the two stone tablets in his hands, he went up Mount Sinai as the LORD had commanded him.
units.rightText: And he hewed two tables of stone like unto the first; and Moses rose up early in the morning, and went up unto mount Sinai, as Jehovah had commanded him, and took in his hand two tables of stone.

units.leftText: And the LORD descended in a cloud, stood with him there, and proclaimed His name, the LORD.
units.rightText: And Jehovah descended in the cloud, and stood with him there, and proclaimed the name of Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then the LORD passed in front of Moses and called out: “The LORD, the LORD God, is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion and faithfulness,
units.rightText: And Jehovah passed by before him, and proclaimed, Jehovah, Jehovah, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in lovingkindness and truth;

units.leftText: maintaining loving devotion to a thousand generations, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin. Yet He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished; He will visit the iniquity of the fathers on their children and grandchildren to the third and fourth generations.”
units.rightText: keeping lovingkindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin; and that will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children’s children, upon the third and upon the fourth generation.
leftNotes: 34:7 Hebrew to thousands

units.leftText: Moses immediately bowed down to the ground and worshiped.
units.rightText: And Moses made haste, and bowed his head toward the earth, and worshipped.

units.leftText: “O Lord,” he said, “if I have indeed found favor in Your sight, my Lord, please go with us. Although this is a stiff-necked people, forgive our iniquity and sin, and take us as Your inheritance.” The LORD Renews the Covenant (2 Corinthians 3:7–18|2CO 3:7-18*)
units.rightText: And he said, If now I have found favor in thy sight, O Lord, let the Lord, I pray thee, go in the midst of us; for it is a stiffnecked people; and pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us for thine inheritance.

units.leftText: And the LORD said, “Behold, I am making a covenant. Before all your people I will perform wonders that have never been done in any nation in all the world. All the people among whom you live will see the LORD’s work, for it is an awesome thing that I am doing with you.
units.rightText: And he said, Behold, I make a covenant: before all thy people I will do marvels, such as have not been wrought in all the earth, nor in any nation; and all the people among which thou art shall see the work of Jehovah; for it is a terrible thing that I do with thee.

units.leftText: Observe what I command you this day. I will drive out before you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
units.rightText: Observe thou that which I command thee this day: behold, I drive out before thee the Amorite, and the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite.

units.leftText: Be careful not to make a treaty with the inhabitants of the land you are entering, lest they become a snare in your midst.
units.rightText: Take heed to thyself, lest thou make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land whither thou goest, lest it be for a snare in the midst of thee:
leftNotes: 34:12 Forms of the Hebrew berit are translated in most passages as covenant.

units.leftText: Rather, you must tear down their altars, smash their sacred stones, and chop down their Asherah poles.
units.rightText: but ye shall break down their altars, and dash in pieces their pillars, and ye shall cut down their Asherim;

units.leftText: For you must not worship any other god, for the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.
units.rightText: (for thou shalt worship no other god: for Jehovah, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God);

units.leftText: Do not make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, for when they prostitute themselves to their gods and sacrifice to them, they will invite you, and you will eat their sacrifices.
units.rightText: lest thou make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, and they play the harlot after their gods, and sacrifice unto their gods, and one call thee and thou eat of his sacrifice;

units.leftText: And when you take some of their daughters as brides for your sons, their daughters will prostitute themselves to their gods and cause your sons to do the same.
units.rightText: and thou take of their daughters unto thy sons, and their daughters play the harlot after their gods, and make thy sons play the harlot after their gods.

units.leftText: You shall make no molten gods for yourselves.
units.rightText: Thou shalt make thee no molten gods.

units.leftText: You are to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread. For seven days at the appointed time in the month of Abib, you are to eat unleavened bread as I commanded you. For in the month of Abib you came out of Egypt.
units.rightText: The feast of unleavened bread shalt thou keep. Seven days thou shalt eat unleavened bread, as I commanded thee, at the time appointed in the month Abib; for in the month Abib thou camest out from Egypt.
leftNotes: 34:18 That is, the seven-day period after the Passover during which no leaven may be eaten; see Exodus 12:14–20|EXO 12:14-20*.
34:18 Abib was the first month of the ancient Hebrew lunar calendar, usually occurring within the months of March and April; twice in this verse.

units.leftText: The first offspring of every womb belongs to Me, including all the firstborn males among your livestock, whether cattle or sheep.
units.rightText: All that openeth the womb is mine; and all thy cattle that is male, the firstlings of cow and sheep.

units.leftText: You must redeem the firstborn of a donkey with a lamb; but if you do not redeem it, you are to break its neck. You must redeem all the firstborn of your sons. No one shall appear before Me empty-handed.
units.rightText: And the firstling of an ass thou shalt redeem with a lamb: and if thou wilt not redeem it, then thou shalt break its neck. All the first-born of thy sons thou shalt redeem. And none shall appear before me empty.

units.leftText: Six days you shall labor, but on the seventh day you shall rest; even in the seasons of plowing and harvesting, you must rest.
units.rightText: Six days thou shalt work, but on the seventh day thou shalt rest: in plowing time and in harvest thou shalt rest.

units.leftText: And you are to celebrate the Feast of Weeks with the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the Feast of Ingathering at the turn of the year.
units.rightText: And thou shalt observe the feast of weeks, even of the first-fruits of wheat harvest, and the feast of ingathering at the year’s end.
leftNotes: 34:22 That is, Shavuot, the late spring feast of pilgrimage to Jerusalem; it is also known as the Feast of Harvest(see Exodus 23:16|EXO 23:16*) or the Feast of Pentecost(see Acts 2:1|ACT 2:1*).
34:22 That is, Sukkot, the autumn feast of pilgrimage to Jerusalem; it is later called the Feast of Tabernacles (or Booths or Shelters).

units.leftText: Three times a year all your males are to appear before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel.
units.rightText: Three times in the year shall all thy males appear before the Lord Jehovah, the God of Israel.

units.leftText: For I will drive out the nations before you and enlarge your borders, and no one will covet your land when you go up three times a year to appear before the LORD your God.
units.rightText: For I will cast out nations before thee, and enlarge thy borders: neither shall any man desire thy land, when thou goest up to appear before Jehovah thy God three times in the year.

units.leftText: Do not offer the blood of a sacrifice to Me along with anything leavened, and do not let any of the sacrifice from the Passover Feast remain until morning.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread; neither shall the sacrifice of the feast of the passover be left unto the morning.

units.leftText: Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God. You must not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.”
units.rightText: The first of the first-fruits of thy ground thou shalt bring unto the house of Jehovah thy God. Thou shalt not boil a kid in its mother’s milk.

units.leftText: The LORD also said to Moses, “Write down these words, for in accordance with these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Write thou these words: for after the tenor of these words I have made a covenant with thee and with Israel.

units.leftText: So Moses was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights without eating bread or drinking water. He wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant — the Ten Commandments.
units.rightText: And he was there with Jehovah forty days and forty nights; he did neither eat bread, nor drink water. And he wrote upon the tables the words of the covenant, the ten commandments.
leftNotes: 34:28 Hebrew the Ten Words

units.leftText: And when Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the Testimony in his hands, he was unaware that his face had become radiant from speaking with the LORD.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Moses came down from mount Sinai with the two tables of the testimony in Moses’ hand, when he came down from the mount, that Moses knew not that the skin of his face shone by reason of his speaking with him.

units.leftText: Aaron and all the Israelites looked at Moses, and behold, his face was radiant. And they were afraid to approach him.
units.rightText: And when Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come nigh him.

units.leftText: But Moses called out to them; so Aaron and all the leaders of the congregation returned to him, and Moses spoke to them.
units.rightText: And Moses called unto them; and Aaron and all the rulers of the congregation returned unto him: and Moses spake to them.

units.leftText: And after this all the Israelites came near, and Moses commanded them to do everything that the LORD had told him on Mount Sinai.
units.rightText: And afterward all the children of Israel came nigh: and he gave them in commandment all that Jehovah had spoken with him in mount Sinai.

units.leftText: When Moses had finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face.
units.rightText: And when Moses had done speaking with them, he put a veil on his face.

units.leftText: But whenever Moses went in before the LORD to speak with Him, he would remove the veil until he came out. And when he came out, he would tell the Israelites what he had been commanded,
units.rightText: But when Moses went in before Jehovah to speak with him, he took the veil off, until he came out; and he came out, and spake unto the children of Israel that which he was commanded.

units.leftText: and the Israelites would see that the face of Moses was radiant. So Moses would put the veil back over his face until he went in to speak with the LORD.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel saw the face of Moses, that the skin of Moses’ face shone: and Moses put the veil upon his face again, until he went in to speak with him.

units.leftText: Then Moses assembled the whole congregation of Israel and said to them, “These are the things that the LORD has commanded you to do:
units.rightText: And Moses assembled all the congregation of the children of Israel, and said unto them, These are the words which Jehovah hath commanded, that ye should do them.

units.leftText: For six days work may be done, but the seventh day shall be your holy day, a Sabbath of complete rest to the LORD. Whoever does any work on that day must be put to death.
