units.rightText: Six days shall work be done; but on the seventh day there shall be to you a holy day, a sabbath of solemn rest to Jehovah: whosoever doeth any work therein shall be put to death.

units.leftText: Do not light a fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day.” Offerings for the Tabernacle (Exodus 25:1–9|EXO 25:1-9*)
units.rightText: Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day.

units.leftText: Moses also told the whole congregation of Israel, “This is what the LORD has commanded:
units.rightText: And Moses spake unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying, This is the thing which Jehovah commanded, saying,

units.leftText: Take from among you an offering to the LORD. Let everyone whose heart is willing bring an offering to the LORD: gold, silver, and bronze;
units.rightText: Take ye from among you an offering unto Jehovah; whosoever is of a willing heart, let him bring it, Jehovah’s offering: gold, and silver, and brass,

units.leftText: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen and goat hair;
units.rightText: and blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats’ hair,

units.leftText: ram skins dyed red and fine leather; acacia wood;
units.rightText: and rams’ skins dyed red, and sealskins, and acacia wood,
leftNotes: 35:7 Possibly the hides of large aquatic mammals; also in verse 23

units.leftText: olive oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
units.rightText: and oil for the light, and spices for the anointing oil, and for the sweet incense,

units.leftText: and onyx stones and gemstones to be mounted on the ephod and breastpiece. The Skilled Craftsmen
units.rightText: and onyx stones, and stones to be set, for the ephod, and for the breastplate.

units.leftText: Let every skilled craftsman among you come and make everything that the LORD has commanded:
units.rightText: And let every wise-hearted man among you come, and make all that Jehovah hath commanded:

units.leftText: the tabernacle with its tent and covering, its clasps and frames, its crossbars, posts, and bases;
units.rightText: the tabernacle, its tent, and its covering, its clasps, and its boards, its bars, its pillars, and its sockets;

units.leftText: the ark with its poles and mercy seat, and the veil to shield it;
units.rightText: the ark, and the staves thereof, the mercy-seat, and the veil of the screen;

units.leftText: the table with its poles, all its utensils, and the Bread of the Presence;
units.rightText: the table, and its staves, and all its vessels, and the showbread;

units.leftText: the lampstand for light with its accessories and lamps and oil for the light;
units.rightText: the candlestick also for the light, and its vessels, and its lamps, and the oil for the light;

units.leftText: the altar of incense with its poles; the anointing oil and fragrant incense; the curtain for the doorway at the entrance to the tabernacle;
units.rightText: and the altar of incense, and its staves, and the anointing oil, and the sweet incense, and the screen for the door, at the door of the tabernacle;

units.leftText: the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grate, its poles, and all its utensils; the basin with its stand;
units.rightText: the altar of burnt-offering, with its grating of brass, its staves, and all its vessels, the laver and its base;

units.leftText: the curtains of the courtyard with its posts and bases, and the curtain for the gate of the courtyard;
units.rightText: the hangings of the court, the pillars thereof, and their sockets, and the screen for the gate of the court;

units.leftText: the tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the courtyard, along with their ropes;
units.rightText: the pins of the tabernacle, and the pins of the court, and their cords;

units.leftText: and the woven garments for ministering in the holy place— both the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons to serve as priests.” The People Offer Gifts
units.rightText: the finely wrought garments, for ministering in the holy place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest’s office.

units.leftText: Then the whole congregation of Israel withdrew from the presence of Moses.
units.rightText: And all the congregation of the children of Israel departed from the presence of Moses.

units.leftText: And everyone whose heart stirred him and whose spirit prompted him came and brought an offering to the LORD for the work on the Tent of Meeting, for all its services, and for the holy garments.
units.rightText: And they came, every one whose heart stirred him up, and every one whom his spirit made willing, and brought Jehovah’s offering, for the work of the tent of meeting, and for all the service thereof, and for the holy garments.

units.leftText: So all who had willing hearts, both men and women, came and brought brooches and earrings, rings and necklaces, and all kinds of gold jewelry. And they all presented their gold as a wave offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: And they came, both men and women, as many as were willing-hearted, and brought brooches, and ear-rings, and signet-rings, and armlets, all jewels of gold; even every man that offered an offering of gold unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: Everyone who had blue, purple, or scarlet yarn, or fine linen, goat hair, ram skins dyed red, or articles of fine leather, brought them.
units.rightText: And every man, with whom was found blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats’ hair, and rams’ skins dyed red, and sealskins, brought them.

units.leftText: And all who could present an offering of silver or bronze brought it as a contribution to the LORD. Also, everyone who had acacia wood for any part of the service brought it.
units.rightText: Every one that did offer an offering of silver and brass brought Jehovah’s offering; and every man, with whom was found acacia wood for any work of the service, brought it.

units.leftText: Every skilled woman spun with her hands and brought what she had spun: blue, purple, or scarlet yarn, or fine linen.
units.rightText: And all the women that were wise-hearted did spin with their hands, and brought that which they had spun, the blue, and the purple, the scarlet, and the fine linen.

units.leftText: And all the skilled women whose hearts were stirred spun the goat hair.
units.rightText: And all the women whose heart stirred them up in wisdom spun the goats’ hair.

units.leftText: The leaders brought onyx stones and gemstones to mount on the ephod and breastpiece,
units.rightText: And the rulers brought the onyx stones, and the stones to be set, for the ephod, and for the breastplate;

units.leftText: as well as spices and olive oil for the light, for the anointing oil, and for the fragrant incense.
units.rightText: and the spice, and the oil; for the light, and for the anointing oil, and for the sweet incense.

units.leftText: So all the men and women of the Israelites whose hearts prompted them brought a freewill offering to the LORD for all the work that the LORD through Moses had commanded them to do. Bezalel and Oholiab (Exodus 31:1–11|EXO 31:1-11*)
units.rightText: The children of Israel brought a freewill-offering unto Jehovah; every man and woman, whose heart made them willing to bring for all the work, which Jehovah had commanded to be made by Moses.

units.leftText: Then Moses said to the Israelites, “See, the LORD has called by name Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
units.rightText: And Moses said unto the children of Israel, See, Jehovah hath called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah;

units.leftText: And He has filled him with the Spirit of God, with skill, ability, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship,
units.rightText: and he hath filled him with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship;

units.leftText: to design artistic works in gold, silver, and bronze,
units.rightText: and to devise skilful works, to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass,

units.leftText: to cut gemstones for settings, and to carve wood, so that he may be a master of every artistic craft.
units.rightText: and in cutting of stones for setting, and in carving of wood, to work in all manner of skilful workmanship.

units.leftText: And the LORD has given both him and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, the ability to teach others.
units.rightText: And he hath put in his heart that he may teach, both he, and Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

units.leftText: He has filled them with skill to do all kinds of work as engravers, designers, embroiderers in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen, and as weavers — as artistic designers of every kind of craft.[’’]
units.rightText: Them hath he filled with wisdom of heart, to work all manner of workmanship, of the engraver, and of the skilful workman, and of the embroiderer, in blue, and in purple, in scarlet, and in fine linen, and of the weaver, even of them that do any workmanship, and of those that devise skilful works.

units.leftText: “So Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled person are to carry out everything commanded by the LORD, who has given them skill and ability to know how to perform all the work of constructing the sanctuary.”
units.rightText: And Bezalel and Oholiab shall work, and every wise-hearted man, in whom Jehovah hath put wisdom and understanding to know how to work all the work for the service of the sanctuary, according to all that Jehovah hath commanded.

units.leftText: Then Moses summoned Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled person whom the LORD had gifted — everyone whose heart stirred him to come and do the work.
units.rightText: And Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab, and every wise-hearted man, in whose heart Jehovah had put wisdom, even every one whose heart stirred him up to come unto the work to do it:

units.leftText: They received from Moses all the contributions that the Israelites had brought to carry out the service of constructing the sanctuary.
units.rightText: and they received of Moses all the offering which the children of Israel had brought for the work of the service of the sanctuary, wherewith to make it. And they brought yet unto him freewill-offerings every morning.

units.leftText: so that all the skilled craftsmen who were doing all the work on the sanctuary left their work
units.rightText: And all the wise men, that wrought all the work of the sanctuary, came every man from his work which they wrought;

units.leftText: and said to Moses, “The people are bringing more than enough for doing the work the LORD has commanded us to do.”
units.rightText: and they spake unto Moses, saying, The people bring much more than enough for the service of the work which Jehovah commanded to make.

units.leftText: After Moses had given an order, they sent a proclamation throughout the camp: “No man or woman should make anything else as an offering for the sanctuary.” So the people were restrained from bringing more,
units.rightText: And Moses gave commandment, and they caused it to be proclaimed throughout the camp, saying, Let neither man nor woman make any more work for the offering of the sanctuary. So the people were restrained from bringing.

units.leftText: since what they already had was more than enough to perform all the work. The Ten Curtains for the Tabernacle (Exodus 26:1–6|EXO 26:1-6*)
units.rightText: For the stuff they had was sufficient for all the work to make it, and too much.

units.leftText: All the skilled craftsmen among the workmen made the ten curtains for the tabernacle. They were made of finely spun linen, as well as blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, with cherubim skillfully worked into them.
units.rightText: And all the wise-hearted men among them that wrought the work made the tabernacle with ten curtains; of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, with cherubim, the work of the skilful workman, Bezalel made them.

units.leftText: Each curtain was twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide; all the curtains were the same size.
units.rightText: The length of each curtain was eight and twenty cubits, and the breadth of each curtain four cubits: all the curtains had one measure.
leftNotes: 36:9 Each of the ten curtains was approximately 42 feet long and 6 feet wide (12.8 meters long and 1.8 meters wide).

units.leftText: And he joined five of the curtains together, and the other five he joined as well.
units.rightText: And he coupled five curtains one to another: and the other five curtains he coupled one to another.

units.leftText: He made loops of blue material on the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and also on the end curtain in the second set.
units.rightText: And he made loops of blue upon the edge of the one curtain from the selvedge in the coupling: likewise he made in the edge of the curtain that was outmost in the second coupling.

units.leftText: He made fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the second set, so that the loops lined up opposite one another.
units.rightText: Fifty loops made he in the one curtain, and fifty loops made he in the edge of the curtain that was in the second coupling: the loops were opposite one to another.

units.leftText: He also made fifty gold clasps to join the curtains together, so that the tabernacle was a unit. The Eleven Curtains of Goat Hair (Exodus 26:7–14|EXO 26:7-14*)
units.rightText: And he made fifty clasps of gold, and coupled the curtains one to another with the clasps: so the tabernacle was one.

units.leftText: He then made curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle — eleven curtains in all.
units.rightText: And he made curtains of goats’ hair for a tent over the tabernacle: eleven curtains he made them.

units.leftText: Each of the eleven curtains was the same size — thirty cubits long and four cubits wide.
units.rightText: The length of each curtain was thirty cubits, and four cubits the breadth of each curtain: the eleven curtains had one measure.
leftNotes: 36:15 Each of the eleven curtains was approximately 45 feet long and 6 feet wide (13.7 meters long and 1.8 meters wide).

units.leftText: He joined five of the curtains into one set and the other six into another.
units.rightText: And he coupled five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves.

units.leftText: He made fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and fifty loops along the edge of the corresponding curtain in the second set.
units.rightText: And he made fifty loops on the edge of the curtain that was outmost in the coupling, and fifty loops made he upon the edge of the curtain which was outmost in the second coupling.

units.leftText: He also made fifty bronze clasps to join the tent together as a unit.
units.rightText: And he made fifty clasps of brass to couple the tent together, that it might be one.

units.leftText: Additionally, he made for the tent a covering of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather. The Frames and Bases (Exodus 26:15–30|EXO 26:15-30*)
units.rightText: And he made a covering for the tent of rams’ skins dyed red, and a covering of sealskins above.
leftNotes: 36:19 Possibly the hides of large aquatic mammals

units.leftText: Next, he constructed upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
units.rightText: And he made the boards for the tabernacle, of acacia wood, standing up.

units.leftText: Each frame was ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
units.rightText: Ten cubits was the length of a board, and a cubit and a half the breadth of each board.
leftNotes: 36:21 Each frame was approximately 15 feet long and 2.25 feet wide (4.6 meters long and 68.6 centimeters wide).

units.leftText: Two tenons were connected to each other for each frame. He made all the frames of the tabernacle in this way.
units.rightText: Each board had two tenons, joined one to another: thus did he make for all the boards of the tabernacle.
leftNotes: 36:22 That is, projecting pieces of wood made for insertion into another piece; similarly in verse 24.

units.leftText: He constructed twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle,
units.rightText: And he made the boards for the tabernacle: twenty boards for the south side southward;

units.leftText: with forty silver bases to put under the twenty frames — two bases for each frame, one under each tenon.
units.rightText: and he made forty sockets of silver under the twenty boards; two sockets under one board for its two tenons, and two sockets under another board for its two tenons.

units.leftText: For the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, he made twenty frames
units.rightText: And for the second side of the tabernacle, on the north side, he made twenty boards,

units.leftText: and forty silver bases — two bases under each frame.
units.rightText: and their forty sockets of silver; two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.

units.leftText: He made six frames for the rear of the tabernacle, the west side,
units.rightText: And for the hinder part of the tabernacle westward he made six boards.

units.leftText: and two frames for the two back corners of the tabernacle,
units.rightText: And two boards made he for the corners of the tabernacle in the hinder part.

units.leftText: coupled together from bottom to top and fitted into a single ring. He made both corners in this way.
units.rightText: And they were double beneath; and in like manner they were entire unto the top thereof unto one ring: thus he did to both of them in the two corners.

units.leftText: So there were eight frames and sixteen silver bases — two under each frame.
units.rightText: And there were eight boards, and their sockets of silver, sixteen sockets; under every board two sockets.

units.leftText: He also made five crossbars of acacia wood for the frames on one side of the tabernacle,
units.rightText: And he made bars of acacia wood; five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,

units.leftText: five for those on the other side, and five for those on the rear side of the tabernacle, to the west.
units.rightText: and five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the tabernacle for the hinder part westward.

units.leftText: He made the central crossbar to run through the center of the frames, from one end to the other.
units.rightText: And he made the middle bar to pass through in the midst of the boards from the one end to the other.

units.leftText: And he overlaid the frames with gold and made gold rings to hold the crossbars. He also overlaid the crossbars with gold. The Veil (Exodus 26:31–35|EXO 26:31-35*)
units.rightText: And he overlaid the boards with gold, and made their rings of gold for places for the bars, and overlaid the bars with gold.

units.leftText: Next, he made the veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen, with cherubim skillfully worked into it.
units.rightText: And he made the veil of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen: with cherubim, the work of the skilful workman, made he it.

units.leftText: He also made four posts of acacia wood for it and overlaid them with gold, along with gold hooks; and he cast four silver bases for the posts. The Curtain for the Entrance (Exodus 26:36–37|EXO 26:36-37*)
units.rightText: And he made thereunto four pillars of acacia, and overlaid them with gold: their hooks were of gold; and he cast for them four sockets of silver.

units.leftText: For the entrance to the tent, he made a curtain embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen,
units.rightText: And he made a screen for the door of the Tent, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, the work of the embroiderer;

units.leftText: together with five posts and their hooks. He overlaid the tops of the posts and their bands with gold, and their five bases were bronze.
units.rightText: and the five pillars of it with their hooks: and he overlaid their capitals and their fillets with gold; and their five sockets were of brass.

units.leftText: Bezalel went on to construct the ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
units.rightText: And Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood: two cubits and a half was the length of it, and a cubit and a half the breadth of it, and a cubit and a half the height of it.
leftNotes: 37:1 The ark was approximately 3.75 feet long, 2.25 feet wide, and 2.25 feet high (114.3 centimeters long, 68.6 centimeters wide, and 68.6 centimeters high).

units.leftText: He overlaid it with pure gold, both inside and out, and made a gold molding around it.
units.rightText: And he overlaid it with pure gold within and without, and made a crown of gold to it round about.

units.leftText: And he cast four gold rings for its four feet, two rings on one side and two on the other.
units.rightText: And he cast for it four rings of gold, in the four feet thereof; even two rings on the one side of it, and two rings on the other side of it.

units.leftText: Then he made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
units.rightText: And he made staves of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold.

units.leftText: He inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark in order to carry it. The Mercy Seat (Exodus 25:17–22|EXO 25:17-22*)
units.rightText: And he put the staves into the rings on the sides of the ark, to bear the ark.

units.leftText: He constructed a mercy seat of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
units.rightText: And he made a mercy-seat of pure gold: two cubits and a half was the length thereof, and a cubit and a half the breadth thereof.
leftNotes: 37:6 The mercy seat was approximately 3.75 feet long and 2.25 feet wide (114.3 centimeters long and 68.6 centimeters wide).

units.leftText: He made two cherubim of hammered gold at the ends of the mercy seat,
units.rightText: And he made two cherubim of gold; of beaten work made he them, at the two ends of the mercy-seat;

units.leftText: one cherub on one end and one on the other, all made from one piece of gold.
units.rightText: one cherub at the one end, and one cherub at the other end: of one piece with the mercy-seat made he the cherubim at the two ends thereof.

units.leftText: And the cherubim had wings that spread upward, overshadowing the mercy seat. The cherubim faced each other, looking toward the mercy seat. The Table of Showbread (Exodus 25:23–30|EXO 25:23-30*; Leviticus 24:5–9|LEV 24:5-9*)
units.rightText: And the cherubim spread out their wings on high, covering the mercy-seat with their wings, with their faces one to another; toward the mercy-seat were the faces of the cherubim.

units.leftText: He also made the table of acacia wood two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
units.rightText: And he made the table of acacia wood: two cubits was the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof.
leftNotes: 37:10 The table was approximately 3 feet long, 1.5 feet wide, and 2.25 feet high (91.4 centimeters long, 45.7 centimeters wide, and 68.6 centimeters high).

units.leftText: He overlaid it with pure gold and made a gold molding around it.
units.rightText: And he overlaid it with pure gold, and made thereto a crown of gold round about.

units.leftText: And he made a rim around it a handbreadth wide and put a gold molding on the rim.
units.rightText: And he made unto it a border of a handbreadth round about, and made a golden crown to the border thereof round about.
leftNotes: 37:12 A handbreadth is approximately 2.9 inches or 7.4 centimeters.

units.leftText: He cast four gold rings for the table and fastened them to the four corners at its four legs.
units.rightText: And he cast for it four rings of gold, and put the rings in the four corners that were on the four feet thereof.

units.leftText: The rings were placed close to the rim, to serve as holders for the poles used to carry the table.
units.rightText: Close by the border were the rings, the places for the staves to bear the table.

units.leftText: He made the poles of acacia wood for carrying the table and overlaid them with gold.
units.rightText: And he made the staves of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold, to bear the table.

units.leftText: He also made the utensils for the table out of pure gold: its plates and dishes, as well as its bowls and pitchers for pouring drink offerings. The Lampstand (Exodus 25:31–40|EXO 25:31-40*; Numbers 8:1–4|NUM 8:1-4*)
units.rightText: And he made the vessels which were upon the table, the dishes thereof, and the spoons thereof, and the bowls thereof, and the flagons thereof, wherewith to pour out, of pure gold.

units.leftText: Then he made the lampstand out of pure hammered gold, all of one piece: its base and shaft, its cups, and its buds and petals.
units.rightText: And he made the candlestick of pure gold: of beaten work made he the candlestick, even its base, and its shaft; its cups, its knops, and its flowers, were of one piece with it.

units.leftText: Six branches extended from the sides, three on one side and three on the other.
units.rightText: And there were six branches going out of the sides thereof; three branches of the candlestick out of the one side thereof, and three branches of the candlestick out of the other side thereof:

units.leftText: There were three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the first branch, each with buds and petals, three on the next branch, and the same for all six branches that extended from the lampstand.
units.rightText: three cups made like almond-blossoms in one branch, a knop and a flower, and three cups made like almond-blossoms in the other branch, a knop and a flower: so for the six branches going out of the candlestick.

units.leftText: And on the lampstand were four cups shaped like almond blossoms with buds and petals.
units.rightText: And in the candlestick were four cups made like almond-blossoms, the knops thereof, and the flowers thereof;

units.leftText: A bud was under the first pair of branches that extended from the lampstand, a bud under the second pair, and a bud under the third pair.
units.rightText: and a knop under two branches of one piece with it, and a knop under two branches of one piece with it, and a knop under two branches of one piece with it, for the six branches going out of it.

units.leftText: The buds and branches were all of one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.
units.rightText: Their knops and their branches were of one piece with it: the whole of it was one beaten work of pure gold.

units.leftText: He also made its seven lamps, its wick trimmers, and trays of pure gold.
units.rightText: And he made the lamps thereof, seven, and the snuffers thereof, and the snuffdishes thereof, of pure gold.

units.leftText: He made the lampstand and all its utensils from a talent of pure gold. The Altar of Incense (Exodus 30:1–10|EXO 30:1-10*)
units.rightText: Of a talent of pure gold made he it, and all the vessels thereof.
leftNotes: 37:24 A talent is approximately 75.4 pounds or 34.2 kilograms of gold.

units.leftText: He made the altar of incense out of acacia wood. It was square, a cubit long, a cubit wide, and two cubits high. Its horns were of one piece.
units.rightText: And he made the altar of incense of acacia wood: a cubit was the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof, foursquare; and two cubits was the height thereof; the horns thereof were of one piece with it.
leftNotes: 37:25 The altar was approximately 1.5 feet in length and width, and 3 feet high (45.7 centimeters in length and width, and 91.4 centimeters high).

units.leftText: And he overlaid with pure gold the top and all the sides and horns. Then he made a molding of gold around it.
units.rightText: And he overlaid it with pure gold, the top thereof, and the sides thereof round about, and the horns of it: and he made unto it a crown of gold round about.

units.leftText: He made two gold rings below the molding on opposite sides to hold the poles used to carry it.
units.rightText: And he made for it two golden rings under the crown thereof, upon the two ribs thereof, upon the two sides of it, for places for staves wherewith to bear it.

units.leftText: And he made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
units.rightText: And he made the staves of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold.

units.leftText: He also made the sacred anointing oil and the pure, fragrant incense, the work of a perfumer.
units.rightText: And he made the holy anointing oil, and the pure incense of sweet spices, after the art of the perfumer.

units.leftText: Bezalel constructed the altar of burnt offering from acacia wood. It was square, five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high.
units.rightText: And he made the altar of burnt-offering of acacia wood: five cubits was the length thereof, and five cubits the breadth thereof, foursquare; and three cubits the height thereof.
leftNotes: 38:1 Literally He constructed
38:1 The altar was approximately 7.5 feet in length and width, and 4.5 feet high (2.3 meters in length and width, and 1.4 meters high).

units.leftText: He made a horn at each of its four corners, so that the horns and altar were of one piece, and he overlaid the altar with bronze.
units.rightText: And he made the horns thereof upon the four corners of it; the horns thereof were of one piece with it: and he overlaid it with brass.

units.leftText: He made all the altar’s utensils of bronze — its pots, shovels, sprinkling bowls, meat forks, and firepans.
units.rightText: And he made all the vessels of the altar, the pots, and the shovels, and the basins, the flesh-hooks, and the firepans: all the vessels thereof made he of brass.

units.leftText: He made a grate of bronze mesh for the altar under its ledge, halfway up from the bottom.
units.rightText: And he made for the altar a grating of network of brass, under the ledge round it beneath, reaching halfway up.

units.leftText: At the four corners of the bronze grate he cast four rings as holders for the poles.
units.rightText: And he cast four rings for the four ends of the grating of brass, to be places for the staves.

units.leftText: And he made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze.
units.rightText: And he made the staves of acacia wood, and overlaid them with brass.

units.leftText: Then he inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar for carrying it. He made the altar with boards so that it was hollow. The Bronze Basin (Exodus 30:17–21|EXO 30:17-21*)
units.rightText: And he put the staves into the rings on the sides of the altar, wherewith to bear it; he made it hollow with planks.

units.leftText: Next he made the bronze basin and its stand from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. The Courtyard (Exodus 27:9–19|EXO 27:9-19*)
units.rightText: And he made the laver of brass, and the base thereof of brass, of the mirrors of the ministering women that ministered at the door of the tent of meeting.

units.leftText: Then he constructed the courtyard. The south side of the courtyard was a hundred cubits long and had curtains of finely spun linen,
units.rightText: And he made the court: for the south side southward the hangings of the court were of fine twined linen, a hundred cubits;
leftNotes: 38:9 100 cubits is approximately 150 feet or 45.7 meters.

units.leftText: with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and with silver hooks and bands on the posts.
units.rightText: their pillars were twenty, and their sockets twenty, of brass; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets were of silver.

units.leftText: The north side was also a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases. The hooks and bands of the posts were silver.
units.rightText: And for the north side a hundred cubits, their pillars twenty, and their sockets twenty, of brass; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of silver.

units.leftText: The west side was fifty cubits long and had curtains, with ten posts and ten bases. The hooks and bands of the posts were silver.
units.rightText: And for the west side were hangings of fifty cubits, their pillars ten, and their sockets ten; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of silver.
leftNotes: 38:12 50 cubits is approximately 75 feet or 22.9 meters.

units.leftText: And the east side, toward the sunrise, was also fifty cubits long.
units.rightText: And for the east side eastward fifty cubits.

units.leftText: The curtains on one side of the entrance were fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases.
units.rightText: The hangings for the one side of the gate were fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three;
leftNotes: 38:14 15 cubits is approximately 22.5 feet or 6.9 meters.

units.leftText: And the curtains on the other side were also fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases as well.
units.rightText: and so for the other side: on this hand and that hand by the gate of the court were hangings of fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three.

units.leftText: All the curtains around the courtyard were made of finely spun linen.
units.rightText: All the hangings of the court round about were of fine twined linen.

units.leftText: The bases for the posts were bronze, the hooks and bands were silver, and the plating for the tops of the posts was silver. So all the posts of the courtyard were banded with silver.
units.rightText: And the sockets for the pillars were of brass; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of silver; and the overlaying of their capitals, of silver; and all the pillars of the court were filleted with silver.

units.leftText: The curtain for the entrance to the courtyard was embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen. It was twenty cubits long and, like the curtains of the courtyard, five cubits high,
units.rightText: And the screen for the gate of the court was the work of the embroiderer, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen: and twenty cubits was the length, and the height in the breadth was five cubits, answerable to the hangings of the court.
leftNotes: 38:18 20 cubits is approximately 30 feet or 9.1 meters.
38:18 5 cubits is approximately 7.5 feet or 2.3 meters.

units.leftText: with four posts and four bronze bases. Their hooks were silver, as well as the bands and the plating of their tops.
units.rightText: And their pillars were four, and their sockets four, of brass; their hooks of silver, and the overlaying of their capitals, and their fillets, of silver.

units.leftText: All the tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the surrounding courtyard were bronze. An Inventory of Materials (Ezra 2:68–70|EZR 2:68-70*; Nehemiah 7:70–73|NEH 7:70-73*)
units.rightText: And all the pins of the tabernacle, and of the court round about, were of brass.

units.leftText: This is the inventory for the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the Testimony, as recorded at Moses’ command by the Levites under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
units.rightText: This is the sum of the things for the tabernacle, even the tabernacle of the testimony, as they were counted, according to the commandment of Moses, for the service of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.

units.leftText: Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made everything that the LORD had commanded Moses.
units.rightText: And Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made all that Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: With him was Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver, designer, and embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen.
units.rightText: And with him was Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver, and a skilful workman, and an embroiderer in blue, and in purple, and in scarlet, and in fine linen.

units.leftText: All the gold from the wave offering used for the work on the sanctuary totaled 29 talents and 730 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
units.rightText: All the gold that was used for the work in all the work of the sanctuary, even the gold of the offering, was twenty and nine talents, and seven hundred and thirty shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary.
leftNotes: 38:24 The total weight of the gold was approximately 1.1 tons or 1 metric ton.

units.leftText: The silver from those numbered among the congregation totaled 100 talents and 1,775 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel—
units.rightText: And the silver of them that were numbered of the congregation was a hundred talents, and a thousand seven hundred and threescore and fifteen shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary:
leftNotes: 38:25 The total weight of the silver was approximately 3.79 tons or 3.44 metric tons.

units.leftText: a beka per person, that is, half a shekel, according to the sanctuary shekel, from everyone twenty years of age or older who had crossed over to be numbered, a total of 603,550 men.
units.rightText: a beka a head, that is, half a shekel, after the shekel of the sanctuary, for every one that passed over to them that were numbered, from twenty years old and upward, for six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty men.
leftNotes: 38:26 A beka is half a shekel, or approximately 0.2 ounces or 5.7 grams.

units.leftText: The hundred talents of silver were used to cast the bases of the sanctuary and the bases of the veil— 100 bases from the 100 talents, one talent per base.
units.rightText: And the hundred talents of silver were for casting the sockets of the sanctuary, and the sockets of the veil; a hundred sockets for the hundred talents, a talent for a socket.
leftNotes: 38:27 100 talents is approximately 3.77 tons or 3.42 metric tons of silver.

units.leftText: With the 1,775 shekels [of silver] he made the hooks for the posts, overlaid their tops, and supplied bands for them.
units.rightText: And of the thousand seven hundred seventy and five shekels he made hooks for the pillars, and overlaid their capitals, and made fillets for them.
leftNotes: 38:28 1,775 shekels is approximately 44.6 pounds or 20.2 kilograms of silver.

units.leftText: The bronze from the wave offering totaled 70 talents and 2,400 shekels.
units.rightText: And the brass of the offering was seventy talents, and two thousand and four hundred shekels.
leftNotes: 38:29 The total weight of the bronze was approximately 2.67 tons or 2.42 metric tons.

units.leftText: He used it to make the bases for the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, the bronze altar and its bronze grating, all the utensils for the altar,
units.rightText: And therewith he made the sockets to the door of the tent of meeting, and the brazen altar, and the brazen grating for it, and all the vessels of the altar,

units.leftText: the bases for the surrounding courtyard and its gate, and all the tent pegs for the tabernacle and its surrounding courtyard.
units.rightText: and the sockets of the court round about, and the sockets of the gate of the court, and all the pins of the tabernacle, and all the pins of the court round about.

units.leftText: From the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn they made specially woven garments for ministry in the sanctuary, as well as the holy garments for Aaron, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
units.rightText: And of the blue, and purple, and scarlet, they made finely wrought garments, for ministering in the holy place, and made the holy garments for Aaron; as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: Bezalel made the ephod of finely spun linen embroidered with gold, and with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
units.rightText: And he made the ephod of gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen.
leftNotes: 39:2 Literally He made

units.leftText: They hammered out thin sheets of gold and cut threads from them to interweave with the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen — the work of a skilled craftsman.
units.rightText: And they did beat the gold into thin plates, and cut it into wires, to work it in the blue, and in the purple, and in the scarlet, and in the fine linen, the work of the skilful workman.

units.leftText: They made shoulder pieces for the ephod, which were attached at two of its corners, so it could be fastened.
units.rightText: They made shoulder-pieces for it, joined together; at the two ends was it joined together.

units.leftText: And the skillfully woven waistband of the ephod was of one piece with the ephod, of the same workmanship — with gold, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and with finely spun linen, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
units.rightText: And the skilfully woven band, that was upon it, wherewith to gird it on, was of the same piece and like the work thereof; of gold, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen; as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: They mounted the onyx stones in gold filigree settings, engraved like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel.
units.rightText: And they wrought the onyx stones, inclosed in settings of gold, graven with the engravings of a signet, according to the names of the children of Israel.

units.leftText: Then they fastened them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel, as the LORD had commanded Moses. The Breastpiece (Exodus 28:15–30|EXO 28:15-30*)
units.rightText: And he put them on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod, to be stones of memorial for the children of Israel; as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: He made the breastpiece with the same workmanship as the ephod, with gold, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and with finely spun linen.
units.rightText: And he made the breastplate, the work of the skilful workman, like the work of the ephod; of gold, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen.

units.leftText: It was square when folded over double, a span long and a span wide.
units.rightText: It was foursquare; they made the breastplate double: a span was the length thereof, and a span the breadth thereof, being double.
leftNotes: 39:9 The breastpiece, when folded over, was approximately 9 inches or 22.9 centimeters in both length and width.

units.leftText: And they mounted on it four rows of gemstones: The first row had a ruby, a topaz, and an emerald;
units.rightText: And they set in it four rows of stones. A row of sardius, topaz, and carbuncle was the first row;
leftNotes: 39:10 The precise identification of some of these gemstones is uncertain.

units.leftText: the second row had a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond;
units.rightText: and the second row, an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond;

units.leftText: the third row had a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
units.rightText: and the third row, a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;

units.leftText: and the fourth row had a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. These stones were mounted in gold filigree settings.
units.rightText: and the fourth row, a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper: they were inclosed in inclosings of gold in their settings.

units.leftText: The twelve stones corresponded to the names of the sons of Israel. Each stone was engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
units.rightText: And the stones were according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names; like the engravings of a signet, every one according to his name, for the twelve tribes.

units.leftText: For the breastpiece they made braided chains like cords of pure gold.
units.rightText: And they made upon the breastplate chains like cords, of wreathen work of pure gold.

units.leftText: They also made two gold filigree settings and two gold rings, and fastened the two rings to the two corners of the breastpiece.
units.rightText: And they made two settings of gold, and two gold rings, and put the two rings on the two ends of the breastplate.

units.leftText: Then they fastened the two gold chains to the two gold rings at the corners of the breastpiece,
units.rightText: And they put the two wreathen chains of gold in the two rings at the ends of the breastplate.

units.leftText: and they fastened the other ends of the two chains to the two filigree settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
units.rightText: And the other two ends of the two wreathen chains they put on the two settings, and put them on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod, in the forepart thereof.

units.leftText: They made two more gold rings and attached them to the other two corners of the breastpiece, on the inside edge next to the ephod.
units.rightText: And they made two rings of gold, and put them upon the two ends of the breastplate, upon the edge thereof, which was toward the side of the ephod inward.

units.leftText: They made two additional gold rings and attached them to the bottom of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, on its front, near the seam just above its woven waistband.
units.rightText: And they made two rings of gold, and put them on the two shoulder-pieces of the ephod underneath, in the forepart thereof, close by the coupling thereof, above the skilfully woven band of the ephod.

units.leftText: Then they tied the rings of the breastpiece to the rings of the ephod with a cord of blue yarn, so that the breastpiece was above the waistband of the ephod and would not swing out from the ephod, just as the LORD had commanded Moses. Additional Priestly Garments (Exodus 28:31–43|EXO 28:31-43*)
units.rightText: And they did bind the breastplate by the rings thereof unto the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue, that it might be upon the skilfully woven band of the ephod, and that the breastplate might not be loosed from the ephod; as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: They made the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth, the work of a weaver,
units.rightText: And he made the robe of the ephod of woven work, all of blue;

units.leftText: with an opening in the center of the robe like that of a garment, with a collar around the opening so that it would not tear.
units.rightText: and the hole of the robe in the midst thereof, as the hole of a coat of mail, with a binding round about the hole of it, that it should not be rent.
leftNotes: 39:23 The meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain; possibly a coat of mail.

units.leftText: They made pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely spun linen on the lower hem of the robe.
units.rightText: And they made upon the skirts of the robe pomegranates of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and twined linen.

units.leftText: They also made bells of pure gold and attached them around the hem between the pomegranates,
units.rightText: And they made bells of pure gold, and put the bells between the pomegranates upon the skirts of the robe round about, between the pomegranates;

units.leftText: alternating the bells and pomegranates around the lower hem of the robe to be worn for ministry, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
units.rightText: a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, upon the skirts of the robe round about, to minister in; as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: For Aaron and his sons they made tunics of fine linen, the work of a weaver,
units.rightText: And they made the coats of fine linen of woven work for Aaron, and for his sons,

units.leftText: as well as the turban of fine linen, the ornate headbands and undergarments of finely spun linen,
units.rightText: and the mitre of fine linen, and the goodly head-tires of fine linen, and the linen breeches of fine twined linen,

units.leftText: and the sash of finely spun linen, embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
units.rightText: and the girdle of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, the work of the embroiderer; as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: They also made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, and they engraved on it, like an inscription on a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD.
units.rightText: And they made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, and wrote upon it a writing, like the engravings of a signet, HOLY TO JEHOVAH.
leftNotes: 39:30 That is, the LORD

units.leftText: Then they fastened to it a blue cord to mount it on the turban, just as the LORD had commanded Moses. Moses Approves the Work
units.rightText: And they tied unto it a lace of blue, to fasten it upon the mitre above; as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: So all the work for the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, was completed. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
units.rightText: Thus was finished all the work of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting: and the children of Israel did according to all that Jehovah commanded Moses; so did they.

units.leftText: Then they brought the tabernacle to Moses: the tent with all its furnishings, its clasps, its frames, its crossbars, and its posts and bases;
units.rightText: And they brought the tabernacle unto Moses, the Tent, and all its furniture, its clasps, its boards, its bars, and its pillars, and its sockets;

units.leftText: the covering of ram skins dyed red, the covering of fine leather, and the veil of the covering;
units.rightText: and the covering of rams’ skins dyed red, and the covering of sealskins, and the veil of the screen;
leftNotes: 39:34 Possibly the hides of large aquatic mammals

units.leftText: the ark of the Testimony with its poles and the mercy seat;
units.rightText: the ark of the testimony, and the staves thereof, and the mercy-seat;
leftNotes: 39:35 That is, the ark of the covenant

units.leftText: the table with all its utensils and the Bread of the Presence;
units.rightText: the table, all the vessels thereof, and the showbread;

units.leftText: the pure gold lampstand with its row of lamps and all its utensils, as well as the oil for the light;
units.rightText: the pure candlestick, the lamps thereof, even the lamps to be set in order, and all the vessels thereof, and the oil for the light;

units.leftText: the gold altar, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the curtain for the entrance to the tent;
units.rightText: and the golden altar, and the anointing oil, and the sweet incense, and the screen for the door of the Tent;

units.leftText: the bronze altar with its bronze grating, its poles, and all its utensils; the basin with its stand;
units.rightText: the brazen altar, and its grating of brass, its staves, and all its vessels, the laver and its base;

units.leftText: the curtains of the courtyard with its posts and bases; the curtain for the gate of the courtyard, its ropes and tent pegs, and all the equipment for the service of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting;
units.rightText: the hangings of the court, its pillars, and its sockets, and the screen for the gate of the court, the cords thereof, and the pins thereof, and all the instruments of the service of the tabernacle, for the tent of meeting;

units.leftText: and the woven garments for ministering in the sanctuary, both the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons to serve as priests.
units.rightText: the finely wrought garments for ministering in the holy place, and the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest’s office.

units.leftText: The Israelites had done all the work just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
units.rightText: According to all that Jehovah commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did all the work.

units.leftText: And Moses inspected all the work and saw that they had accomplished it just as the LORD had commanded. So Moses blessed them.
units.rightText: And Moses saw all the work, and, behold, they had done it; as Jehovah had commanded, even so had they done it: and Moses blessed them.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “On the first day of the first month you are to set up the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: On the first day of the first month shalt thou rear up the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.

units.leftText: Put the ark of the Testimony in it and screen off the ark with the veil.
units.rightText: And thou shalt put therein the ark of the testimony, and thou shalt screen the ark with the veil.
leftNotes: 40:3 That is, the ark of the covenant; also in verses 5 and 21

units.leftText: Then bring in the table and set out its arrangement; bring in the lampstand as well, and set up its lamps.
units.rightText: And thou shalt bring in the table, and set in order the things that are upon it; and thou shalt bring in the candlestick, and light the lamps thereof.

units.leftText: Place the gold altar of incense in front of the ark of the Testimony, and hang the curtain at the entrance to the tabernacle.
units.rightText: And thou shalt set the golden altar for incense before the ark of the testimony, and put the screen of the door to the tabernacle.

units.leftText: Place the altar of burnt offering in front of the entrance to the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: And thou shalt set the altar of burnt-offering before the door of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.

units.leftText: And place the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
units.rightText: And thou shalt set the laver between the tent of meeting and the altar, and shalt put water therein.

units.leftText: Set up the surrounding courtyard and hang the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard.
units.rightText: And thou shalt set up the court round about, and hang up the screen of the gate of the court.

units.leftText: Take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it; consecrate it along with all its furnishings, and it shall be holy.
units.rightText: And thou shalt take the anointing oil, and anoint the tabernacle, and all that is therein, and shalt hallow it, and all the furniture thereof: and it shall be holy.

units.leftText: Anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils; consecrate the altar, and it shall be most holy.
units.rightText: And thou shalt anoint the altar of burnt-offering, and all its vessels, and sanctify the altar: and the altar shall be most holy.

units.leftText: Anoint the basin and its stand and consecrate them.
units.rightText: And thou shalt anoint the laver and its base, and sanctify it.

units.leftText: Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water.
units.rightText: And thou shalt bring Aaron and his sons unto the door of the tent of meeting, and shalt wash them with water.

units.leftText: And you are to clothe Aaron with the holy garments, anoint him, and consecrate him, so that he may serve Me as a priest.
units.rightText: And thou shalt put upon Aaron the holy garments; and thou shalt anoint him, and sanctify him, that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office.

units.leftText: Bring his sons forward and clothe them with tunics.
units.rightText: And thou shalt bring his sons, and put coats upon them;

units.leftText: Anoint them just as you anointed their father, so that they may also serve Me as priests. Their anointing will qualify them for a permanent priesthood throughout their generations.”
units.rightText: and thou shalt anoint them, as thou didst anoint their father, that they may minister unto me in the priest’s office: and their anointing shall be to them for an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.

units.leftText: Moses did everything just as the LORD had commanded him.
units.rightText: Thus did Moses: according to all that Jehovah commanded him, so did he.

units.leftText: So the tabernacle was set up on the first day of the first month of the second year.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the first month in the second year, on the first day of the month, that the tabernacle was reared up.

units.leftText: When Moses set up the tabernacle, he laid its bases, positioned its frames, inserted its crossbars, and set up its posts.
units.rightText: And Moses reared up the tabernacle, and laid its sockets, and set up the boards thereof, and put in the bars thereof, and reared up its pillars.

units.leftText: Then he spread the tent over the tabernacle and put the covering over the tent, just as the LORD had commanded him.
units.rightText: And he spread the tent over the tabernacle, and put the covering of the tent above upon it; as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: Moses took the Testimony and placed it in the ark, attaching the poles to the ark; and he set the mercy seat atop the ark.
units.rightText: And he took and put the testimony into the ark, and set the staves on the ark, and put the mercy-seat above upon the ark:

units.leftText: Then he brought the ark into the tabernacle, put up the veil for the screen, and shielded off the ark of the Testimony, just as the LORD had commanded him.
units.rightText: and he brought the ark into the tabernacle, and set up the veil of the screen, and screened the ark of the testimony; as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: Moses placed the table in the Tent of Meeting on the north side of the tabernacle, outside the veil.
units.rightText: And he put the table in the tent of meeting, upon the side of the tabernacle northward, without the veil.

units.leftText: He arranged the bread on it before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded him.
units.rightText: And he set the bread in order upon it before Jehovah; as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: He also placed the lampstand in the Tent of Meeting opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle
units.rightText: And he put the candlestick in the tent of meeting, over against the table, on the side of the tabernacle southward.

units.leftText: and set up the lamps before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded him.
units.rightText: And he lighted the lamps before Jehovah; as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: Moses placed the gold altar in the Tent of Meeting, in front of the veil,
units.rightText: And he put the golden altar in the tent of meeting before the veil:

units.leftText: and he burned fragrant incense on it, just as the LORD had commanded him.
units.rightText: and he burnt thereon incense of sweet spices; as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: Then he put up the curtain at the entrance to the tabernacle.
units.rightText: And he put the screen of the door to the tabernacle.

units.leftText: He placed the altar of burnt offering near the entrance to the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, and offered on it the burnt offering and the grain offering, just as the LORD had commanded him.
units.rightText: And he set the altar of burnt-offering at the door of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting, and offered upon it the burnt-offering and the meal-offering; as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: He placed the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar and put water in it for washing;
units.rightText: And he set the laver between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water therein, wherewith to wash.

units.leftText: and from it Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and feet.
units.rightText: And Moses and Aaron and his sons washed their hands and their feet thereat;

units.leftText: They washed whenever they entered the Tent of Meeting or approached the altar, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
units.rightText: when they went into the tent of meeting, and when they came near unto the altar, they washed; as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: And Moses set up the courtyard around the tabernacle and the altar, and he hung the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard. So Moses finished the work. The Cloud and the Glory (Numbers 9:15–23|NUM 9:15-23*)
units.rightText: And he reared up the court round about the tabernacle and the altar, and set up the screen of the gate of the court. So Moses finished the work.

units.leftText: Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
units.rightText: Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of Jehovah filled the tabernacle.

units.leftText: Moses was unable to enter the Tent of Meeting because the cloud had settled on it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
units.rightText: And Moses was not able to enter into the tent of meeting, because the cloud abode thereon, and the glory of Jehovah filled the tabernacle.

units.leftText: Whenever the cloud was lifted from above the tabernacle, the Israelites would set out through all the stages of their journey.
units.rightText: And when the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel went onward, throughout all their journeys:

units.leftText: If the cloud was not lifted, they would not set out until the day it was taken up.
units.rightText: but if the cloud was not taken up, then they journeyed not till the day that it was taken up.

units.leftText: For the cloud of the LORD was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in the cloud by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel through all their journeys.
units.rightText: For the cloud of Jehovah was upon the tabernacle by day, and there was fire therein by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys.
